🔺PALITHYAM 


🔺NIDANAM (Etiology)

*Causes of Pālityam (as per Ayurvedic classics):
*Pittaja prakṛti
*Atisevana of ushna, amla,lavana rasa
*Krodha, śoka, chintā, bhaya (mental stress)
*Ahita āhāra-vihāra
*Viruddhāhāra (incompatible food)
*Atyucchraya of Pitta and Rakta
Beeja*dosha (Hereditary factors)
*Reference:Charaka Samhita – Chikitsa Sthana 7/24
Ashtanga Hridaya – Uttara Tantra 24/8

🔺PURVAROOPAM (Prodromal Symptoms)

*Pālityam may not have distinct prodromal signs, but some*consider early signs like:
*Loss of luster of hair
*Dryness and brittleness of hair
*Itching and burning of scalp

🔺LAKSANAM (Symptoms)

*Appearance of white or grey hair at an early age (before 30–35 years)
*Gradual spread of grey hair over scalp, beard, and mustache
*May occur with hair fall in someindividualsReference:
Ashtanga Hridaya – Uttara Tantra 24/8

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION:

*Age of onset: Important to determine if it is premature (before 20 years in Caucasians, before 25 years in Asians).
*Family history: Check for genetic predisposition.
*Dietary habits: Poor nutrition or vitamin deficiencies.
*Stress levels: Mental stress is a known factor.
*Lifestyle habits: Smoking, alcohol, irregular sleep.


🔺 SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION:

*Skin and hair: Observe for texture changes, hair thinning, dryness.
*Nails and mucosa: May show signs of nutritional deficiency.
*Thyroid gland: Palpation for goiter or thyroid nodules.
*Neurological exam: Rule out underlying neurocutaneous disorders if any.
*Signs of autoimmune disorders (e.g., vitiligo).

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS
 
*Complete Blood Count (CBC): Rule out anemia.
*Serum Vitamin B12 and Folate: *Deficiency linked to premature greying.
** Thyroid Profile (TSH, T3, T4): To detect hypothyroidism/hyperthyroidism.
*Fasting Blood Glucose and HbA1c: To screen for  Ferritin: For iron deficiency
*Autoimmune markers: ANA if autoimmune disorders are suspected.
*Genetic testing (if strong familial history or syndromic features).

🔺PALITHYAM 



🔺DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

*Premature Greying of Hair (Canities praecox)
*Nutritional deficiencies (e.g., B12, iron, copper, zinc).
*Autoimmune disorders (e.g., vitiligo, alopecia areata).
*Thyroid disorders (e.g., hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism)
*Werner syndrome (premature aging).
*Progeria (Hutchinson-Gilford syndrome) – in children.
*Addison’s disease – may include pigmentation changes.
*Pernicious anemia – linked with B12 deficiency.
*Chronic stress-related telogen effluvium.
*Atopy or allergic predisposition.

🔺SAMPRAPTI (Pathogenesis)

*Due to nidana sevana, there is aggravation of Pitta dosha along with vitiation of Rakta and Majjādhātu.
*This affects keśa varṇa(hair color), leading to śveta(white) keśa.
*Rakta + Pitta dushti leads to burning of black*pigment in the hair follicles.
*SampraptiGhataka:
-Doṣa: Pitta
*Dūṣya: Rakta, Majjā
*Srotas:Romakūpa & Rasavaha srotas
*Adhisthāna: Keśa (hair follicles)
*Roga marga: Bāhya

🔺 SAMANYA CHIKITSA (General Treatment)

*Internal Medications:
*Triphala Churna – Rasāyana
*Chyavanaprāśa – Rejuvenative
*Bhringarājāsava
*Drākṣādi Kvātha – Pittahara
*Narasimha Rasāyana
*External Applications:
-Bhringaraja Taila, Nimba Taila
*Keshya Sneha (like Amalaki taila) for Abhyanga

🔺UPASHAYA
 (Pacifying Factors)

*Intake of cooling, Pittahara foods
*Regular use of rasāyana, keshya dravyas
Stress reduction (mental upashaya)
*Nasya with keshya drugs

🔺ANUPASHAYA(Aggravating Factors)

*Ushna, amla, lavanātmaka āhāra
*Excessive anger, anxiety, sleeplessness
*Smoking, alcohol, and spicy food
*Exposure to excessive sun and heat


🔺VISESHA CHIKITSA (Specific Line of Treatment)

*Nasya Therapy:
*"Keśa-shukra-mukha-nāsa-netra-karṇānām vṛddhikaraṃ nāsyaṃ"
(Nasya nourishes the organs of head including hair)
— Ashtanga Hridaya, Sutrasthana 20/36
*Anu Taila, Bhringaraja Taila – for nasya
*Done for 7 to 14 days regularly
*Rasayana Therapy:
*Narasimha Rasāyana, Chyavanaprāśa
*Amalaki Rasāyana *Revitalizes Pitta and rakta
*Shirobasti / Shiropichu:Using Bhringaraja taila, Nimba taila
*Lepa (Hair Packs):Bhringaraja + Amalaki + Jatamansi churna in milk
*Weekly application
*Classical References Summary
*Text	Reference
*Charaka Samhita	Chikitsa Sthana 7/24
Ashtanga Hridaya	Uttara Tantra 24/8
Sushruta Samhita	Nidana Sthana 13/19
Bhavaprakasha	Kesharoga Chikitsa

🔺GUDA VIBRAMSHAM ( PERIANAL ABCESS)


🔺NIDANAM (Etiology)

*Classical references (Su. Ni. 9, Ch. Ni. 10, Aru. Sa. Nida. 12):
*Apathyasevana (improper diet and lifestyle)
*Abhighata(trauma to the anal region)
*Krimidosha (infestation by parasites)
*Vegavidharana(suppression of natural urges)
*Atisnigdha-Amla-Katu-Lavana Ahara
*Ruksha Bhojana and Vyayama immediately after meals

🔺PURVAROOPAM (Prodromal Symptoms)

*Not specifically described for Guda
*Vidradhi but general Vidradhi Purvaroopas apply:Mild pain around the anus
Burning or itching sensation
*Heaviness and discomfort in the perianal area
*Malaise, low-gradefever

🔺LAKSHANA (Clinical Features)

*As per Sushruta Samhita, Nidanasthana 9/13-14 and Chakrapanicommentary:
*Toda (pricking pain) and daha (burning)
*Shotha (swelling) and kandu (itching)
*Guda vedana (severe pain in anus)
*Jwara (fever), mala sanga (constipation), mutrakrichra (painful urination)
*If pus forms:Pidaka (boil), paka (suppuration), and srava(discharge)
*In chronic cases, fistula may develop (Bhagandara)

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*Vitals:Fever (often high-grade)
*Tachycardia
Mild hypotension (if septicemia present)
*General Appearance:Patient may appear acutely ill, uncomfortable, or in pain.
*Inability to sit due to pain.


🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Local perianal/rectal examination:Redness, swelling, and tendernessnear anus or rectum
*Warmth and induration in the perianal area
*Fluctuation test positive (if abscess has formed)
*Possible pus discharge from opening (if ruptured)
*Per Rectal Examination:
*Tender swelling palpable in ischiorectal or intersphincteric space
*Pain on digital rectalexam
*May feel boggy mass or abscess cavity

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*CBC:
Elevated WBC count(leukocytosis) with neutrophilia
*CRP/ESR:
Raised inflammatory markers
*Blood sugarlevels:Important in diabetic patients – increased risk of abscess
*Pus Culture and Sensitivity (if discharge is present):
*To identify causative organism and antibiotic sensitivity
*Radiological Investigations
*Ultrasound (perianal or transrectal):To detect fluid collection/abscess
*MRI Pelvis:Best imaging modality to define abscess cavity and extent (especially for deep-seated abscess or fistula)
*CT scan (in complicated or deep abscess):
*Useful in immunocompromised patients or atypical cases

🔺GUDA VIBRAMSHAM ( PERIANAL ABCESS)

🔺DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS 

*anal trauma
 *anal fissure
 *anal fistula *thrombosed externalhemorrhoid
 *pilonidal cyst buttocks abscess cellulitis *Crohn's disease 
*ulcerative colitis
 *malignancy proctitis 
*HIV/ AIDS other sexually transmitted diseases
 *Bartholin's abscess

🔺SAMPRAPTI (Pathogenesis)

*Doshas (especially Pitta and Rakta) vitiated due to causative factors
*Accumulate in the GudaPradesha and lead to Shotha → Paka → Vidradhi
*Involvement of Mamsa, Rakta, Medas dhatus
*Srotorodha (obstruction of channels) and Dhatu paka (suppuration) occurs

🔺SAMANYA CHIKITSA (General Line of Treatment)

*As per Su. Chi. 17, Ashtanga Hridaya:
*Shodhana (Purificatory):
*Virechana with Trivrit lehya, Avipattikara churna
*Basti karma (especially Niruha basti and Anuvasana basti)
*Shamana (Palliative):Guduchi, Haridra, Nimba, Amalaki – anti-inflammatory and detoxifyingherbs
*Kaishora Guggulu, Triphala Guggulu
*Local Applications:
*Lepa of Haridra + Nimba + Ghee
*Seka (pouring medicated decoctions)
*Pichu with Jatyadi taila

🔺UPASHAYA (Palliatives/Relieving Factors)

*Warm sitz bath
*Application of Jatyadi taila or *Nirgundi taila
*Use of easilydigestible, non-spicy food
*Mild laxatives like Triphala

🔺ANUPASHAYA(Aggravating Factors)

*Sitting for prolonged hours
*Spicy, oily, and junk food
*Alcohol, smoking
*Constipation, straining during defecation

🔺VISHESHA CHIKITSA (Specific Treatment)

*In Early Stage (Ama avastha):
*Langhana, Deepana, Pachana
*Use of Panchatikta kashaya, Guduchi churna, Nimba
*In Suppurative Stage:Snehana + Swedana
*Surgical drainage if abscess matures – described as Vidradhi Bheda karma
*Classical method:Shastra karma followed by:Vrana ropana (wound healing)
*Internal Medicines:
Guggulu preparations (Kaishora, Triphala, Mahatiktaka Ghrta)
*Arogyavardhini Vati, Chandraprabha Vati
*For wound healing:Jatyadi Ghrita / Taila, Panchavalkala decoction
*Classical References:Sushruta Samhita – Nidanastana, Chapter 9 (Vidradhi Nidanam)
*Charaka Samhita – Chikitsa Sthana 12
*Ashtanga Hridaya – Nidana & Chikitsa Sthana
*Bhavaprakasha – Madhyama Khanda

🔺दान्त शैथिल्य (Dantha Shaithilya)Loosening of Teeth

🔺निदानम् (Nidanam – Causes)

*As per Ayurveda, Dantha Shaithilya is a result of vitiation of Kapha and Vata doshas, along with poor oral hygiene and dietary habits. Common Nidanas include:

*Excess intake of ruksha (dry), katu (pungent), and tikshna (sharp)
*substances
*Frequent consumption of veryu hot or very cold foods
*Bruxism (tooth grinding) or trauma to teeth
*Neglect of danta*dhavana (tooth cleaning)
**Suppression of natural urgeslike kshavathu*(sneezing), kasa (coughing)
*Chronic gingival infections or Dantamula roga (periodontal disease)
(Reference:Suśruta Saṃhitā – Chikitsāsthāna 24/6, Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdaya – Sūtrasthāna 22


🔺पूर्वरूपम् (PURVARUPAM – Prodromal Symptoms)

*Gum sensitivity
*Foul breath
*Mild pain or uneasiness in the gums
*Discoloration of gums
*Spongy or swollen gums

🔺लक्षणानि (LAKṢANANI – *Signs and Symptoms)

*Shaithilya (looseness) of teeth
*Bleeding gums(raktasrava)
*Swelling and pain in gums
*Halitosis (bad breath)
*Difficulty in chewing
*Receding gumsor Dana moola vikara
*Reference: Suśruta Saṃhitā – Nidāna Sthāna 16/12, Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdaya – Uttara Sthāna 22

🔺GENERAL & SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION:

*General Examination:
*Pallor – Rule out anemia
*Nutritional status – Vitamin C/D/calcium deficiency
*Signs of systemic illness – Diabetes, immunodeficiency
*Oral hygiene status
*Lymphadenopathy
*Submandibularand cervical nodes


🔺SYSTEMIC  EXAMINATION:

*Endocrine system – Especially for diabetes mellitus (can affect periodontal status)
*Musculoskeletal system – Rule out osteoporosis or bone-related disorders
*Immune status – For possible autoimmune involvement(e.g., periodontitis)

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*Hematological:
*Complete BloodCount (CBC) – *Rule out infection or anemia
*Fasting Blood Sugar / HbA1c – To assess diabetes mellitus
*Vitamin D & Calcium levels – For bone metabolism
*Serum Alkaline Phosphatase – Marker for bone activity
*C-Reactive Protein (CRP) – Inflammatory marker
*Microbiological:
*Oral swabculture – To detect pathogenic flora causing periodontitis
*Radiological:
*Intraoral Periapical *Radiograph(IOPA)
*Orthopantomogram (OPG) *To assess alveolar bone loss

🔺दान्त शैथिल्य (Dantha Shaithilya)Loosening of Teeth


🔺DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS 
	
*Periodontitis (chronic or aggressive)
	*Gingivitis  *periodontal ligament 
*Osteoporosis (localized to alveolar bone)
*Scurvy (Vitamin C deficiency)
*Diabetes-related periodontal disease
*Leukemia (in advanced cases with gum involvement)
*Local trauma
 *occlusal trauma

🔺सम्प्राप्ति (Samprāpti *Pathogenesis)
*Vitiated Vata causes dryness and loosening of supportive*tissues (Asthi and MajjaDhatu).
*Vitiated Kapha loses its sthirata and snigdhatva, leading to gum recession and inflammation.
*Accumulated Ama and Raktadushti contribute to infection and swelling of gums*The pathology progresses from Mukhagataroga to Asthigata vyadhi in severe cases.

🔺सामान्य चिकित्सा (SAMANYA CHIKITSA – *General Treatment)

*Dantadhavana with kashaya rasa dravya (e.g., triphala churna, lodhra, khadira)
*Gandusha and Kavala (oil pulling) using tila taila or triphala kwatha
*Use of Pratisarana(rubbing herbson gums) *with lodhra, madhuka, haridra, yashtimadhu
*Avoiding causative food itemsand maintaining oral hygiene
*Internal use of rasayana and kapha-vata shamaka herbs(Reference:Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdaya – Sutrasthāna 22, Bhavaprakāśa – Dantamoolaroga Adhyaya

🔺उपशय (UPASAYA 
 *Palliative Factors)

*Relief after gandusha and kavala
*Use of astringent, bitter,and cooling substances
*Application of taila or ghrita*preparations
*Maintaining oral hygiene
*Use of Triphala or dashana samskara choorna

🔺अनुपशय (ANUPASAYA – Aggravating Factors)

*Consumption of sour, salty, spicy, and sticky food
*Improper cleaning of teeth
*Brushing with hard brush or vigorous rubbing
*Chewing hard objects
*Night grinding of teeth or mouth breathing



🔺विशेष चिकित्सा (VISESA CHIKITSA – Specific Treatment)

*Internal Medicines:
Dashana samskara vati – for strengthening gums
*Triphala guggulu – for inflammation and infection
*Gandhaka rasayana – if pus or infection present
*Chandraprabhavati – for underlying systemic issues
*External Applications:
*Dashana samskara choorna for brushing
*Tila taila gandusha daily
*Khadiradivati for chewing and disinfection
*Lodhra + Haridra + Yashtimadhu powder for pratisarana
*Panchakarma Procedures:Nasya with Anu Taila
Kavaladharana
*Raktamokshana (if severe rakta dushti signs are present)
*Classical References:Suśruta Saṃhitā – Cikitsāsthāna 24
Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdaya – Uttara Sthāna 22
Charaka Saṃhitā – Chikitsa Sthāna 26
Bhavaprakāśa – Danta Moola Roga Chikitsa

🔺AGNIMANDHYA

 🔺NIDANAM (Etiology/Causative Factors):

*From Charaka Samhita & other texts:
*Ajirna (indigestion) due to:
*Mithya Ahara Vihara (Improper diet and lifestyle)
*GuruAhara (Heavy food)
*Atibhojana (Overeating)
*Vishamashana (Irregular food intake)
*Mandagni (Naturally weak digestive fire)
*Aama accumulation
Stress/mental factors (Krodha, Shoka, Bhaya, etc.)
*Dosha vitiation, especially Kapha & Vata
(Classical Reference:Charaka Samhita Chikitsa Sthana 15/44, Ashtanga Hridaya Sutrasthana 13

🔺PURVAROOPAM (Prodromal Symptoms):

*Arochaka (anorexia)
*Guruta (heaviness of body and abdomen)
*Utsaha hani (lack of enthusiasm)
*Udarashoola (mild abdominal pain)
*Hridaya vyatha (discomfort in chestregion)
*Charaka Samhita Sutrasthana 28/8

🔺LAKSHANA (Symptoms):

*Agnidaurbalya (loss of digestive power)
*Ajeerna (indigestion)
*Udarashoola (abdominal pain)
*Aalasya (laziness)**Malabaddhata(constipation)
*Gaurava (heaviness in body)
*Trishna (thirst)
*Hrullasa (nausea)(Madhava Nidana Ajirna Nidana

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION
 
*General Appearance: May appear lethargic, weak, or fatigued
*Build and Nourishment: Oftenundernourished due to improper digestion and assimilation
*Vital Signs:Temperature: Usually normal, may have low-grade fever if associated with infection
*Pulse:Normal or slightly slow
*BloodPressure: Generally within normal limitsunless there’s systemic involvement
*Hydration Status: Can be mildly dehydrated due to poor food intake
*Tongue: Coated tongue indicating ama (toxins) accumulation
*Skin: Dull, may be dry or have discoloration

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Gastrointestinal System:
-Abdomen: Mild distension, tenderness in epigastrium, gurgling sounds
-Bowel Sounds: Reduced or sluggish peristalsis
-Appetite: Markedly reduced
-Nausea, bloating, belching are common complaints
-Constipation or irregular bowel habits
*Nervous System:
-Lethargy, drowsiness, mental fog
-Reduced alertness and dullness due to toxic accumulation
*Other systems:
-No major findings unless chronic and systemic involvement

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS (Modern Correlation)

*Baseline Tests:
*Complete Blood Count (CBC): May show mild anemia or infection signs
*Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR): Elevated in chronic inflammation 
*C-Reactive Protein (CRP): Elevated if associated with systemic inflammation
*Liver Function Tests (LFT): May show impaired liver enzymes if hepatic metabolism is sluggish
*Serum Electrolytes: May indicate imbalances due to improper digestion
*Thyroid Profile: To rule out hypothyroidism as it mimics Agnimandhya
*Gastro-specific Tests:
*Stool Test: For undigested food particles, parasitic infections
*Helicobacter pylori Test: If gastritis/indigestion is chronic
*Ultrasound Abdomen: To rule out hepatomegaly, fatty liver, gallbladder issues
*Upper GI Endoscopy: If persistent symptoms of indigestion or GERD

🔺AGNIMANDHYA



🔺DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS
 (Modern Correlation of Agnimandhya)

*Functional Dyspepsia
*Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
*Hyperacidity 
*GERD
*gastritis 
*pylori infection 
*Gastrointestinal
*Liver dysfunction-related Agnimandhya
	*Fatty liver 
*Hepatitis
*Gallbladder disease


🔺SAMPRAPTI (Pathogenesis):

*Due to Nidana sevana, Kapha and/or Vata dosha get aggravated → blocks Jatharagni (digestive fire) → leads to Mandagni → Aama formation → Ajirna and systemic impact.
*Dosha: -Predominantly Kapha, sometimes*Vata and Pitta
Dushya:Rasadhatu, Pachaka *Pitta
Srotas:Annavaha Srotas
Roga Marga:Abhyantara
Sadhyasadhyata: Sadhya in early stage*Charaka Chikitsa Sthana 15/44

🔺SAMANYA CHIKITSA (General Management):

*Langhana (Fasting) – to lighten the system
*Deepana-Pachana Dravyas – to enhance digestion (e.g., Trikatu, Chitrak)
*Shodhana (if needed) –*Vamana or Virechana if associated with dosha vitiation
*Agni Vardhana – using*Agni-deepaka formulations
(Charaka Samhita Chikitsa Sthana 15

🔺UPASHAYA (Palliative Factors):

*Intake of Deepana-Pachana ahara

🔺 PRANJAPARADHAM 


🔺NIDANAM (Etiology)

Prajnāparādha literally means “crime against wisdom” or "intellectual blasphemy". It is one of the three primary causes of disease according to Ayurveda:
Charaka Sutrasthana 1/102:
"Prajnaparadha, Asatmendriyartha Samyoga, and Parinama are the three causes of diseases."


🔺 Causes of Prajnaparadha :

*Deliberately choosing unhealthy behaviors
*Ignoring knowledge of right and wrong
*Engaging in actions against natural laws
*Repression of natural urges
*Overuse, misuse, or disuse of senses, mind, or intellect

🔺 PURVAROOPAM (Premonitory Symptoms)

-Not specifically listed in classical texts for Prajnāparādha, but general early signs include:
-Mental confusion
-Disinterest in good habits
-Poor judgment
-Emotional instability

🔺LAKSANA (Symptoms)

*The symptoms vary depending on the disease caused by the prajnaparadha, as it is an indirect cause.
-General signs:
*Decline in mental faculties
*Repeated mistakes
*Stress, anxiety, delusions
*Diseases due to suppressed urges (e.g., constipation, headaches)
 Reference:
*Charaka Vimanastana 5/6
"Manasa vyadhi and sharirika vyadhi both can be caused by prajnaparadha."

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION:

*Observation of behavior (abnormal actions, impulsiveness)
*Mental state assessment – restlessness, anxiety, emotional instability
*Speech – incoherent, aggressive, or depressed tone
*Appearance – hygiene neglect, poor dressing sense
*Sleep pattern – insomnia or hypersomnia

🔺 SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION:

*Central Nervous System (CNS):
*Level of orientation
*Cognitive function testing (memory, reasoning, judgment)
*Reflexes, coordination (for substance-induced cases)
*Psychiatric Examination:
*Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE)
*Mental Status Examination (MSE) – appearance, behavior, thought process, mood, perception


🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS
 (as per modern correlation):

*Based on clinical suspicion (substance use, mental illness, etc.):
*CBC – rule out infections or anemia affecting cognition
*Thyroid profile (T3, T4, TSH) – to rule out hypothyroidism-related cognitive decline
*Blood sugar & HbA1c – to rule out diabetic encephalopathy
*LFT/KFT – liver or kidney-related encephalopathy
*Serum electrolytes – especially sodium/calcium abnormalities
*Toxicology screen – for substance abuse
*MRI/CT brain – in suspected structural or degenerative brain issues
*EEG – in suspected seizure disorder or encephalopathy

🔺NIDANAM (Etiology)

*Astmyendriyartha Samyoga refersto the improper contact of senses (Indriyas) with their respective objects (Artha).
*Types of improper contact:
*Atiyoga – Overuse (e.g., loud noise, excessive viewing)
*Ayoga – Non-use (e.g., avoiding sound, light, etc.)
*Mithyayoga – Misuse (e.g., watching terrifying images, listening to unpleasant sounds)
*Reference:Charaka Samhita Sutrasthana 8/5
*Charaka Samhita Sharirasthana 1/102
*Ashtanga Hridaya Sutrasthana 1/20


🔺PURVAROOPAM (Prodromal symptoms)

*Pūrvāroopas are generally vague sensory discomforts, such as:
*Dullness or over-sensitivity in a specific sense
*Avoidance or craving for certain stimuli
*Early fatigue or irritation upon sensory use
*These vary depending on the specific Indriya affected (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin, mind).

🔺LAKSANAM 
*(Symptoms)

*Depending on the Indriya involved:
*Indriya	Symptoms
-Chakshur (Eyes)	Blurred vision, photophobia, eye strain

Ghrana (Nose)	Loss of smell, aversion to smell
Jivha (Tongue)	Taste disorders
Sparshana (Skin)	Numbness, tingling, hypersensitivity
Mana (Mind)	Confusion, irritability, emotional imbalance
(Charaka Samhita Sutrasthana 8/5-10

*Parameter	Findings/Observations

-Nervous System

*Visual acuity issues from overexposure to screens
-ENT Exam
*Tinnitus, temporary hearing loss, discomfort from loud noise

*Symptoms of depression, anxiety, ADHD

🔺 KAPALA BHAGNAM (SKULL FRACTURE)

🔺NIDANAM (Causes)

As per Bhela Samhita, Bhagna (fracture) is caused by:

*Bahya Abhighata (external trauma) – fall, blow, accident.
*Vega Darana – suppression or forceful expression of natural urges.
*Ativyayama (excess exertion)
*Atyucchrāyāt patanam (falling from height)
*Āghāta by weapons or blunt object
-For Kapala Bhagnam, trauma directly over the skull region (head injury) is the chief cause.

🔺PURVARUPAM (Prodromal symptoms)

These may not always be specifically mentioned for Kapāla Bhagna, but general signs may include:
*Dizziness
*Headache
*Blurred vision
*Confusion or disorientation


🔺LAKSANAM (Symptoms)

*As described in Suśruta Saṃhitā Chikitsāsthāna 3/18–19:

*Śoṇitapāta (bleeding from nostrils, ears)
*Moha (loss of consciousness)
*Bhrama (giddiness)
*Akṣṇoḥ vikāraḥ (eye abnormalities)
*Mūrcchā (fainting)
*Jṛmbhā (excessive yawning)
*Vaktra vikṛti (facial disfigurement)
*Kapāla śūla (pain in skull region)
*Vedana (severe pain at the site)
*Śiraśūla (headache)

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*Consciousness level: Assess using Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)
*Pallor, cyanosis, icterus
*Pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, temperature
*Bleeding from nose/ear/mouth
*Signs of head trauma: scalp swelling, laceration, hematoma

🔺 SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Central Nervous System (CNS)
*GCS scoring
*Pupillary reflexes
*Signs of raised intracranial pressure (ICP): vomiting, bradycardia, altered consciousness
*Cranial nerve examination
*Motor and sensory system evaluation
-ENT and Eye
*Rhinorrhea or otorrhea (CSF leak)
*Battle’s sign (ecchymosis behind ear – basal fracture)
*Raccoon eyes (periorbital ecchymosis – anterior cranial fossa fracture)
*Check for diplopia, vision changes
*Respiratory and Cardiovascular
*Secondary trauma assessment
*Oxygen saturation monitoring
*Auscultation to rule out aspiration or chest trauma

🔺 LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*Complete Blood Count (CBC): detect hemorrhage or infection
*Coagulation Profile: PT, aPTT, INR (especially before surgery)
*Blood grouping & crossmatch: if transfusion needed
*Blood glucose & electrolytes: for baseline and monitoring
*CSF Analysis (if leak suspected): glucose test, β2-transferrin
*Toxicology screening: if unconscious or substance abuse suspected
 -Imaging
*CT Scan (Non-contrast head): primary investigation for skull fracture
*X-ray Skull: limited use; mostly replaced by CT
*MRI Brain: to assess soft tissue/brain injury
*CT Angiography: if vascular injury suspected

🔺 KAPALA BHAGNAM (SKULL FRACTURE


🔺DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS


1. Linear Skull Fracture
2. Depressed Skull Fracture
3. Basilar Skull Fracture
4. Diastatic Skull Fracture
5. Penetrating Head Injury
6. Intracranial Hemorrhage (e.g.,
Epidural Hematoma
Subdural Hematoma
Subarachnoid Hemorrhage)
7. Concussion
8. Contusion of Brain
9. Post-traumatic Cerebral Edema
10. Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) – mild/moderate/severe
11. Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) Leak
12. Facial Bone Fractures (especially frontal sinus or orbital wall fractures)


🔺 SAMPRAPTI (Pathogenesis)

*Trauma (Abhighāta) leads to Kapāla Asthi Bhagna.
*Vitiation of Vāta Doṣa leads to:
*Pain
*Displacement of bone fragments
*Dryness, degeneration
*Bleeding due to involvement of Rakta Dhātu.
*If severe, can involve Majjā Dhātu (marrow/brain) → neurological symptoms.


🔺SAMANYA CHIKITSA (General Treatment)

*According to Suśruta Saṃhitā – Chikitsāsthāna 3/3–7, the general management of Asthi Bhagna includes:
*Bhagna sthāna sthāpana (immobilization/reduction)
*Bandhana (bandaging) – splinting or cranial dressing
*Sneha (internal & external oleation) with Mahānarayana taila, Bala taila
*Swedana (sudation therapy) for relieving pain
*Pañcakarma like Basti – especially Mātrā Basti to pacify Vāta
*Rakta sthāpana in case of bleeding (using Lodhra, Nāgakesara, etc.)
*Medhya Rasayana – Brahmi, Śaṅkhuśhpi, etc. for memory/consciousness

🔺 UPASHAYA (Relieving factors)

*Application of Sneha, Mṛdu Sweda
*Use of Medhya drugs (Brahmi, Mandukaparni)
*Vāta pacifying diet and regimen
*Immobilization and rest

🔺 ANUPASAYA (Aggravating factors)

*Movement of head or neck
*Exposure to cold or wind
*Suppression of natural urges
*Loud noises or mental agitation
*Vāta-vardhaka āhāra-vihāra

🔺VISESA CHIKITSA(Specific Treatment)

*As per Suśruta Saṃhitā – Chikitsāsthāna 3, Kapāla Bhagna (among the 6 types of Bhagna) needs specific care:
*Śastrakarma (Surgical intervention) when:
*There is depression of skull bone
*Wound is open or compound fracture
-Signs of Majjā avapāta (brain matter exposure)
-Ayurvedic medicines:
-Yograj Guggulu, Lakshādi Guggulu – bone healing
-Abha Guggulu, Rasnā Saptaka Kaṣāya
*Bala taila – external application and Śirobasti
-Ghṛta preparations: Brahmi ghṛta, Kalyāka ghṛta – for neurological symptoms
-Rasāyana:
*Aśvagandhā, Śatāvarī, Gudūci, Pippalī Rasāyana
*Classical References:
*Suśruta Saṃhitā Chikitsāsthāna 3/1–19
*Suśruta Saṃhitā Nidānasthāna 15/41 (Bhagna classification)
*Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdaya Uttarasthāna 27
*Bhela Saṃhitā – Bhagna Cikitsā
*Bhāvaprakāśa – Bhagna Prakaraṇa

🔺VYANGA

🔺NIDANAM (Etiology)

*Vyanga is mainly caused due to:
-Krodha (Anger)
-Shoka (Grief)
-Shrama (Exertion)
-Nidra nasha (Loss of sleep)
-Vega dharana (Suppression of natural urges)
Reference: “Krodha shoka nidra kshaya shrama vegadharanat cha vyanga upajayate”
— Ashtanga Hridaya, Uttarasthana 24/3

🔺PURVARUPAM (Prodromal Symptoms)

*Not explicitly mentioned, but can be inferred:
*Localized darkness or dullness
*Mild dryness
*Slight discoloration on facial skin

🔺 LAKSHANAM (Symptoms)

*Nirujam (Painless)
*Shyava varna mandala (bluish-black circular patches)
*Occurs mostly on face
*Twak vaivarnya – Skin discoloration

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION:

*Skin type: Dry, oily, or combination
*Lesion location: Usually on cheeks, forehead, upper lip, nose
*Color: Brown to gray-brown macules
*Onset and duration: Sudden or gradual, often chronic
*History of sun exposure
*Use of cosmetics or medications 
*Family history of pigmentation disorders
*Hormonal history: Pregnancy, oral contraceptives, thyroid dysfunction
*Stress and sleep pattern

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION:

*Thyroid gland: Check for goiter or nodules
*Liver and gastrointestinal system: To rule out underlying hepatic issues
*Endocrine system: Signs of hormonal imbalance (e.g., PCOS, Cushing's)
*Reproductive system (females): *Menstrual history, hirsutism
*Psychological evaluation: Assess for stress or depression


🔺 LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS:

1. Thyroid Function Tests (T3, T4, TSH
2. Liver Function Tests (LFT)
3. Hormonal Panel (especially in females):
*Estrogen
*Progesterone 
*LH, FSH
*Testosterone (for PCOS suspicion)
4. Blood sugar levels (FBS, PPBS)
5. ANA (to rule out autoimmune causes)
6. Skin biopsy (rarely required; if diagnosis is uncertain)

*Exposure to sun

*Vata-Pitta aggravating diet and lifestyle

-External Applications (Lepa)

-Eladi churna with milk as face pack
-Mukha lepa with Rakta prasadaka dravyas
- Reference:
Ashtanga Hridaya – Uttara Tantra 24

🔺 ADDITIONAL THERAPIES
*Nasya karma (with medicated oils like Anu taila)
*Raktamokshana (if there is rakta dushti)

🔺KARNAPALI KACHAPIKA 

🔺NIDANAM (Etiology)

*The causative factors of Karnapāli Kachapika are mostly Kapha–Pitta aggravating factors, which can include:
*Intake of snigdha (unctuous), guru (heavy), and vidāhi (pungent) foods
*Abhiṣyandi ahāra (obstructive food like curd, paneer)
*Exposure to cold winds, bathing in cold water frequently
*Poor ear hygiene, recurrent infection
*Suppression of natural urges (e.g. sneezing, vomiting)
*Use of cold oils in ear or overuse of ear buds
*Prāgvaāta karma (sudden exposure to wind)
*Reference: Ashtanga Hridaya (Uttara Sthana 12), Sushruta Samhita (Uttara Tantra 20)

🔺PURVARUPAM (Prodromal Symptoms)

*Mild itching in ear
*Heaviness in ear
*Occasional mild pain or discomfort
*Feeling of fullness or blockage
*Mild watery discharge
*Reference: Acharya Vagbhata & Sushruta on karṇaroga pūrvarūpa

🔺 LAKṢAṆAM (Symptoms)

*Kachapika specifically presents as:
*Manda śula (dull pain) in the ear
*Śopha (swelling) behind or around ear
*Ear appears like the back of a tortoise (Kachapika = tortoise-backed), due to rounded swelling
*Jalapūrṇa iva śabdaḥ – sensation of fluid or crackling sound in the ear
*Discharge: mucous or serous, sometimes thick
*Mastoid area tenderness
* Reference: Ashtanga Hridaya Uttara Sthana 12/16–18

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION:

-Vital Signs:
*Temperature (fever may suggest infection)
*Pulse, Blood Pressure, Respiratory Rate
*Signs of infection or inflammation:
*Look for erythema, warmth, and tenderness
*Check for systemic involvement:
*Lymphadenopathy (preauricular/postauricular)
*General malaise or other systemic symptoms

🔺 SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION:

*Ear Examination (Otoscopic & Physical):
*Inspect pinna: swelling, redness, abscess, discharge
*Check for trauma, insect bite, or signs of cellulitis
*Neck and Lymph Nodes: Palpate for cervical and postauricular nodes
*Cranial Nerve Examination: If facial nerve involvement suspected
*ENT and Skin Examination: Rule out associated dermatological or upper respiratory conditions

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS:

1. Complete Blood Count (CBC) – Look for raised WBC count (infection/inflammation)
2. ESR / CRP – Elevated in inflammation
3. Bacterial culture & sensitivity (if discharge/aspiration present)
4. Pus aspiration for gram stain – In case of abscess
5. Blood sugar level – Especially if diabetes is suspected (which predisposes to infections)
6. Imaging if needed – USG or CT scan of the ear (for abscess or perichondritis)

*Gandhaka Rasayana

🔺ANUPASAYA (Aggravating factors)

*Cold exposure
*Sour, salty, fermented foods
*Suppression of natural urges
*Application of cold oils in ear
*Improper pratisarana or ear cleansing

🔺 VISESHA CHIKITSA (Specific Treatment)

-Local Applications:
*Karṇapurana (ear drops) with:
*Dashamula taila
*Nirgundi taila
*Bilva taila
*Pratisarana with Triphala choorna or Haridra for local swelling
*Lepa (medicated paste) over mastoid swelling:
*Eranda moola + Nirgundi + Haridra
*If suppuration occurs (abscess):
*Bhedana karma (incision and drainage) under sterile conditions
*Followed by vrana shodhana and ropana with:
*Jatyadi Taila, Pancha tikta ghrita
*Reference: Sushruta Samhita Uttara Tantra 20/17-20; Ashtanga Hridaya Uttara Sthana 12

5. PURE TONE AUDIOMETRY (PTA) – TO EVALUATE HEARING LOSS
6. MRI/CT BRAIN – IF INTRACRANIAL SPREAD SUSPECTED

*Ear drops made from herbs like Nimba, Haridra, Yashtimadhu

*Excessive oil instillation in ears
*Exposure to dust, wind, water
*Scratching the ear frequently

*Virechana with trivrit, draksha, haritaki
*Nasya with Nimbadi taila
*Krimighna virechana if krimi lakshana present
* Local Treatment:
*Karna dharana: Putting Nimbadi taila, Arimedadi taila, or Chandana bala lakshadi taila in the ear
*Dhoomapana (medicated smoke) for drying and disinfecting the ear
*Gandusha with Triphala kwatha, Yashtimadhu kwatha
* Internal Medications:
*Triphala guggulu, Nimbadi churna, Chandraprabha vati, Guggulu panchapala churna
*Amrutadi guggulu in chronic suppurative conditions
- Classical References:
* Sushruta Samhita, Uttara Tantra – Chapter 20
* Ashtanga Hridaya, Uttara Sthana – Chapter 12

 (Symptoms)

*Charaka Chikitsa 17/61-65
*Vega aagatam swasam (sudden bouts of breathlessness)
*Shwasa kruchrata (difficulty in breathing)
*Urah shoola (chest pain)
*Kapha nishthivanam (expectoration of thick sputum)
*Ghurghuraka (wheezing sound)
*Vaishwari (change in voice)
*Nidra nasha (insomnia due to dyspnea)

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION:

1. Appearance: Patient may appear anxious, dyspneic (short of breath)
2. Posture: Patient may assume a sitting, forward-leaning position to ease breathing (tripod position).
3. Speech: Difficulty speaking full sentences during acute attacks.
4. Respiratory rate: Increased (Tachypnea).
5. Pulse: Tachycardia (especially during attack).
6. Use of accessory muscles: Sternocleidomastoid and intercostals active in inspiration.
7. Cyanosis: In severe or prolonged cases.
8. Pallor: Sometimes observed.
9. Clubbing: Not usually present in asthma (helps rule out other conditions).


🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION:

*Respiratory System:
*Inspection:
*Barrel-shaped chest (in chronic cases)
*Prolonged expiration
*Palpation: Decreased chest expansion
*Percussion: Hyperresonant note
*Auscultation:
*Wheezing (especially during expiration)
*Decreased breath sounds (in severe obstruction)
*Rhonchi (musical sound)
*Cardiovascular System:
*May show tachycardia or pulsus paradoxus (in severe attack)

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS:

1. CBC (Complete Blood Count):
*Eosinophilia often present
*Mild leukocytosis (during exacerbations)
2. Sputum Examination:
*Curschmann’s spirals, Charcot-Leyden crystals, eosinophils
3. Chest X-ray:
*May show hyperinflated lungs
*Flattened diaphragm in chronic asthma
4. Pulmonary Function Tests(PFTs):
*↓ FEV1 (Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 sec)
*↓ FEV1/FVC ratio
*Improves with bronchodilator (reversible obstruction)
5. Peak Expiratory Flow Rate (PEFR):
*Reduced during attack
*Daily monitoring helps assess control
6. Allergy Testing (if allergic asthma suspected):
*Skin prick test
*Serum IgE levels – may be elevated
7. Arterial Blood Gas (ABG):
*In acute severe asthma:
*Early stage: ↓ CO₂ (hypocapnia), ↑ O₂
*Late stage: ↑ CO₂ (hypercapnia), ↓ O₂ → respiratory failure

🔺 NIDANA (निदानम्) – Causes

*The main causative factors (according to Acharya Sushruta – Su. Ut. 20/7) include:
*Kshata (trauma) to tongue or its base
*Kaphaja vitiation (especially due to kapha-aggravating ahara-vihara)
*Mamsa and Rakta dushti
*Retention of doshas under the tongue
*Overuse of heavy, unctuous, and cold foods


🔺PURVARUPA (पूर्वरूपाणि) – Premonitory Symptoms

*Although not distinctly mentioned, general prodromal signs of jihvaroga may include:
*Slight discomfort under the tongue
*Feeling of heaviness or swelling
*Mild pain or tension in the tongue or mouth floor


🔺LAKSHANA (लक्षणानि) – SYMPTOMS

As per Sushruta Samhita – Uttara Tantra 20/7:
*A rounded, raised swelling occurs beneath the tongue
*Swelling appears like a blister or air-filled balloon (resembling a frog’s underthroat sac – hence modern synonym ranula)
*It causes difficulty in speaking, chewing, or swallowing
*May be painless or mildly painful
*Soft, bluish, or translucent appearance (in kapha dominance)



🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION:

*Vital signs: Temperature (check for fever), pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate.
*Appearance: Look for signs of discomfort, drooling, or difficulty speaking/swallowing.
*Oral hygiene: Assess for poor hygiene or trauma.
*Lymph nodes: Palpate for submandibular or cervical lymphadenopathy.

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION:

*ENT Examination:
*Inspect oral cavity (floor of mouth, tongue movement, swelling, pus).
*Palpation of sublingual swelling: fluctuant or firm?
*Tongue elevation test: may reveal sublingual swelling.
*Neurological Exam (if speech/swallowing affected).
*Neck Examination: For tenderness, masses, or signs of spread.

🔺 LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS:

*Complete Blood Count (CBC): Look for elevated WBCs (infection).
*CRP/ESR: Inflammatory markers.
*Culture & Sensitivity: If pus or fluid is drained.
*Blood sugar levels: Especially in recurrent abscess (diabetes link).
*Ultrasound (Neck/Oral Cavity): To detect cyst or abscess.
*MRI or CT scan (if needed): For deeper infection or mass assessment.

🔺 DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

1. Ranula – Mucous cyst under the tongue due to sublingual gland duct obstruction.
2. Mucocele – Minor salivary gland cyst (usually painless).
3. Sialolithiasis – Salivary duct stone (may cause painful swelling).
4. Sublingual Abscess – Bacterial infection; often painful, with fever.
5. Dermoid/Epidermoid Cyst – Congenital, slow-growing swelling.
6. Ludwig's Angina – Serious, bilateral cellulitis of floor of mouth.
7. Neoplasms – Benign or malignant tumors (e.g., squamous cell carcinoma).
8. Lingual Thyroid or Thyroglossal Duct Cyst – Rare, congenital anomalies.

🔺SAMPRAPTI (सम्प्राप्तिः) – Pathogenesis

🔺 GARBHAPATANAM /ABORTION



🔺 DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

1. Threatened Abortion – vaginal bleeding without cervical dilation
2. Inevitable Abortion – vaginal bleeding with open cervical os
3. Incomplete Abortion – partial expulsion of products of conception
4. Complete Abortion – all products expelled, uterus empty
5. Missed Abortion – fetal demise without expulsion
6. Septic Abortion – infection after incomplete abortion
7. Ectopic Pregnancy – pregnancy outside uterus, often in fallopian tube
8. Molar Pregnancy – gestational trophoblastic disease
9. Implantation bleeding – early pregnancy spotting
10. Cervical or vaginal pathology – e.g., polyps, carcinoma


🔺SAMPRAPTI 
(सम्प्राप्ति – Pathogenesis)

*Vitiated Apāna Vāta gets obstructed due to kapha or māṃsa granthi, or is weakened, preventing natural expulsion.
*Obstruction may also be mechanical due to dead fetus or malposition.
*Leads to difficulty, delay, or abnormal expulsion of fetus or placental products.

*Bhāvaprakāśa (Kṣudraroga Prakaraṇa)

*Mild itching (Kaṇḍū)

🔺LAKSANAM 
 (Symptoms)

*Severe itching (Kaṇḍū)

* Musculoskeletal Examination
*Tenderness over calcaneus/plantar fascia
*Limited dorsiflexion or plantar flexion
*Swelling around ankle joint or foot
*Deformity or nodular growth (if present)

*Reflexes – ankle jerk

*X-ray foot/ankle – check for spurs, deformity, or fracture

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*General appearance – distress, pallor, cyanosis, respiratory difficulty
*Pulse – tachycardia (possible hypovolemia or shock)
*Blood pressure – hypotension in severe cases
*Respiratory rate – tachypnea or bradypnea depending on severity
*Temperature – normal or low (shock)
*Level of consciousness – alertness, confusion, or unconsciousness
*Skin – pallor, diaphoresis, cold clammy extremities
*Posture – splinting of chest, reluctance to move
*Inspection of chest – swelling, deformity, bruising, open wounds, asymmetry of movement

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Respiratory System
*Inspection: unequal chest movement, flail segment, visible wound
*Palpation: tenderness, crepitus (subcutaneous emphysema), rib step deformity
*Percussion: dullness (hemothorax) or hyperresonance (pneumothorax)
*Auscultation: diminished/absent breath sounds, crackles, wheeze
*Cardiovascular System
*Heart sounds: muffled (pericardial tamponade)
*Jugular venous distension (tension pneumothorax, cardiac tamponade)
*Signs of shock
*Abdomen
*Check for associated injuries (diaphragmatic rupture, organ injury)

🔺 LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*CBC – anemia, leukocytosis
*Blood grouping & cross-matching – if transfusion required
*ABG (Arterial Blood Gas) – hypoxia, acidosis
*Chest X-ray – rib fracture, lung collapse, hemothorax, pneumothorax
*CT scan (Thorax) – detailed injury mapping
*ECG – arrhythmia, myocardial injury
*Ultrasound / FAST – pericardial or pleural fluid
*Serum electrolytes – in severe trauma
*Coagulation profile – before surgery if indicated

🔺 YONI PICHU



📌DEFINITION

🔸Yoni Pichu is a local vaginal treatment in which a sterile cotton swab/pad (pichu) soaked in medicated oil or ghee is placed inside the vagina for a specified period to treat various gynecological disorders.


📌DRUGS USED 

🔸Yashtimadhu Taila
🔸Bala Taila
🔸Jatyadi Taila
🔸Shatadhauta Ghrita
🔸Triphaladi Taila
🔸Dhanvantaram Taila
🔸Kumari Taila


📌PROCEDURE

🔸 Preparation – Patient empties bladder; genital area cleaned with warm water/decoction (e.g., Triphala Kashaya).
🔸Position – Lithotomy position.
🔸 Medicine Preparation – Selected medicated oil/ghee warmed mildly.
🔸 Pichu Preparation – Sterile cotton swab is soaked in the medicated oil/ghee.
🔸 Insertion – Pichu placed gently inside vagina covering cervical region.
🔸Retention – Kept for 30 min to several hours (as advised).
🔸Removal & Cleaning – Pichu removed; area cleaned with lukewarm water or mild decoction.


🔺INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Yoni Vyapad
🔸Vandhyatva
🔸Yonikanda
🔸Yoni Daha
🔸Yoni Kandu
🔸Yoni Srava
🔸Vataja Yoni Roga
🔸Pittaja Yoni Roga
🔸Kaphaja Yoni Roga
🔸Vulvovaginitis
🔸Cervical erosion


🔺MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸During menstruation
🔸Pregnancy (unless prescribed for specific condition)
🔸Acute genital infections
🔸Sexually transmitted diseases (active stage)
🔸Genital trauma or bleeding

🔺PRECAUTIONS

🔸Maintain strict hygiene of hands, cotton, and instruments.
🔸Avoid overheated oil (only lukewarm).
🔸Check for oil/ghee allergies before application.
🔸Do not exceed prescribed retention time.
🔸Stop treatment if burning, itching, swelling, or discomfort occurs.

🔺YONI VARTI / INTRA VAGINAL MEDICATED SUPPOSITORY

📌DEFINITION

🔸Yoni Varti is a form of local intravaginal therapy in which a medicated stick or bolus (varti) made from herbal drugs is inserted into the vagina for therapeutic purposes. It is mainly used to treat local infections, inflammation, and disorders of the female reproductive tract.


📌DRUGS USED

🔸Triphala
🔸Lodhra
🔸Haridra
🔸Guggulu
🔸Daruharidra
🔸Neem (Nimba)

🔸Manjistha
🔸Shatavari
🔸Jati
🔸Guduchi


📌PROCEDURE

1. Patient is advised to empty bladder and clean the local area.
2. Perform gentle vaginal cleansing with lukewarm medicated decoction (e.g.,Triphala Kwatha).

15/08/2025, 12:06 - +91 95446 87331: 🔺TREATMENT NO :06
🔺 NJAVARA KIZHI 

📌DEFINITION

Njavara Kizhi (Shashtika Shali Pinda Sweda) is a type of sudation therapy where the body is massaged with boluses containing cooked Njavara rice, milk, and herbal decoction to induce sweating, nourish tissues, and relieve stiffness.


📌DRUGS USED 

🔸Njavara rice (Shashtika Shali)
🔸Bala (Sida cordifolia) decoction
🔸Cow’s milk
🔸Ghee
🔸Herbal oils (as per condition – e.g., Ksheerabala taila)

📌PROCEDURE

1. Preparation of Bolus:

🔸Cook Njavara rice in a mixture of Bala root decoction and milk until soft.
🔸Tie the cooked rice into small cotton cloth pouches (kizhi).

2. Application:

🔸Patient is given mild oil massage with suitable medicated oil.
🔸Warm boluses are dipped repeatedly in hot milk-decoction mixture and massaged over the whole body or affected part in synchronized strokes.

3. Duration:

🔸Generally 30–45 minutes per session.

4. Completion:

🔸After sweating is induced, remove boluses.
🔸Wipe the body and apply a thin coat of medicated oil.
🔸Patient rests for some time; light diet advised.


📌INDICATED DISEASES 

🔸Osteoarthritis
🔸Rheumatoid arthritis
🔸Muscular dystrophy
🔸Neuromuscular disorders
🔸Low back pain
🔸Hemiplegia
🔸Cervical spondylosis
🔸Sciatica
🔸Generalized weakness

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Fever
🔸Acute inflammation
🔸Skin diseases with infection
🔸Severe cardiac disorders
🔸Uncontrolled diabetes
🔸Severe hypertension
🔸Active bleeding disorders


📌PRECAUTIONS IN TREATMENT

🔸Maintain correct temperature (avoid burns).
🔸Avoid excessive pressure during massage in weak or injured tissues.
🔸Monitor patient’s comfort and sweating response.
🔸Adjust number of boluses to maintain warmth throughout.
🔸Use fresh milk and decoction each session.
🔸Avoid in pregnancy unless specifically indicated and supervised.

🔺 VISESHA CHIKITSA (Specific Management)

🔺 RAKTHA MOKSHANAM / BLOOD LETTING THERAPY

📌DEFINITION

Raktamokṣaṇam is one of the Pañcakarma procedures in Ayurveda aimed at eliminating vitiated blood (doṣha-duṣhita rakta) from the body to cure blood-borne and Pitta-dominant disorders. It is a shodhana (purificatory) therapy.

📌DRUGS USED

🔸Jalaukā (leech)
🔸Alabu (bitter gourd shell)
🔸Śṛṅga (horn)
🔸Sirāvyadha (venesection instruments)
🔸Prachchanna (lancet, scalpel)


📌PROCEDURE

1. Purvakarma (pre-procedure):

🔸Examination of patient, selection of method (jalaukā, sirāvyadha, alabu, śṛṅga, prachchanna).
🔸Preparation of patient and area.

2. Pradhanakarma (main procedure)

🔸Application of the chosen method:
🔸Jalaukā (leech application): Leech is applied to the affected site.
🔸Sirāvyadha (venesection): Controlled incision in vein to let out blood.
🔸Alabu/Śṛṅga/Prachchanna: Localized bloodletting techniques.

3. Paschatkarma (post-procedure)

🔸Removal of leech/incision closure.
🔸Dressing, applying healing drugs, dietary advice, observation.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Vatarakta
🔸Visarpa
🔸Arbuda
🔸Kushta
🔸Vidradhi
🔸Pidaka
🔸Shvitra
🔸Gridhrasi (in severe cases)
🔸Rakta-pitta
🔸Visha roga

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Bala (children)
🔸Vriddha (elderly)
🔸Stri (pregnant women, menstruating women)
🔸Alpa-rakta (anemia, low blood volume)
🔸Pandu roga (anemia)
🔸Karshya (emaciated persons)
🔸Atisara (diarrhea, dysentery)
🔸Kshata kshina (injury, debility)
🔸Murcha, Bhrama (fainting tendencies)


📌PRECAUTIONS IN TREATMENT

🔸Patient should be examined for Bala (strength), Rakta mātra (blood volume), and Roga bala.
🔸Perform in aseptic conditions.
🔸Avoid excessive bloodletting to prevent shock, murcha (fainting), bala kshaya (weakness).
🔸Always keep stambhana (hemostatic drugs) ready.
🔸Post-therapy care: light diet, rest, avoiding exertion, spicy food, alcohol.

🔺SHIRAKAMPHAM /
(HEAD TREMOR)

🔺NIDANAM 
(निदानम् – Etiological factors)

*Ati mātra kṣaya of Vāta doṣa due to:
*Ati vyāyāma (excessive exercise)
*Ati chintā (excessive worry/stress)
*Rūkṣa–laghu āhāra (dry, light food intake)
*Dhātu kṣaya (tissue depletion, esp. majjā & śukra)
*Jara (aging process)
*All these lead to Vāta prakopa in the śiras and cause kampana (tremor).
*Reference: Caraka Sūtrasthāna 20/11; Suśruta Sūtrasthāna 24/8.

🔺PURVARUPAM
 (पूर्वरूपम् – Premonitory signs)

*Śiro gaurava (heaviness of head)
*Manda śūla (mild pain in head)
*Bhrama (giddiness)
*Sandigdha vākyam (unclear speech in some cases)
*Daurbalya (weakness)

🔺LAKSANAM 
 (लक्षणम् – Clinical features)

*Kapana (tremors) in the head
*Kampana aggravated on movement
*Śiraḥ-śūla (headache)
*Nidrā-nāśa (insomnia due to Vāta prakopa)
*Manyā-stambha (stiffness of neck)
*In chronic cases: hand tremor, jaw tremor, speech disturbance may also be present.
*Ref: Suśruta Uttara-tantra 25/3, Vāta-vyādhi lakṣaṇa.

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*Gait observation – unsteadiness, shuffling, festination
*Posture – stooped or rigid posture
*Tremor observation – at rest, during activity, or intentional
*Speech – slow, low-pitched, slurred speech
*Facial expression – mask-like face, reduced blinking
*Muscle tone – rigidity or spasticity
*Reflexes – exaggerated or diminished depending on cause

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Central Nervous System (CNS):
*Tremors (resting, postural, or intention type)
*Bradykinesia (slowness of movements)
*Rigidity of muscles
*Loss of coordination, imbalance
*Cardiovascular system: rule out postural hypotension in neurodegenerative disorders
*Endocrine system: tremors in hyperthyroidism
*Respiratory system: not directly involved but can assess for drug-induced side effects


🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*Blood tests:
*Thyroid function tests (T3, T4, TSH) → to rule out hyperthyroidism
*Blood sugar (to rule out hypoglycemia-induced tremor)
*Serum electrolytes (Ca, Mg, K, Na) → electrolyte imbalance causing tremor
*Liver and renal function tests (drug metabolism & systemic disease effects)
*Neurological imaging:
*MRI/CT Brain – to detect basal ganglia, cerebellar or structural lesions
*Dopamine transporter scan (DaT-SPECT) – for Parkinson’s disease

🔺ANUPASAYA

*Rūkṣa, laghu āhāra (dry, fasting, undernutrition)

*Intraocular pressure measurement (to rule out secondary glaucoma)

🔺 VIRECHANAM/ PURGATION

📌Definition
🔸Virechanam is one among the Panchakarma therapies, in which purgation is induced by administering suitable purgative medicines, aimed at expelling vitiated Pitta dosha (mainly) along with other doshas through the anal route.

📌DRUGS USED 

🔸Trivrit
🔸Aragwadha
🔸Danti
🔸Draksha
🔸Haritaki
🔸Eranda taila
🔸Avipattikara churna
🔸Nimbapatra
🔸Kutaja


📌PROCEDURE

1. Poorvakarma (pre-procedure):

🔸Deepana–Pachana
🔸Snehapana (internal oleation)
🔸Abhyanga & Swedana (external oleation + sudation)

2. Pradhanakarma (main procedure):

🔸Patient given purgative medicine early in the morning on empty stomach with warm water/milk/ghee.
🔸Patient monitored for onset of vegas (purgation urges).
🔸Purgation continues till proper samyak virechana lakshanas appear.

3. Paschatkarma (post-procedure):

🔸Samsarjana krama (specific diet regimen with gradual transition from light to normal food).
🔸Rest advised.


📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Kamala (Jaundice)
🔸Pandu (Anemia)
🔸Raktapitta (Bleeding disorders)
🔸Kushtha (Skin diseases)
🔸Amavata (Rheumatoid arthritis)
🔸Gulma (Abdominal tumors/masses)
🔸Udara roga (Ascites)
🔸Arsha (Piles)

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Bala (children)
🔸Vriddha (old age)
🔸Pregnancy
🔸Extreme debility
🔸Diarrhea, dysentery
🔸Severe anemia
🔸Unfit after oleation/sudation
🔸Cardiac patients

📌PRECAUTIONS IN TREATMENT

🔸Ensure proper poorvakarma before starting
🔸Assess patient strength, age, and disease condition
🔸Use appropriate dose & drug based on constitution
🔸Strict observation during purgation for dehydration & complications
🔸Maintain hygiene and hydration
🔸Follow samsarjana krama strictly after procedure

🔺SUDDHA VRANA


🔺NIDANAM 
(Etiology)

*Śuddha Vraṇa is the stage of a wound that is clean, without infection, with healthy granulation tissue.
*It is usually the outcome of proper wound healing after removal of Doṣa, Doṣa-duṣya saṅga.
*Not directly caused by specific nidānas (etiological factors), rather it is the end result of proper vraṇa-śodhana and vraṇa-ropana measures.
*Acharya Suśruta mentions that after the elimination of doṣa-mala and proper wound care, a wound becomes śuddha (clean).
* Suśruta Saṃhitā, Sūtra Sthāna 22/9; Cikitsā Sthāna 1/46


🔺 PURVAROOPAM (Premonitory Symptoms)

*Since it is a healthy stage of vraṇa, purvarūpa is seen in aśuddha vraṇa (unclean wound), not in śuddha vraṇa.
*Transition signs toward śuddha vraṇa include:
*Reduction of pain, swelling, and redness
*Absence of foul smell and discharge
*Appearance of pinkish granulation tissue
*Wound margins smooth and healthy


🔺LAKSANAM 
 (Clinical Features of Śuddha Vraṇa)

*According to Suśruta:
*Māṃsa ragaḥ – reddish pink healthy granulation tissue
*Māṃsa vr̥ddhiḥ – filling up with new tissue
*Śuddha varṇaḥ – normal skin color
*Māṃsa mādhurya – softness and smoothness of wound bed
*Alpa srāva – minimal or no discharge
*Nirugandha – no foul smell
 * Suśruta Saṃhitā, Sūtra Sthāna 22/9

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*Vital signs: Pulse, BP, Temperature, Respiratory rate
*Pallor, Icterus, Cyanosis, Clubbing, Lymphadenopathy, Edema
*Nutritional status (since wound healing depends on nutrition)
*Systemic review – to rule out systemic illness (diabetes, hypertension, tuberculosis, immunodeficiency, etc.)


🔺 SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Local examination of wound (Śuddha Vraṇa):
*Size, site, depth, edges, floor, margins 
*Discharge – minimal/absent (serous, non-purulent)
*Granulation tissue – healthy red, vascular, non-foul smelling
*No slough or necrosis
*No signs of infection (no pus, redness, spreading cellulitis)
*Tenderness mild or absent
*System-specific:
*Cardiovascular – peripheral circulation assessment
*Respiratory – chronic infections (if systemic cause for delayed healing suspected)
*Nervous system – peripheral neuropathy (in diabetes)
*Musculoskeletal – mobility and deformity around wound site


🔺 LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*Complete Blood Count (CBC) – Hb%, TLC, DLC (rule out infection, anemia)
*Blood Sugar (FBS, PPBS, HbA1C) – to rule out diabetes mellitus
*ESR / CRP – for inflammatory activity
*Wound swab culture & sensitivity (if infection suspected despite clean appearance)
*Serology – HIV, HBsAg, HCV (in chronic non-healing cases)
*Renal and Liver function tests – if systemic disease suspected
*X-ray / Ultrasound – if bone/joint involvement suspected (osteomyelitis, foreign body)

🔺PART NO : 02
🔺SUDDHA VRANA

🔺DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS (DD) 

*Acute wound (incision, laceration, surgical wound, traumatic wound)
*Healing ulcer
*Chronic ulcer (early stage but clean)
*Venous ulcer (in healing stage)
*Diabetic ulcer (controlled, without secondary infection)
*Pressure sore (granulating, non-infected stage)
*Post-burn healing wound

🔺SAMPRAPTI (Pathogenesis)


*Initially, due to injury or nidāna, doṣa duṣṭi occurs leading to aśuddha vraṇa.
*After proper śodhana (cleansing), śamana (pacification), and ropana (healing) therapies, doṣa-mala are eliminated.
*Śuddha vraṇa represents the stage of balanced doṣas and healing response → wound becomes clean, non-infected, and filled with healthy granulation tissue.

🔺SAMANYA CHIKITSA (General Line of Treatment)

*Maintain wound cleanliness and dryness
*Application of ropana dravyas (healing drugs)
*Avoid factors that delay wound healing (dust, trauma, improper bandaging)
*Pathya āhāra-vihāra (proper diet and lifestyle
*Suśruta Saṃhitā, Cikitsā Sthāna 1/46–47

🔺UPASHAYA 
(Wholesome/Beneficial Factors)

*Proper wound dressing (vrana-bandhana)
*Use of ropana taila/ghee (e.g., Jatyādi taila, Ghrita preparations)
*Intake of light, easily digestible, and doṣa-śāmaka diet
*Clean environment

🔺ANUPASHAYA (Unwholesome/Aggravating Factors)

*application of guru, snigdha, abhishyandi dravya on wound
*Excessive moistening or leaving wound exposed to dust/infection
*Improper bandaging
*Indulgence in katu, amla, lavana āhāra (delaying healing)

🔺 VISESHA CHIKITSA
 (Specific Treatment for Śuddha Vraṇa)

*Once wound is śuddha, the aim is ropana (healing and scar formation):
*Ropana Dravyas:
*Jatyādi Taila
*Madhūcchiṣṭa (beeswax) preparations
*Ghṛita based formulations (like Ghṛita kumāri)
*Madhu (honey) application
*Suśruta Saṃhitā, Cikitsā Sthāna 1/46–49
*Bandhana (dressing): Soft, sterile dressing to protect healing tissue.
*Kṣāra-sūtra (if sinus present): Applied till śuddhatva is maintained.

🔺DUSTHA VRANA

🔺NIDANAM 
(Causes)

(Ref: Suśruta Saṃhitā, Sūtrasthāna 22/6, Cikitsāsthāna 1/6)
*Āgantuja – due to trauma, injury, burn, bite, foreign body.
*Doṣaja – vitiation of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha individually or combined.
*Improper management of Śuddha Vraṇa.
*Neglect, repeated contamination, improper dressing.

🔺PURVAROOPAM (Prodromal features)

*Pain, swelling, redness.
*Burning sensation.
*Itching, mild discharge.
*Feeling of heaviness around wound.

🔺LAKSANAM 
 (Clinical features)

*(Ref: Suśruta Cikitsāsthāna 1/8-12)
*Discharge: foul smell, purulent, bloody or excessive.
*Abnormal colour (blue, black, pale, red).
*Excessive pain or no pain (nerve involvement).
*Burning sensation, itching.
*Swelling around wound.
*Slow or non-healing nature.
*Granulation tissue unhealthy (pale, friable, exuberant).

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*General condition of patient – built, nourishment, hydration.
*Vital signs – pulse, BP, temperature, respiratory rate.
*Pallor, icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, edema, lymphadenopathy.
*Nutritional status, anemia signs, systemic illness evidence (diabetes, renal/hepatic disease).

🔺 SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Cardiovascular system – peripheral pulses, signs of peripheral vascular disease.
*Respiratory system – signs of chronic infection, TB.
*Abdomen – hepatomegaly, splenomegaly (suggesting chronic illness).
*Nervous system – peripheral neuropathy (esp. diabetic neuropathy).
*Local examination of ulcer
*Site, size, shape, depth, edge, floor, margin, base.
*Type of discharge, smell, color.
*Surrounding skin (pigmentation, induration, edema).
*Signs of infection (warmth, redness, pus).
*Healing features vs. non-healing features (undermined edges, unhealthy granulation tissue).


🔺 LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*Basic tests
*CBC (Hb%, WBC count, ESR).
*Blood sugar (FBS, PPBS, HbA1c).
*Urine analysis (sugar, protein, ketones).
*Renal function tests (BUN, Creatinine).
*Liver function tests (if systemic illness suspected).
** Local investigations
*Swab culture & sensitivity (for bacterial growth).
*Biopsy of ulcer edge (to rule out malignant change).
*Doppler study (for peripheral arterial disease/venous insufficiency).
*X-ray of part (to rule out osteomyelitis).

🔺 DUSHTA VRANA

🔺DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

*Venous ulcer
*Arterial ulcer
*Diabetic ulcer
*Trophic/Neuropathic ulcer
*Tuberculous ulcer
*Syphilitic ulcer
*Leprotic ulcer
*Malignant ulcer (Marjolin’s ulcer, squamous cell carcinoma)
*Pyogenic ulcer
*Tropical ulcer

🔺SAMPRAPTI (Pathogenesis)

*Nidāna sevana → Doṣa prakopa (Vāta, Pitta, Kapha) → Doṣa saṅcaya at wound site → Dhātu duṣṭi (rakta, māṃsa) → Impaired Śodhana–Ropaṇa → Dhustha Vraṇa (chronic/infected ulcer).


🔺SAMANYA CHIKITSA (General treatment)

*(Ref: Suśruta Cikitsāsthāna 1/24-26, Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdaya Sūtrasthāna 29/4)
*Śodhana (cleansing):
*Kṣāra, Agni, Śastra śodhana (depending on wound).
*Parisheka (irrigation), Avagāha (immersion), Dhāraṇa with Kaṣāya (decoctions).
*Śamana:
*Application of lepa, taila, ghṛta (depending on doṣa).
*Ropaṇa:
*Use of drugs having Ropaṇa, Sandhāna, Vraṇashodhana properties.

🔺UPASAYA 
(Wholesome factors)

*Wound treated with Śodhana dravyas (Triphala, Pañcavalkala).
*Proper aseptic bandaging (Suśruta described 60 types of bandages).
*Use of honey, ghee, and herbal oils (Ropaka dravyas).

🔺ANUPASAYA (Unwholesome factors)

*Untimely or improper dressing.
*Use of guru, snigdha, abhishyandī ahāra.
*Exposure to dust, dirt, insects, trauma.
*Neglect of rest and improper lifestyle.

🔺VISESHA CHIKITSA (Specific management)

*(Ref: Suśruta Cikitsāsthāna 1/38-52)
*Vāta duṣṭa vraṇa – Sneha, svedana, taila, ghee, mṛdu lepa.
*Pitta duṣṭa vraṇa – Śīta upakrama, Tikta-kaṣāya dravya, ghṛta.
*Kapha duṣṭa vraṇa – Kṣāra, uṣṇa lepa, kaṭu-tikta dravyas.
*Saṃsarga/saṃnipāta duṣṭha vraṇa – Combined treatment according to doṣa dominance.
*Śoṇita duṣṭa vraṇa – Raktamokṣaṇa, tikta-kaṣāya dravyas.

*Special measures:
*Madhu (honey): śodhana + ropaṇa.
*Ghṛta (clarified butter): pitta-hara, śīta, ropaka.
*Taila preparations: Nimba taila, Jatyādi taila, Nārāyaṇa taila.
*Kṣāra & Agni karma: for slough and necrotic tissue.
*Śastra karma (surgery): excision, drainage, scraping of unhealthy tissue.
*Classical Reference Summary:
*Suśruta Saṃhitā, Sūtrasthāna 22/6, Cikitsāsthāna 1/6-52
*Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdaya, Sūtrasthāna 29

🔺NASYAM

📌DEFINITION

🔸Nasya is a Panchakarma therapy in which medicated oils, powders, juices, or decoctions are administered through the nasal route. It primarily treats diseases of the head and neck region by clearing accumulated doshas.

📌DRUGS USED

🔸Anu taila
🔸Shadbindu taila
🔸Ksheerabala taila
🔸Brahmi ghritha
🔸Panchendriya vardhana taila
🔸Triphala ghritha
🔸Jivaneeya gana siddha taila
🔸Goghrita

📌PROCEDURE

1. Purva Karma (Preparation)

🔸Gentle facial massage with suitable oil
🔸Mild fomentation (swedana) to face, forehead, neck

2. Pradhana Karma (Main procedure)

🔸Patient lies in supine position with head slightly tilted back
🔸Warm medicated oil/ghee/decoction instilled into nostrils (usually 4–10 drops)
🔸Patient inhales deeply; massage around nose, forehead and palms

3. Paschat Karma (Post procedure)

🔸Spit out excess medicine through mouth
🔸Gentle massage of shoulders, palms, soles
🔸Advise to avoid cold exposure, dust, strong sunlight, exertion immediately after

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Ardhavabhedaka (Migraine)
🔸Apasmara (Epilepsy)
🔸Ardita (Facial palsy)
🔸Siroroga (Headache)
🔸Kasa (Cough)
🔸Jwara (Fever – certain types)
🔸Pinasa (Chronic rhinitis/sinusitis)
🔸Danta roga (Dental disorders)
🔸Indriya vikara (Eye, ear, nose disorders)

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Immediately after food
🔸After alcohol consumption
🔸After sneha pana (internal oleation)
🔸In very young (<7 years) and very old (>80 years)
🔸During pregnancy and menstruation
🔸In indigestion, acute fever, acute rhinitis, intoxication
🔸In severe weakness

📌PRECAUTIONS

🔸Correct selection of medicine and dosage based on dosha and patient’s strength
🔸Should not be done in empty stomach or immediately after meals
🔸Avoid exposure to wind, dust, cold water, day sleep, sexual activity immediately after
🔸Done only under supervision of a trained physician

*Krimi āvaraṇa (intestinal infections).
*Māruta prakopa leading to obstruction in the intestine.

🔺PURVAROOPAM 
(Premonitory symptoms)

*Udarashūla (abdominal pain)
*Āma-janya lakṣaṇas (loss of *appetite, heaviness, indigestion)
*Trishna (excessive thirst)
*Ādhmāna (bloating, distension)
*Manda jvara (low grade fever)

🔺LAKSANAM 
 (Clinical features)

*Severe colicky abdominal pain (Baddha shūla).
*Udaravr̥ddhi (abdominal enlargement).

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*General condition – febrile or toxic look
*Pallor – anemia due to chronic infection
*Icterus – if liver abscess
*Dehydration signs – dry tongue, sunken eyes
*Lymphadenopathy (rare, in TB origin)
*Temperature – fever (usually intermittent, with chills/rigors)
*Pulse – tachycardia
*Blood pressure – may be low in septicemia

*Abdomen
*Inspection: Distension, visible fullness, asymmetry
*Palpation:
*Localized tenderness (right iliac fossa / hypogastrium / hepatic region depending on site)
*Guarding / rigidity
*Palpable lump (ill-defined, tender, soft to firm)
*Percussion: Localized dullness over abscess area
*Auscultation: Decreased or absent bowel sounds (ileus)
*Other Systems
*Respiratory system: basal crepitations if subphrenic abscess
*CVS: tachycardia, septic changes
*CNS: delirium in septicemia

*Anemia (chronic abscess)

*CT Scan Abdomen – gold standard, defines exact location, extent, relation to viscera
*MRI – if needed, for soft tissue delineation
*X-ray Abdomen/Chest: air-fluid level, subdiaphragmatic collection

🔺VAMANAM

📌DEFINITION

🔸Vamana is one of the Panchakarma therapies, in which controlled therapeutic emesis (induced vomiting) is performed to expel aggravated Kapha dosha and associated toxins from the upper gastrointestinal tract.

📌DRUGS USED

🔸Madanaphala
🔸Ikshvaku
🔸Jimutaka
🔸Kutaja
🔸Pippali
🔸Yashtimadhu
🔸Vacha
🔸Saindhava lavana
🔸Madhu

📌PROCEDURE

1. Purvakarma (Pre-operative measures):
🔸Snehana (internal & external oleation)
🔸Swedana (fomentation)
2. Pradhanakarma (Main procedure):
🔸Patient is given emesis-inducing drugs with suitable adjuvants.
🔸Repeated vomiting continues until proper signs of purification (Shuddhi Lakshana) are achieved.
3. Paschatkarma (Post-operative measures):
🔸Samsarjana Krama (gradual dietetic regimen starting from Manda, Peya, Vilepi to normal diet).

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Kasa (Cough)
🔸Shwasa (Asthma)
🔸Kaphaja Jwara (Fever with Kapha dominance)
🔸Kaphaja Unmada (Insanity due to Kapha)
🔸Apasmara (Epilepsy)
🔸Medoroga (Obesity)
🔸Kushtha (Skin diseases)
🔸Prameha (Diabetes)
🔸Vridhi (Abscess/Tumor conditions)

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Children
🔸Elderly and very weak persons
🔸Pregnancy
🔸Rajonivritta (post-menopausal women)
🔸Garbhini (pregnant)
🔸Hridaya roga (heart diseases)
🔸Udara roga (ascites, hepatosplenomegaly)
🔸Atisara (diarrhea)
🔸Arsha (piles)
🔸Kshata/kshina (injury, emaciated persons)


📌PRECAUTIONS IN TREATMENT

🔸Should be done only after proper snehana & swedana.
🔸Conducted under empty stomach in morning.
🔸Proper observation of Shuddhi Lakshanas (adequate vomiting signs).
🔸Avoid over-administration to prevent complications.
🔸Post-therapy diet regimen (Samsarjana Krama) must be followed strictly.
🔸Patient should be under rest and observation for few days.

📌DEFINITION

🔸Rasāyana Chikitsā is a specialized Ayurvedic treatment aimed at rejuvenation, promoting longevity, enhancing immunity, improving intellect, and delaying aging through specific herbal formulations and regimens.

📌DRUGS USED

🔸Amalaki
🔸Haritaki
🔸Guduchi

🔸Ashwagandha
🔸Pippali
🔸Yashtimadhu
🔸Mandukaparni
🔸Brahmi
🔸Guggulu
🔸Triphala
🔸Chyawanprasha

📌PROCEDURE

1. Purification (Shodhana) if required before Rasayana intake.
2. Selection of Rasayana drug based on age, strength, season, and disease.
3. Drugs administered in proper dosage (churna, ghrita, leha, or avaleha form).
4. Patient advised to follow proper diet (Pathya ahara) and lifestyle (Dinacharya, Ritucharya).
5. Regular monitoring of digestion (Agni) and body response.
6. Treatment continued for a specified duration for rejuvenation effect.

🔸Kshaya (Emaciation)

🔸Unmada (Psychiatric disorders)
🔸Rajayakshma (Tuberculosis)
🔸Skin disorders (Kustha)
🔸General debility, Immunodeficiency conditions

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸During acute fever and infections
🔸Severe indigestion / Ama condition
🔸Persons with uncontrolled Kapha disorders (obesity, excessive mucus)
🔸During pregnancy (except specific advised rasayanas)
🔸Immediately after heavy meals or alcohol intake

📌PRECAUTIONS

🔸Strict Pathya-Apathya (dietary rules) to be followed.
🔸Avoid stress, exertion, and irregular lifestyle.
🔸Regular monitoring is essential for long-term administration.

🔺JALUKA AVACHARANAM / LEECH THERAPY 

📌DEFINITION

🔸Jalaukavacharaṇa is a type of Raktamokṣaṇa (bloodletting therapy) where leeches (jalauka) are used to remove vitiated blood from the body in a safe and controlled manner. It is especially recommended for delicate patients where sharp instruments cannot be used.

📌DRUGS USED

*Jalauka (Leech)
*Haridra
*Saindhava lavana
*Ghṛita
*Triphalā decoction

📌PROCEDURE

1. Poorva Karma (Preparation)
*Selection of non-poisonous, healthy leeches.
*Cleansing leech with turmeric water.
*Patient examination and area preparation.
2. Pradhana Karma (Main Procedure)
*Apply leech on the affected site.
*Allow it to attach and suck vitiated blood.
*Once it detaches or becomes sluggish, remove it carefully.
*Make the leech vomit ingested blood by applying turmeric or saindhava.
3. Paschat Karma (Post-Procedure)
*Apply haridra churna or ghṛita on the bite site.
*Bandaging if required.
*Observation for signs of infection or excessive bleeding.

📌Indicated Diseases

*Vatarakta
*Kushta (Skin diseases)
*Visarpa
*Vidradhi (Abscess)
*Netra rogas (Eye diseases)
*Granthi (Cyst/tumor)
*Dushta vrana (Non-healing ulcer)
*Pidaka (Boils)

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN(Contraindications)

*Ativata (excessive vata disorders)
*Pandu (Anemia)
*Karshya (emaciation)
*Arsha (hemorrhoids with bleeding)
*Garbhini (pregnant women)
*Bālaka (children)
*Vriddha (elderly)
*Raktapitta (bleeding disorders)

📌PRECAUTIONS

*Use only healthy, non-poisonous leeches.

🔺JALUKA AVACHARANAM / LEECH THERAPY 

📌DEFINITION

🔸Jalaukavacharaṇa is a type of Raktamokṣaṇa (bloodletting therapy) where leeches (jalauka) are used to remove vitiated blood from the body in a safe and controlled manner. It is especially recommended for delicate patients where sharp instruments cannot be used.

📌DRUGS USED

*Jalauka (Leech)
*Haridra
*Saindhava lavana
*Ghṛita
*Triphalā decoction

📌PROCEDURE

1. Poorva Karma (Preparation)
*Selection of non-poisonous, healthy leeches.
*Cleansing leech with turmeric water.
*Patient examination and area preparation.
2. Pradhana Karma (Main Procedure)
*Apply leech on the affected site.
*Allow it to attach and suck vitiated blood.
*Once it detaches or becomes sluggish, remove it carefully.
*Make the leech vomit ingested blood by applying turmeric or saindhava.
3. Paschat Karma (Post-Procedure)
*Apply haridra churna or ghṛita on the bite site.
*Bandaging if required.
*Observation for signs of infection or excessive bleeding.

📌Indicated Diseases

*Vatarakta
*Kushta (Skin diseases)
*Visarpa
*Vidradhi (Abscess)
*Netra rogas (Eye diseases)
*Granthi (Cyst/tumor)
*Dushta vrana (Non-healing ulcer)
*Pidaka (Boils)

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN(Contraindications)

*Ativata (excessive vata disorders)
*Pandu (Anemia)
*Karshya (emaciation)
*Arsha (hemorrhoids with bleeding)
*Garbhini (pregnant women)
*Bālaka (children)
*Vriddha (elderly)
*Raktapitta (bleeding disorders)

📌PRECAUTIONS

*Use only healthy, non-poisonous leeches.
*Ensure proper sterilization before and after application.
*Avoid in weak, malnourished, or anemic patients.
*Monitor patient for allergic reactions, excessive bleeding, or infection.
*Post-procedure wound care with haridra, ghṛita, or antiseptic.

🔺VALUKA SWEDHAM

📌DEFINITION

🔸Valuka Swedana is a type of Rūkṣa Sweda (dry fomentation) where heated sand (valuka) is used to induce sweating. It helps in reducing stiffness, swelling, and pain, particularly in conditions with kapha and meda predominance.

📌DRUG USED

🔸Valuka (Sand) – cleaned
and dried.

📌PROCEDURE

1. Sand Preparation – Clean sand is heated in a pan until sufficiently hot.
2. Packing – The heated sand is tied in a thick cloth to make a pottali (bolus).
3. Application – The hot sand bolus is gently applied over the affected part or whole body in rhythmic movements.
4. Reheating – When the bolus cools down, sand is reheated and reused.
5. Duration – Carried out for 15–30 minutes depending on the condition and patient’s tolerance.
 
📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Amavata (Rheumatoid arthritis)
🔸Sandhigata Vata (Osteoarthritis)
🔸Vatarakta (Gout)
🔸Katigraha (Low back pain)
🔸Urustambha (Thigh stiffness)
🔸Medoroga (Obesity)
🔸Kapha-vataja disorders with pain and stiffness

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Pitta pradhana vyadhis
🔸Raktapitta (bleeding disorders)
🔸Vrana (open wounds, ulcers)
🔸Twak vikara with burning sensation
🔸Dehydrated or weak patients
🔸Pregnancy
🔸Very young and very old

📌PRECAUTIONS

🔸Temperature of sand must be carefully checked to prevent burns.
🔸Should not be done in excessive weakness or dehydration.
🔸Avoid in fever, acute inflammation, or skin lesions.
🔸Patient’s comfort and tolerance should be monitored continuously.
🔸Stop immediately if patient experiences excessive burning, giddiness, or discomfort.

07/09/2025, 09:28 - +91 95446 87331: 🔺TREATMENT NO : 30
🔺GANDUSHA

📌DEFINITION

🔸Gandūṣha is an Ayurvedic oral therapy where the mouth is completely filled with medicated liquid (oil, decoction, or other formulations) and held for a prescribed period without movement, until signs of proper action appear. It is one among the Mukhachikitsa and an important part of Dinacharya.

📌DRUGS USED


🔸Taila (Sesame oil, Coconut oil, Mustard oil)
🔸Ghṛita
🔸Madhu
🔸Triphala kwatha
🔸Yashtimadhu kwatha
🔸Irimedadi taila
🔸Dantapala taila
🔸Dashamoola kwatha
🔸Saindhava lavana with water

📌PROCEDURE

1. Patient should sit comfortably in an upright posture.
2. Warm medicated liquid is prepared as per indication.
3. The mouth is completely filled with the liquid (without allowing movement inside).
4. Retain until mouth waters, eyes and nose start watering, or until unable to hold.
5. Spit out and rinse the mouth with warm water.
6. Repeat if prescribed.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Mukharoga (oral diseases)
🔸Dantashoola (toothache)
🔸Dantaharsha (sensitivity)
🔸Dantakshata (fractured tooth)
🔸Dantamalī (dirty teeth)
🔸Jihvaroga (tongue disorders)
🔸Kantharoga (throat disorders)
🔸Shiroroga (head diseases)
🔸Ardita (facial palsy)
🔸Mukhashosha (dryness of mouth)
🔸Trishna (excessive thirst)
🔸Krimi (oral worms/infections)

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Ati-balaheenata (extreme weakness)
🔸Ati-tarshita (excessive thirst, dehydration)
🔸Ati-matta (intoxicated state)
🔸Ati-kshudha (extreme hunger)
🔸Ati-tripta (just after heavy meals)
🔸Chardi (vomiting tendency)
🔸Jwara (fever, acute stage)
🔸Bala, Vriddha, Garbhini (in debilitated, very old, and pregnancy unless prescribed carefully)

📌PRECAUTIONS

🔸Medicine should not be too hot or too cold.
🔸Avoid swallowing the liquid.
🔸Quantity should be sufficient to fill the mouth.
🔸Patient should be in comfortable sitting posture.
🔸Perform under empty stomach or light stomach.
🔸Stop once signs of Samyak
Gandūṣha (salivation, watering of eyes/nose) appear.

🔺YONI LEPANAM

📌DEFINITION

🔸Yoni Lepana is an Ayurvedic local treatment in which medicated paste (Lepa) prepared from herbal drugs is applied externally over the Yoni (female genital region) for therapeutic purposes. It is mainly indicated in Stree Roga.

📌DRUGS USED

🔸Haridra
🔸Daruharidra
🔸Lodhra
🔸Musta
🔸Manjishta
🔸Triphala
🔸Kumari (Aloe vera)
🔸Nimba
🔸Chandana
🔸Yashtimadhu

📌PROCEDURE

1. Patient should lie in supine position after proper cleansing of Yoni with lukewarm water/decoction.
2. Herbal drugs are made into a paste with suitable liquid media (ghṛita, taila, decoction, or water).
3. The paste is applied evenly over the external Yoni region.
4. Retain for prescribed duration (until semi-dry or absorbed).
5. Wash with lukewarm water or prescribed decoction.
6. Repeat as per physician’s advice.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Yoni kanda
🔸Yoni shotha
🔸Yoni daha
🔸Yoni srava
🔸Yoni kandu
🔸Yoni vedana
🔸Yoni roga (general vulvo-vaginal disorders)

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸During menstruation
🔸During pregnancy (unless specially advised)
🔸Immediately after delivery (sutika kala)
🔸Severe acute infections with pus discharge
🔸Hypersensitivity to applied drugs
🔸Open wounds/ulcerated lesions in genital area

📌PRECAUTIONS

🔸Paste should not be too hot or too cold.
🔸Drugs must be freshly prepared and hygienically applied.
🔸Ensure proper cleansing before and after procedure.
🔸Avoid excessive rubbing or thick application causing discomfort.
🔸Perform under medical supervision in sensitive conditions.

🔺NETRA TARPANAM

📌DEFINITION

🔸Netra Tarpanam is an Ayurvedic local treatment for the eyes, where medicated ghee or oil is retained in a boundary (made with flour paste) around the eyes for a specific duration. It nourishes, strengthens, and protects the eyes.

📌DRUGS USED 

🔸Triphala ghṛita
🔸Mahatriphala ghṛita
🔸Jīvantyādi ghṛita
🔸Shatāvaryādi ghṛita
🔸Mahatiktaka ghṛita
🔸Go ghṛita (cow’s ghee)
🔸Patoladi ghṛita

📌PROCEDURE

1. Patient lies in a comfortable supine position in a quiet room.
2. A circular boundary is built around both eyes using paste of black gram flour (masha pindi).
3. Lukewarm medicated ghṛita is gently poured and retained over the eyes within the boundary.
4. Patient is instructed to keep eyes open and blink intermittently.
5. After prescribed time, ghṛita is removed and eyes are gently cleaned with cotton and warm water.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Netra shosha (dry eye)
🔸Netra daha (burning eyes)
🔸Netra abhishyanda (conjunctivitis)
🔸Timira (early cataract / refractive errors)
🔸Akshi shula (eye pain)
🔸Sandhigata roga of eye (eye strain)
🔸Pakshmashata (falling of eyelashes)
🔸Arjuna (corneal opacity)
🔸Netra klanti (eye fatigue)

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Acute eye infections with pus discharge
🔸Severe conjunctivitis (redness, swelling, pain)
🔸Recent eye surgery
🔸Glaucoma (unless specially prescribed)
🔸Injury/trauma to eye
🔸Fever, severe cold, cough, or acute systemic illness
🔸Children below 7 years without medical advice

📌PRECAUTIONS

🔸Ghṛita should be fresh, medicated, and lukewarm.
🔸Avoid very hot or very cold medicines.
🔸Maintain strict hygiene during procedure.
🔸Perform in a closed room, free from wind and dust.
🔸Patient should remain still and relaxed.
🔸After procedure, avoid exposure to bright light, wind, and screen use for a few hours.

🔺KAVALA GRAHANA

📌DEFINITION

🔸Kavala Grahaṇa is an Ayurvedic oral therapy in which medicated oil, ghee, or decoction is taken into the mouth in a smaller quantity (than Gandusha), moved around (gargled), and then spat out after a specific duration.

📌DRUGS USED

*Taila: Tila Taila, Eranda Taila, Narikela Taila
*Ghrita: Go Ghrita
*Kashaya: Triphala Kashaya, Yashtimadhu Kashaya, Musta Kashaya
*Others: Madhu, Usheera, Haridra

📌PROCEDURE

1. Select suitable medicine (oil, ghee, or decoction) based on disease and doshas.
2. Take a small quantity of the liquid (not filling the entire mouth).
3. Move it around gently in the mouth with the help of cheeks, tongue, and lips.
4. Continue until tears appear in eyes or nose discharges slightly (sign of proper time).
5. Spit out the liquid.
6. Wash mouth with lukewarm water.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Mukhapaka
🔸Danta Shoola
🔸Dantaharsha
🔸Dantasharkara
🔸Ardita
🔸Mukha Roga (general)
🔸Jihwa Shosha
🔸Kantha Roga

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Ati Bala (very weak person)
🔸Ati Kshudha (excessive hunger)
🔸Ati Trishna (severe thirst)
🔸Atisheetala (excessive cold exposure)
🔸Immediately after Vamana or Virechana

📌PRECAUTIONS IN TREATMENT

🔸Medicine should not be too hot or too cold.
🔸Avoid swallowing the liquid.
🔸Duration should not be too short or too prolonged.
🔸Choose medicine according to dosha predominance.
🔸Perform in a calm environment, preferably in the morning.

🔺APRAJATA (INFERTILITY)

🔺NIDANAM 
(Etiology / Causes)

*According to Ayurveda, causes are:
*Bīja doṣa – Defects in ovum (śoṇita) and sperm (śukra)
*Kṣetra doṣa – Uterine abnormalities
*Rtu doṣa – Improper timing of intercourse
*Āhāra vihāra – Unwholesome food, excessive exercise, stress
*Manasika hetu – Anxiety, fear, depression
*Doṣa prakopa – Vitiation of Vāta (mainly Apāna vāyu), Pitta and Kapha
*Reference: Charaka Saṃhitā, Sūtrasthāna 30/26-27; Suśruta Saṃhitā, Śārīrasthāna 2/46

🔺PURVARUPAM 
(Premonitory Symptoms)

*Ārtava doṣa (irregular, scanty, painful, or absent menstruation)
*Śukra doṣa (thin, frothy, less in quantity, foul smell)
*Yonigata vikāra (discharge, itching, pain, dryness)
*Daurbalya, kṣaya lakṣaṇas (weakness, weight loss, fatigue)



🔺LAKSANAM 
 (Clinical Features)

*Inability to conceive after regular intercourse
*Repeated pregnancy loss
*Menstrual irregularities (oligomenorrhea, amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea)
*Sexual dysfunction in male/female
*Features of aggravated doṣa (vāta prakopa → dryness, irregularity; kapha prakopa → obstruction, heaviness; pitta prakopa → burning, bleeding disorders)


🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*Build, nutrition, BMI (obesity/underweight may affect fertility).
*Secondary sexual characters (breast development, pubic/axillary hair, voice).
*Thyroid swelling (hypo/hyperthyroidism).
*Hirsutism/acne (suggests PCOS, hyperandrogenism).
*Pallor (anemia), edema (renal/hepatic/endocrine disorder).
*Signs of chronic illness (TB, diabetes, autoimmune).

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION


*Cardiovascular system – rule out hypertension, heart disease affecting pregnancy.
*Respiratory system – chronic illness (TB, asthma).
*Abdomen – organomegaly, masses, tenderness, pelvic pathology.
*Pelvic examination – uterine size, shape, position, adnexal masses, cervical changes.
*Breast examination – galactorrhea (hyperprolactinemia).

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*For Female Partner
*Basic Blood Tests
*CBC (anemia, infection).
*FBS, HbA1c (diabetes).
*Thyroid profile (TSH, T3, T4).
*Serum prolactin.
*Serum FSH, LH, AMH (ovarian reserve).
*Serum progesterone (luteal phase).
*Serum estradiol, testosterone (hormonal balance).
*Imaging
*Transvaginal ultrasound (uterus, ovaries, PCOS, fibroids, endometrial thickness).
*HSG (Hysterosalpingography) – tubal patency.
*Sonohysterography / Hysteroscopy / Laparoscopy (if indicated).
** Other Tests
*TORCH test (if recurrent pregnancy loss).
*Endometrial biopsy (if endometrial factor suspected).
*For Male Partner
*Semen analysis (count, motility, morphology).
*Serum testosterone, FSH, LH, prolactin.
*Scrotal USG (varicocele, obstruction).
*Genetic testing (Klinefelter, Y-chromosome microdeletions if azoospermia).

🔸Hing

🔸Monitor for side effects like excessive bleeding.
🔸Combine with proper diet, lifestyle, and mental health support.
