🔺 VARNYA LEPA

📌DEFINITION

🔸Varnya Lepa Chikitsā is an external Ayurvedic treatment where herbal paste (Lepa) made of Varnya dravyas (complexion-enhancing herbs) is applied to the skin to improve varṇa (complexion), tvak-prasādana (skin glow), and reduce skin blemishes. It is a type of Twak Chikitsā under Kushta and Soundarya Chikitsā.

📌DRUGS USED 

🔸Chandana
🔸Usheera
🔸Padmaka
🔸Manjishta
🔸Lodhra
🔸Haridra
🔸Daruharidra
🔸Yashtimadhu
🔸Kumkuma (Saffron)
🔸Nimba
🔸Triphala

📌PROCEDURE

1. Cleanse the face/skin with lukewarm water or decoction.
2. Prepare a fine paste of selected Varnya dravyas using suitable liquid media (rose water, milk, honey, ghṛita, etc.).
3. Apply evenly over the affected area or face in an upward and outward direction.
4. Retain until it becomes semi-dry.
5. Wash gently with lukewarm water.
6. Repeat as per physician’s advice (daily or periodically).

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Vyanga (melasma, pigmentation)
🔸Nilika (dark circles)
🔸Pama (eczema)
🔸Kustha (skin disorders)
🔸Mukhadushika (acne, pimples)
🔸Twak vaivarnya (discoloration of skin)

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Hypersensitivity or allergy to applied herbs
🔸Open wounds, cuts, or oozing skin lesions
🔸Severe inflammatory skin disorders (acute stage)
🔸Very dry, cracked skin (unless medicated ghṛita/taila base is used)
🔸During exposure to dust, heat, or sun immediately after application

📌PRECAUTIONS

🔸Always test the paste on a small area before full application.
🔸Use freshly prepared paste each time.
🔸Avoid applying very thick or very thin layers.
🔸Do not keep the lepa for excessive time (remove after semi-dry stage).
🔸Apply in a clean, calm environment free from dust and heat.
🔸Follow pathya (dietary advice) supportive for skin health (avoid excess spicy, oily, sour foods).

11/09/2025, 14:20 - +91 95446 87331: 🔺TREATMENT NO : 36
🔺GREEVA VASTHI

📌DEFINITION

🔸Greeva Vasti is an external Snehana–Swedana procedure in which warm medicated oil is retained in a specially prepared reservoir over the cervical (neck) region for a specific duration to relieve pain and stiffness.

📌DRUGS USED

🔸Dhanvantaram Taila
🔸Ksheerabala Taila
🔸Sahacharadi Taila
🔸Mahanarayana Taila
🔸Prabhanjana Vimardana Taila

📌 PROCEDURE

🔸 The patient is made to lie in prone position.
🔸The cervical region (Greeva pradesha) is cleaned and massaged lightly.
🔸A leak-proof circular boundary is prepared with black gram paste (Masha pindi) or wheat flour dough.
🔸 Warm medicated oil is poured into this reservoir and maintained at a tolerable temperature.
🔸 Oil is retained for 30–40 minutes, reheated/replaced as required.
🔸After the procedure, oil is removed, the area is gently massaged, and mild swedana (fomentation) is given.


📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Greeva Sthambha
🔸Greeva Graha
🔸Manyasthambha
🔸Cervical spondylosis
🔸Cervical myelopathy
🔸Neck pain due to Vata disorders
🔸Muscle spasm / stiffness in neck

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Open wounds, infections, or skin diseases in neck region
🔸Acute fever
🔸Acute inflammation and abscess in cervical area
🔸Severe hypotension
🔸Uncontrolled diabetes
🔸During pregnancy (over neck heating contraindicated in sensitive cases)

📌PRECAUTIONS

🔸Oil temperature should be tolerable, not too hot.
🔸Proper sealing of dough to prevent leakage.
🔸Patient should not move during procedure.
🔸Conduct in calm environment to avoid strain.
🔸Monitor for dizziness, excessive sweating, or discomfort.
🔸Use sterile and fresh oil each time.

📌DEFINITION

🔸Vajikaraṇam is one of the Aṣṭa Cikitsās (eight branches of Ayurveda).

🔸Dosage and drug selection must be individualized.
🔸Avoid excessive sexual indulgence during therapy.
🔸Maintain Pathya–Apathya (dietary rules).
🔸Should be done under expert supervision to prevent side effects.

🔺AGNIKARMA

📌DEFINITION

🔸Agnikarma is a para-surgical procedure in Ayurveda where therapeutic burns are made using heated instruments (like metals, sticks, or other substances) for the management of diseases not easily curable by medicines or surgery.

📌DRUGS/MATERIALS USED

🔸Loha (Iron)
🔸Tamra (Copper)
🔸Shankha (Conch)
🔸Panchaloha (Five-metal alloy)
🔸Pippali (Long pepper)
🔸Godanta (Gypsum)
🔸Ajashakrit (Goat excreta)
🔸Guda (Jaggery)
🔸Honey

📌PROCEDURE

1. Preparation: Patient and affected site cleaned; area marked.
2. Heating: Selected instrument/material heated to red-hot.
3. Application: Applied directly or indirectly on the diseased part in different patterns (Bindu, Valaya, Vilekha, etc.).
4. Aftercare: Ghrita, Madhu, or cooling pastes applied to reduce burning and promote healing.
5. Follow-up: Proper wound care and diet regimen advised.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Arsha (Piles)
🔸Bhagandara (Fistula-in-ano)
🔸Arbuda (Tumor)
🔸Granthi (Cyst/Swelling)
🔸Arbudaja shotha (Hard inflammation)
🔸Charma kilaka (Warts)
🔸Mashaka (Corn/Callosity)
🔸Nadivrana (Sinus)
🔸Vicharchika (Eczema, resistant type)
🔸Sandhigata Vata (Osteoarthritis pain)
🔸Gridhrasi (Sciatica)

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Bala (Children)
🔸Vriddha (Elderly)
🔸Atishuska (Very emaciated)
🔸Bhiru (Fearful, weak-minded)
🔸Garbhini (Pregnant women)
🔸Those with bleeding/clotting disorders

📌PRECAUTIONS IN TREATMENT

🔸Proper sterilization and heating of instruments.
🔸Avoid excessive burning or deep tissue damage.
🔸Cooling agents (Ghrita, Madhu) should be kept ready.
🔸Not to be performed in vital areas (Marma).
🔸Patient should be monitored for pain, blistering, or infection.

17/09/2025, 11:38 - +91 95446 87331: 🔺TREATMENT NO :45
🔺KSHARA KARMA

📌DEFINITION

🔸Kshara Karma is a para-surgical procedure in Ayurveda where an alkaline preparation (Kṣhāra) is applied locally to destroy, excise, or cauterize unhealthy tissue. It is considered a minimally invasive procedure for various surgical diseases.

📌DRUGS USED

🔸Apāmārga Kṣhāra
🔸Aragvadha Kṣhāra
🔸Palāśa Kṣhāra
🔸Snuhi Kṣhāra
🔸Yava Kṣhāra
🔸Kutaja Kṣhāra

📌PROCEDURE

1. Preparation of the patient – cleaning and local anesthesia (if needed).
2. Application of Kṣhāra – applied directly over the diseased part with a probe or stick.
3. Observation – left in place for a stipulated time (until the tissue attains the desired color change).
4. Neutralization – washing with sour liquids (e.g., lemon juice, buttermilk, kanji) to stop further action.
5. Post-care – wound management with ghṛita/oil dressings.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Arsas(Piles)
🔸Bhagandara (Fistula-in-ano)
🔸Arbuda (Benign growths/tumors)
🔸Charma Keela (Warts)
🔸Nadi Vrana (Sinus)
🔸Dushta Vrana (Non-healing ulcer)
🔸Kilasa (Leukoderma – external application in some contexts)

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Snigdha Deha (very fatty individuals )
🔸Ati-krisha (very lean/debilitated persons)
🔸Mrdu Koshta (sensitive bowel)
🔸Raktapitta (bleeding disorders)
🔸Garbhini (pregnancy)
🔸Bala, Vriddha (children, elderly, weak patients)
🔸Persons with uncontrolled diabetes

📌PRECAUTIONS IN TREATMENT

🔸Strictly avoid excessive duration of Kṣhāra contact (can cause necrosis).
🔸Always neutralize with acidic medium after use.
🔸Ensure sterile preparation and application.
🔸Assess the strength of Kṣhāra according to disease severity (Mridu, Madhyama, Tikshna Kṣhāra).
🔸Regular wound dressing with soothing agents post-application.
🔸Monitor for pain, burning, and secondary infection.

🔺GARBHASTHAPAKA 
CHIKITSA 

📌DEFINITION

🔸Garbhasthāpaka Chikitsā refers to the treatment and therapeutic measures aimed at supporting conception and maintaining pregnancy, preventing recurrent abortions, and stabilizing the foetus in the womb.

📌DRUGS USED

🔸Ashoka (Saraca asoca)
🔸Lodhra (Symplocos racemosa)
🔸Shatavari (Asparagus racemosus)
🔸Yashtimadhu (Glycyrrhiza glabra)
🔸Amalaki (Emblica officinalis)
🔸Bala (Sida cordifolia)
🔸Nagakeshara (Mesua ferrea)
🔸Musta (Cyperus rotundus)
🔸Guduchi (Tinospora cordifolia)
🔸Kushtha (Saussurea lappa)

📌PROCEDURE

🔸Administration of Garbhasthāpaka dravyas in the form of:
🔸Kashaya (decoction)
🔸Phanta (infusion)
🔸Churna (powder with milk/ghee)
🔸Ghrita / Taila preparations
🔸Following Pathya (wholesome diet and regimen supportive of pregnancy).
🔸Avoiding Apathya (activities or food that disturb Vata-Pitta and can harm foetus).
🔸Use of Snehana (oleation) and Mridu Upakrama to keep Vata in balance.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Garbhapata (Recurrent miscarriage)
🔸Garbhasrava (Threatened abortion)
🔸Garbha vyapad (Complications of pregnancy)
🔸Vandhyatva (Infertility – supportive role)

📌 MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Mṛtagarbha (dead foetus in womb)
🔸Garbha vyapad with severe complications (like congenital anomalies incompatible with life)
🔸When surgical/modern obstetric intervention is urgently required
🔸Pitta-prakopa or Aama conditions (until corrected)

📌 PRECAUTIONS IN TREATMENT

🔸Avoid strong Shodhana (panchakarma) during pregnancy.
🔸Careful dose adjustment to avoid uterine stimulation.
🔸Only Mridu (mild) drugs should be used.
🔸Strict avoidance of Apathya ahara-vihara (e.g., heavy exercise, fasting, spicy foods).
🔸Treatment must be done under close observation of both mother’s and foetus’s condition.

🔺DHANYAMLA DHARA

📌DEFINITION

Dhanyamla Dhara is a type of Parisheka therapy where Dhānyāmla (fermented liquid prepared from cereals) is continuously poured in a stream over the affected part or whole body for a specific time. It is mainly used in Kapha-Vāta disorders.


📌DRUGS USED 

🔸Rice
🔸Horse gram (Kulatha)
🔸Navadhanya (different cereals)
🔸Citrus fruits (Nimbu, Tamarind)
🔸Dry ginger (Shunthi)
🔸Chilies (Maricha)
🔸Other sour substances

📌PROCEDURE

1. Prepare Dhānyāmla by fermenting cereals and sour substances for a few days.
2. Warm the liquid to a tolerable temperature.
3. Patient is made to lie on the table (Droni).
4. Dhānyāmla is poured in a continuous stream over the whole body or affected part for 30–45 minutes.
5. After completion, body is wiped and patient is allowed to rest.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Rheumatoid arthritis (Amavata)
🔸Osteoarthritis (Sandhivata)
🔸Sciatica (Gridhrasi)
🔸Obesity (Sthoulya)
🔸Hemiplegia (Pakshaghata)
🔸Parkinsonism (Kampavata)
🔸Skin diseases (Kustha)


📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Severe debility
🔸Fever with Pitta predominance
🔸Open wounds or ulcers
🔸Extreme emaciation
🔸Pregnancy
🔸Severe anemia

📌PRECAUTIONS

🔸Maintain proper temperature of liquid (lukewarm, not too hot).
🔸Avoid exposure to cold after therapy.
🔸Monitor patient for excessive fatigue or discomfort.
🔸Use freshly prepared, properly fermented Dhānyāmla.
🔸Duration and frequency should be decided as per strength of patient (Rogi Bala) and disease condition.

🔺SIRA VYADHANAM

📌DEFINITION

🔸Sira Vyadhanam is a para-surgical procedure described in Ayurveda where bloodletting is done by puncturing or incising a vein (sira) to expel vitiated blood (dushta rakta). It is considered the most effective among all Raktamokshana procedures.

📌DRUGS USED

🔸Haridra
🔸Nimba
🔸Jati
🔸Aragvadha
🔸Guduchi
🔸Triphala
🔸(These are mainly used for purification, dressing and healing after the procedure rather than during incision.)

📌PROCEDURE

1. Poorva karma (pre-procedure):
🔸Selection of patient and site.
🔸Snehana (oleation) and Swedana (fomentation).
🔸Preparation of sterile instruments.
2. Pradhana karma (main procedure):
🔸Patient positioned comfortably.
🔸Identification of vein (sira).
🔸Incision/puncture made with appropriate sharp instrument.
🔸Blood allowed to flow till signs of samyak raktamokshana (proper elimination).
3. Paschat karma (post-procedure):
🔸Acharya advised to stop blood flow by pressure, bandaging, and application of drugs like Haridra, Triphala, Nimba.
🔸Light diet and rest recommended.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Vatarakta
🔸Gridhrasi (sciatica)
🔸Visarpa
🔸Kushta (skin disorders)
🔸Netra roga (eye diseases)
🔸Arsha (piles)
🔸Vidradhi (abscess)
🔸Gout
🔸Dandaka roga (stiffness disorders)
🔸Manya stambha (cervical spondylosis)

📌Must Be Avoided In

🔸Bala (children)
🔸Vriddha (elderly)
🔸Garbhini (pregnant women)
🔸Kshata (trauma patients)
🔸Pandu (anemia)
🔸Ksheena (emaciated)
🔸Atisara (diarrhea)
🔸Jwara (fever)
🔸Severe dehydration


🔺PRECAUTIONS IN TREATMENT

🔸Proper patient selection is essential.
🔸Avoid excessive bloodletting (can cause shock, murcha, or death).
🔸Use sterilized instruments and drugs.
🔸Ensure proper hemostasis and wound care.
🔸Monitor for signs of complications like dizziness, fainting, or excessive bleeding.

7. Neonatal meningitis
8. Birth trauma-related complications

🔺SAMPRAPTI (Pathogenesis)

1. Vitiation of Vāta, Pitta, Kapha due to improper sutika shiksha.
2. Rakta & Mamsa dhatu dusti → systemic manifestations.
3. Leads to weakness, fever, irritability, skin eruptions in neonates.

🔺ANUPASAYA

*Cold, unhygienic environment

*Exposure to infections

*Nimba, Haridra, Triphala taila for minor skin infections
*Lepanam / local applications for pustules
*Monitor fever, hydration, and systemic signs for timely intervention

🔺AJAGALLIKA 

🔺NIDANAM 
(Etiology / Causative factors)

*Caused by vitiation of Kapha and Rakta along with obstruction of Vāta.
*Unwholesome diet and lifestyle that increase Kapha (guru, snigdha, sheetala āhāra), excessive intake of curd, fish, incompatible food.
*Local trauma, unhygienic practices.
*(Ref: Suśruta Saṃhitā – Nidanasthāna, Kushta & Granthi contexts, Madhava Nidāna, Adhyāya on Granthi)

🔺PURVAROOPAM (Prodromal symptoms)

*Localised kandu (itching)
*Slight śotha (swelling)
*Sūkṣma vedanā (mild pain)
*Raga mandala (slight reddish patches)

🔺LAKSANAM 
 (Clinical features)

*Śotha – localized rounded swelling
*Ruk / Toda – pain, pricking type
*dāha – burning sensation
*Śyāva–rakta varṇa (blackish-red discoloration)
*Indurated and firm swelling, difficult to move.
*Suppuration may occur later.
*(Ref: Suśruta – Nidāna & Cikitsā sthāna; Madhava Nidāna – Granthi)

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*Built, nourishment, hydration status
*Temperature (fever)
*Pulse rate (tachycardia if fever present)
*Blood pressure
*Respiratory rate
*General appearance: malaise, fatigue, facial swelling
*Lymph node examination (submandibular, pre-auricular)

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

1. Local (Head & Neck) Examination
*Inspection:
*Unilateral or bilateral parotid swelling (below and in front of ear)
*Swelling extends from angle of mandible to mastoid region
*Overlying skin: stretched, shiny, not inflamed initially
*Palpation:
*Tender, firm swelling
*Hotness may be present in acute stage
*No fluctuation (unless suppuration occurs)
*Mouth:
*Redness/swelling at parotid duct opening
*Pain while chewing or swallowing sour foods
2. Other Systems (for complications)
*Abdomen: check for tenderness (pancreatitis, orchitis)
*Genital examination (orchitis in males)
*CNS examination (rule out meningitis/encephalitis in severe cases)

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*CBC: mild leukopenia with relative lymphocytosis
*Serum amylase: elevated (due to salivary gland inflammation)
*LFT: to rule out hepatitis (rare complication)
*Urine amylase: may be increased
*Mumps IgM antibody (ELISA) – diagnostic test
*PCR for mumps virus RNA (where available)

🔺CHEDHANA KARMA

📌DEFINITION

🔸Chedhana Karma is one of the Śaṣṭi Upakrama (60 measures for wound management), defined as the surgical procedure of incising or excising unwanted/abnormal tissues such as abscesses, cysts, or overgrowths, to allow drainage or removal.

📌DRUGS USED

🔸Haridra
🔸Nimba
🔸Triphala
🔸Daruharidra
🔸Lodhra
🔸Yashtimadhu
🔸Honey (Madhu)
🔸Ghee (Ghrita)
(mainly for cleansing, healing, dressing after incision)

📌PROCEDURE

1. Poorva Karma (Preparation):
🔸Patient examination, consent, cleansing of area, local or systemic snehana–swedana if required.
2. Pradhana Karma (Main procedure):
🔸Sterilize area → make incision with sharp instrument (scalpel/ancient shastra).
🔸Allow pus/blood/discharge to drain.
🔸Remove necrosed or abnormal tissue if present.
3. Paschat Karma (Aftercare):
🔸Wash wound with antiseptic decoction (Triphala Kashaya, Nimba Kashaya).
🔸Apply Vrana Ropana drugs (Haridra, Madhu, Ghrita, Lodhra).
🔸Bandaging and regular dressing.
🔸Shodhana and Ropana therapy as per need.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Vidradhi (Abscess)
🔸Bhagandara (Fistula-in-ano)
🔸Arsha (Hemorrhoids – external excision type)
🔸Arbuda (Tumor)
🔸Granthi (Cyst/Benign swelling)
🔸Vrana with pus collection
🔸Dushta Vrana (Non-healing ulcer)

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Atisthoola (Obese) and Ati-krisha (very weak) patients
🔸Bala (children), Vriddha (elderly), and Garbhini (pregnant women)
🔸Bleeding disorders (Raktapitta, hemophilia-like conditions)
🔸Severe debility, cachexia
🔸Patients unfit for surgery (cardiorespiratory weakness, uncontrolled diabetes, etc.)

📌PRECAUTIONS

🔸Strict aseptic measures during incision
🔸Ensure proper hemostasis after procedure
🔸Avoid injury to vital structures (nerves, vessels)
🔸Post-operative care with Shodhana-Ropana drugs
🔸Regular dressing and observation for infection
🔸Proper dietary regimen (Pathya–Apathya) for wound healing

🔺UTTPHULLIKA (उत्फुल्लिका)

🔺NIDANAM 
(Etiology / Causative factors)

*(As per Charaka, Suśruta, Madhava Nidāna) – General Nidāna of Kuṣṭha applicable:
*Viruddhāhāra sevana (incompatible foods)
*Guru, snigdha, ati-madhura, dadhi sevana
*Matsya–dugdha sevana
*Divāsvapna
*Asatmya sevana
*Abhyavahāra of navanna, adhyashana
*Beejadoṣa (genetic predisposition)

🔺PURVARUPAM 
(Premonitory features)

*Kandu (itching)
*Toda (pricking pain)
*Daha (burning sensation)
*Varṇa vaivarnyata (discoloration)
*Slight raised eruption (pre-stage of papules/lesions)

🔺LAKSANAM 
 (Clinical features)

*Charaka & Suśruta:
*Small, red, round eruptions, slightly elevated
*Pidaka rūpa (looks like small pustules)
*Painful, burning sensation
*Gradually enlarges
*Mostly localized but can spread
*Madhava Nidāna: resembles pidaka, with kṛṣṇa-rakta varṇa, surrounded with burning and pain


🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*Vital signs: Temperature, pulse, BP, respiration
*Pallor, icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, lymphadenopathy, edema
*General health status and nutritional condition

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Skin:
*Localized swelling, redness, tenderness, central suppuration (pustule/pointing abscess)
*Surrounding cellulitis
*Number, size, distribution of lesions
*Lymph nodes: Regional lymphadenitis
*Other systems: Respiratory, cardiovascular, GIT, CNS – usually normal, but assessed for systemic spread (sepsis)

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*CBC: Leukocytosis, neutrophilia (suggesting acute infection)
*Blood sugar: To rule out diabetes (predisposing factor)
*Culture & sensitivity (pus swab): To identify organism (commonly Staphylococcus aureus) and antibiotic sensitivity
*Urine routine & blood tests: If recurrent boils → screen for diabetes or immunodeficiency
*ESR/CRP: Raised in infection/inflammation

🔺PURVARUPAM 
 (Prodromal Symptoms)

*Kṣudra vedanā in udara
*Daurbalya, ālasya
*Bāla garbha–chala–anubhava (feeling of abnormal foetal movement)

🔺LAKSANAM
 (Clinical Features)

*Gārbhikā suffers from severe kukṣi–śūla (abdominal pain)
*Ati–pravṛtti of vāyu, leading to āṭopa (distension)
*Foetus gets compressed / abnormal presentation
*Difficulty in prasava
*Reference: Caraka Saṃhitā, Cikitsāsthāna 30 (Yonivyapad Cikitsā); Mādhava Nidāna, Yonivyapad Nidanam

*Respiratory system – breath sounds, tachypnea (if anemic or in shock)
*Abdominal examination
*Fundal height vs. gestational age
*Fetal heart rate & activity
*Uterine tenderness (suggestive of abruption)
*Abdominal girth
*Per speculum & per vaginal examination (only if indicated and safe)
*Source of bleeding
*Status of cervix (open/closed, dilatation, effacement)
*Any local lesions (cervical polyp, carcinoma)

🔺 LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*Coagulation profile – PT, aPTT, INR, fibrinogen

*Urine analysis – proteinuria, infection
*Ultrasound (USG Abdomen + Pelvis / Obstetric scan)
*placental location & abnormalities
*Retroplacental clot
*Fetal viability & growth parameters
*Amniotic fluid volume
*Doppler studies – uteroplacental blood flow
*Kleihauer–Betke test (if fetomaternal hemorrhage suspected)

🔺KARNA BHEDHANAM

📌DEFINITION

🔸Karna Bhedanam is the Ayurvedic procedure of piercing the earlobes, usually performed in children, considered both a samskara (purificatory ritual) and a preventive measure for certain diseases

📌DRUGS USED 
(only names)

🔸Haridra
🔸Yashtimadhu
🔸Saindhava Lavana
🔸Ghee
🔸Taila (e.g., Tila taila, Eranda taila)
🔸Madhu

📌PROCEDURE

1. Purvakarma – Selection of appropriate time (6th–7th month for boys, 5th–6th year for girls), cleansing of the ear with antiseptic herbal decoction.
2. Sthanika Shodhana – Cleaning ear lobes with Haridra, Saindhava, and Ghrita.
3. Marmasthana Pariksha – Marking the correct point for piercing, avoiding marma siras.
4. Karma – Piercing ear lobes with sterilized needle or wire.
5. Paschatkarma – Application of medicated ghee/oil, insertion of thread or small wire to keep the hole patent, regular dressing with Haridra and ghee.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Apasmara
🔸Apatanaka
🔸Arsha
🔸Pleeha roga
🔸Krimi roga
🔸Dantavikaras

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Very weak or malnourished children
🔸Children suffering from fever, diarrhea, cough, cold
🔸During teething period
🔸In children with congenital ear deformities

📌PRECAUTIONS IN TREATMENT

🔸Avoid piercing on marmasthana (vital spots).
🔸Perform only in Shubha Muhurta (auspicious time) with proper sterilization.
🔸Ensure the child is healthy and not suffering from acute illness.
🔸Post-piercing care with Haridra + Ghrita to prevent infection.
🔸Monitor for swelling, pain, pus discharge and manage promptly

*Temperature: fever may be present

🔺 Systemic Examination

*CNS – hyperexcitability, hydrophobia, aerophobia, spasms of pharyngeal/laryngeal muscles, agitation, paralysis (in paralytic rabies)

*Cardiovascular system – tachycardia, arrhythmias, hypertension/hypotension in later stage
*GIT – nausea, vomiting, dysphagia
*Musculoskeletal system – painful spasms, stiffness, weakness progressing to paralysis

*CBC (leukocytosis)
*LFT, RFT (to assess systemic condition)
*Electrolytes (to correct imbalances)
*Specific for Rabies –
*Direct Fluorescent Antibody Test (dFA) on skin biopsy (gold standard)
*RT-PCR (saliva, CSF, skin, corneal impression)
*Rabies virus neutralizing antibody (RVNA) test
*Histopathology (post-mortem) – Negri bodies in brain tissue

🔺ACHARYA RASYANAM 

📌DEFINITION

🔸Ācārya Rasāyanam is the special rejuvenation therapy achieved through ācāra (code of conduct, good behavior, discipline, righteous living). It is a non-drug Rasāyana, emphasizing ethical, moral, and spiritual practices to promote longevity, memory, health, and mental clarity.

📌DRUGS USED

🔸No specific drugs are prescribed – it is a behavioral Rasāyana.

📌PROCEDURE

🔸Practicing truthfulness (satya).
🔸Avoiding anger, alcohol, and violence.
🔸Following celibacy or controlled sexual conduct.
🔸Respecting teachers, elders, and learned persons.
🔸Practicing compassion, non-violence (ahiṃsā), and mental discipline.
🔸Maintaining cleanliness, self-control, and balanced lifestyle.
🔸Chanting, meditation, and regular study of sacred texts.
🔸Engaging in social harmony and righteous deeds.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Acharya Rasāyanam is not targeted for a single disease but is beneficial in prevention and management of:
🔸Stress disorders
🔸Anxiety
🔸Depression
🔸Psychosomatic disorders
🔸Memory impairment
🔸Neurodegenerative conditions

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Persons unwilling or unable to follow ethical and disciplined lifestyle.
🔸Individuals with indulgence in excessive alcohol, anger, or violence.
🔸Patients seeking immediate curative effects (since it is preventive/promotive, not acute curative).

📌PRECAUTIONS

🔸Should be practiced under guidance of a teacher/Ācārya.
🔸Must be continued consistently; irregular practice reduces benefits.
🔸Should be combined with sattvic āhāra and proper daily regimen (dinacharya).
🔸Avoid hypocrisy – practices must be genuine, not superficial.

🔺KUPIPAKVA RASAYANAM 

📌DEFINITION

🔸Kupipākva Rasāyanam is a method of preparing metallic and mineral formulations by heating ingredients in a glass bottle (Kupi) sealed with mud-smeared cloth layers, placed in a sand bath (Valuka Yantra), under regulated fire (Mṛdu, Madhyama, Tivra Agni) until the desired Bhasma or Rasāyana is formed.


📌PROCEDURE

1. Selection of drugs – Mercury, Gandhaka (sulphur), Abhraka, Lohā, Tamra, etc. depending on the formulation.
2. Shodhana (purification) of metals, minerals, Gandhaka, and other ingredients.
3. Mardana (trituration) – All purified drugs are triturated with herbal juices or decoctions.
4. Filling in Kupi (glass bottle) – The prepared mixture is filled inside a special Kanthastha Kupi.
5. Sealing of Kupi – The mouth is closed with seven layers of cloth smeared with mud (Mud-smeared cloth = mrittikā lepana).
6. Heating in Valuka Yantra
🔸Mṛdu Agni (mild heat) – For initial drying and melting.
🔸Madhyama Agni (moderate heat) – For proper chemical reactions.
🔸Tīvra Agni (strong heat) – To complete sublimation and Rasāyana formation.
7. Cooling & breaking of Kupi – After proper heating and self-cooling, the bottle is carefully broken to collect the medicine.
8. Collection of Rasāyana
🔸Kupipakva Rasāyana is found deposited at the bottom (Tāla Pakva), middle (Madhya Bhāga), or neck (Kanthastha).
🔸Ex: Ras Sindhura (neck portion), Makaradhwaja (bottom portion).

🔸Examples of Kupipākva Rasāyana
🔸Ras Sindhura
🔸Makaradhwaja
🔸Rasendrasindhura
🔸Poornachandrodaya Makara Dhwaja

📌INDICATIONS

🔸Used in:
🔸Rasāyana (rejuvenation, longevity)
🔸Vrishya (aphrodisiac)
🔸Jīvanīya (vitality promoting)
🔸Treatment of fevers, respiratory disorders, neurological disorders, sexual debility, general weakness, etc. (depends on formulation).

📌PRECAUTIONS

🔸Strictly requires expert Rasavaidya supervision.
🔸Wrong preparation may lead to toxic effects.
🔸Only purified (Shodhita) metals & minerals must be used.
🔸Proper heating schedule (Agni pāka) must be maintained.

🔺NIRUHA BASTHI

📌DEFINITION

*Nirūha Basti (Āsthāpana Basti) is a therapeutic enema where a decoction (kashaya) mixed with honey, oil, rock salt, and paste of medicinal drugs is administered through the rectal route to expel morbid doshas, mainly Vāta.

📌DRUGS USED

*Madhu (Honey)
*Saindhava (Rock salt)
*Sneha dravya (Taila/Ghṛita)
*Kalka dravya (e.g., Madhanaphala, Pippali, Shunthi, Yavakshara, Yashtimadhu etc.)
*Kashaya dravya (Dashamoola, Punarnava, Musta, Bala, Eranda, etc.)

📌PROCEDURE

1. Purva Karma – Preparation with snehana (oleation) and swedana (sudation).
2. Pradhana Karma –
*The patient lies on the left lateral position.
*The prepared basti dravya is introduced into the rectum using basti yantra.
*The medicine should be retained for a certain period and then expelled naturally.
3. Paschat Karma – After evacuation, light diet, rest, and suitable pathya-apathya are advised.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

*Pakshaghata (Paralysis)
*Gridhrasi (Sciatica)
*Katishoola (Low back pain)
*Amavata (Rheumatoid arthritis)
*Gulma (Abdominal lump)
*Udara roga (Ascites, abdominal disorders)
*Arsha (Piles)
*Asthigata vata (Osteoarthritis)
*Mutrakricchra (Urinary disorders)
*Kushtha (Skin diseases)

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

*Ati-balaheenata (Extreme weakness)
*Ati-bala (Very strong persons immediately after meals
*Mandagni (Severe indigestion)
*Ajirna (Undigested food)
*Atisara (Diarrhea)
*Pravahika (Dysentery)
*Rajonivritta sthri (Immediately after menstruation)
*Garbhini (Pregnant women)
*Bhrashta garbha (Post miscarriage or abortion)
*Bala (Children below suitable age without indication)
*Vriddha (Very old with extreme weakness)

📌PRECAUTIONS

*Medicine should be freshly prepared and used lukewarm.
*Proper anupana (dietary regimen) before and after treatment must be followed.
*Dosage, drugs, and timing should be strictly individualized.
*Patient should rest in a comfortable position, avoiding strain.
*Contraindicated conditions must be ruled out before administration.
*Should be performed under expert supervision to avoid complications like basti vyapad.

🔺NADI SVEDHANAM

📌DEFINITION

🔸Nāḍī Svedanam is a type of Saagni Swedana (sudation therapy using heat) in which medicated steam (from decoctions, water, or herbal mixtures) is directed through a tube/nozzle to a specific part or the whole body for inducing sweating and relieving stiffness, pain, and toxins.

📌DRUGS USED

🔸Daśamoola
🔸Eranda
🔸Nirgundi
🔸Arka
🔸Rasna
🔸Vacha
🔸Shunthi
🔸Devadaru
🔸Musta
🔸Patra

📌PROCEDURE

1. Purva Karma (Preparation):
🔸Selection of patients and medicines.
🔸Abhyanga (oil massage) with suitable medicated oil.
2. Pradhana Karma (Main procedure):
🔸Decoction of selected drugs prepared and boiled.
🔸Steam collected and passed through a tube (nāḍī) directed to the affected part or whole body.
🔸Patient made to sweat until symptoms like lightness, relief of stiffness, and perspiration appear.
3. Paschat Karma (Post-procedure):
🔸Wiping off sweat.
🔸Rest and light diet.
🔸Avoid exposure to cold, wind, and heavy activity immediately.

📌INDICATED DISEASES

🔸Sandhivata (Osteoarthritis)
🔸Amavata (Rheumatoid arthritis)
🔸Gridhrasi (Sciatica)
🔸Katigraha (Low back pain)
🔸Mamsa shosha (Muscle wasting)
🔸Pakshaghata (Hemiplegia)
🔸Stambha (Stiffness)
🔸Vata Vyadhi (neuromuscular disorders)

📌MUST BE AVOIDED IN

🔸Pittaja rogas (Pitta disorders)
🔸Raktapitta (Bleeding disorders)
🔸Prameha (Diabetes with complications)
🔸Jwara (Fever)
🔸Pregnancy
🔸Dehydration and extreme weakness
🔸Patients with severe hypertension, heart diseases, or acute infections

📌PRECAUTIONS

🔸Steam temperature should be tolerable, not excessive.
🔸Protect eyes, ears, and genitals from direct steam exposure.
🔸Patient should be monitored for dizziness, fainting, or excessive sweating.
🔸Not to be performed on empty stomach or immediately after meals.
🔸Should be done under supervision of an Ayurvedic physician.

📌DEFINITION

*Before full manifestation, the following early symptoms occur:
*sirasula (Headache)
*Dantamāṃsa śotha (Swelling and sponginess of gums)
*Mukha dāha (Burning sensation in mouth)
*Lalasrava (Excessive salivation)
*Kampa (Tremors in limbs)
*Hṛllāsa (Nausea)
*Arochaka (Loss of appetite)

🔺 LAKSANAM 
(Manifest Symptoms)

*Classical: Rasa Ratna Samuccaya 5/70–75
*Tīkṣṇa dāha (Severe burning all over body)
*Mukhapāka (Ulceration in mouth and gums)

*Jihva sotha (Swelling of tongue)

*Bhrama, Mūrcchā (Giddiness and fainting)
*Ati Lālāsrāva (Excessive salivation)
*Atisāra (Diarrhoea in severe cases)

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*Appearance: Pale, anxious, or tremulous look
*vital signs:
*Pulse – tachycardia
*Blood pressure – may be normal or elevated
*Temperature – mild fever in acute cases
*Respiratory rate – may increase if respiratory distress present
*Skin: Excessive sweating, rash, desquamation in chronic exposure
*Odor: Metallic smell from breath

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

a) Nervous System
*Tremors (“Mercurial tremors”)
*Insomnia, irritability, memory loss
*Peripheral neuropathy
*Ataxia (loss of coordination)
b) Gastrointestinal System
*Metallic taste in mouth
*Stomatitis, gingivitis, excessive salivation
*Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea
c) Renal System
*Proteinuria, oliguria
*Signs of renal failure in chronic cases
d) Respiratory System
*cough, chest pain, dyspnea (if inhaled mercury vapors)
e) Cardiovascular System
*Palpitations, tachycardia
*Hypertension possible due to stress response
f) Skin and Mucosa
*Dermatitis, peeling, discoloration of gums (“blue line” on gums)

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*Blood mercury level: ↑ (>10 µg/L indicates exposure)
*Urinary mercury level: ↑ (>50 µg/L diagnostic)
*Renal function tests: ↑ BUN, ↑ creatinine
*Liver function tests: May show mild elevation
*CBC: Anemia, leukocytosis possible
*Urinalysis: Proteinuria, cylindruria
*ECG: Non-specific tachycardia or arrhythmia in severe cases

🔺UPASAYA

🔺ANUPASAYA (Aggravating Factors)

*Heat exposure, alcohol intake.

d. Gastrointestinal System:

*CT/MRI Brain: To detect cerebral hemorrhage, infarct, or mass lesion.
*EEG: To assess brain activity in coma.

*Crepitus (crackling sound)
*Abnormal mobility
*Measurement:

*Girth (for swelling or atrophy)

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Musculoskeletal system:
*Examine the affected bone or joint for tenderness, instability, range of motion.
*Neurovascular examination – check distal pulse, capillary refill, and sensory function.
*Cardiovascular system: To assess signs of shock or vascular injury.
*Respiratory system: Especially in fractures of ribs or clavicle.
*Nervous system: To rule out peripheral nerve injury associated with fractures/dislocations.

🔺 LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

1. Routine Tests:
*CBC (to check for infection, anemia, or internal bleeding)
*ESR (may be raised in inflammation)
*Blood sugar (before surgery or plaster application)
. Imaging:

*CT scan – for complex or intra-articular fractures
*MRI – for associated soft tissue, ligament, or cartilage injury
3. Special Tests:
*Doppler study – if vascular injury is suspected
*Nerve conduction test – in case of neurological deficit

📌SAMPRAPTI (pathogenesis)

*Vitiation of vāta, pitta, kapha → these act on duṣyas: tvak, rakta, mamsa, lasikā (seven dravyas) → formation of Kusṭha lesions. 
*The pathogenesis for Kakanaka:

*The classical text emphasises the importance of cleansing (śodhana) therapies due to depth of doṣa involvement. 

🔺 SAMANYA CIKITSA (general treatment principles)

*Irrespective of type, Kusṭha treatment involves a two-fold approach: *sodhana (purificatory) and śamana (pacification). Key general steps:
*Nidana-parivarjana (avoid causative factors)
*Aharavihara correction (diet & lifestyle)
*sodhana therapies (vāmana, virechana, basti, raktamokṣaṇa depending on doṣa predominance) 
*External applications (lepa, snāna with medicated oils) and internal administrations of kushṭha-hāraka drugs.
*Maintaining skin hygiene, avoiding aggravation, restoring normal functions.

*Because Kakanaka is Mahā-Kushta with tridoṣa involvement, the specific treatment is more intensive:

🔺PURISHA KSHAYAM 


🔺NIDANAM 
(Causative factors)

**Any cause that leads to decreased stool formation or evacuation, e.g.: suppression of puriṣa vega (urge) (adhyāśana, atisaṃhṛti), vitiation of Vāta (especially in pakvāśaya) leading to slower movement. For example:
*“Decrease of puriṣa causes …” in the chapter on Mala Kṣaya. 
*Poor digestive fire (agni), resulting in inadequate formation of māla (faeces) → mala kṣaya. 
*Rukṣa, hāra (excessive exertion), vāyu aggravating causes which reduce stool quantity. (Analogous to Vāta kṣaya features)
*Possibly factors such as intense vāmana/virechana or over-cleansing leading to excessive elimination and eventual kṣaya of stool formation.

🔺PURVARUPAM 
(Prodromal signs)

*Pūrvarūpa information is limited in classical texts for puriṣa kṣaya specifically. However from the general mala-kṣaya discussion:
*Slight reduction in frequency of stools
*Feeling of fullness or heaviness in abdomen but less stool passage
*Occasional flatus or upward movement of vāyu (wind) indicating delayed puriṣa evacuation. 
*These early signs may precede full lakṣaṇa.

🔺 LAKSHANAM 
 (Clinical features)

*The chapter on “Mala Kṣaya” (Suśruta Saṃhitā, Sūtra Sthāna 15) lists:
** “When puriṣa decreases – there is pain/discomfort in region of the heart and flanks; upward movement of air (flatus) accompanied with sound in abdomen.” 

*Reduced stool quantity, possibly dry, hard, with difficulty in evacuation
*Accumulation of vāyu in the abdomen, gurgling, distension
*Weakness, loss of appetite, or indigestion may accompany because of underlying agni diminution
*In modern review: “When Puriṣa decreases, the Vāyu comes out from mouth and anus producing sound; pain in heart & abdomen; the kukṣī is surrounded by Vāyu.”


🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*Appearance: Emaciation, dryness of skin
*Vital signs:
*Pulse – normal or feeble
*temperature – normal
*Blood pressure – may be low in dehydration
*Hydration status: Dry tongue, sunken eyes, reduced skin turgor
*Nutritional status: Signs of malnutrition
*Abdominal inspection: Scaphoid abdomen, visible peristalsis sometimes

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

1. Abdomen:
*Palpation – tenderness (if constipation/intestinal obstruction)
*Percussion – distension in chronic constipation
*Auscultation – reduced bowel sounds
2. Cardiovascular system: Weak pulse due to dehydration or electrolyte imbalance
3. Nervous system: Weakness, irritability due to metabolic disturbances

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*Complete Blood Count (CBC): To detect anemia or infection
*Serum Electrolytes: Na⁺, K⁺, Cl⁻ (to check dehydration/electrolyte imbalance)

*Liver Function Test (LFT): For associated hepatic issues
*Stool Examination:
*Quantity, consistency, color

🔺PURISHA KSHAYAM

🔺DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

1. Chronic Constipation

3. Intestinal Obstruction
4. Dehydration with Reduced Bowel Movement
5. Hypothyroidism (causing reduced bowel motility)
6. Colonic Inertia
7. Megacolon (chronic form)




🔺SAMPRAPTI 
(Pathogenesis)

*In Ayurvedic understanding: decrease of stool (mala kṣaya) is due to insufficient formation/secretion of stool or decreased urge (vega) → resulting in retention or minimal elimination → vāyu stagnation, srotodushti of puriṣavāha srotas → disturbed Vāyu–Mala dynamics. 
*Vāta kṣaya (depletion of normal Vāyu) or Vāta prāṇa disturbances may hamper the downward movement of stools → Purīṣa Kṣaya.
*The mala being less leads to accumulation of vāyu, distension; the usual downward kinetic force is less.
*Thus chain: Causative factors → Agni diminishes / srotas obstructed → stool formation/evacuation reduces → vitiated Vāyu + retained mala → lakṣaṇa.

🔺SAMANYA CHIKITSA 
(General treatment)

*The general therapeutic principle for kṣaya (depletion) states: nourish what is depleted (Kṣina Br̥ṃhayitavyā) and avoid further depletion. 
*In this case:
*Enhance agni (deepana, pācana) so stool is formed properly
*Light, moderately lubricated diet (since too heavy may hamper evacuation)
*Avoid suppression of puriṣa vega; ensure regular bowel habit
*Gentle fomentation (svedana), mild oleation (abhyanga) to mobilise vāyu and stimulate downward movement
*Lifestyle: regular exercise, avoid excessive fasting, prolonged supine staying etc which hamper puriṣa elimination.

🔺VISESHA  CHIKITSA
 (Specific treatment)

*In cases where puriṣa kṣaya is prominent with vāyu stagnation: Vāta-pacifying therapies:
*Mild virechana (purgation) if indicated (but careful because stool formation is already low)
*Use of vātaghna, grahi (firming) herbs: e.g., Saṃśodhaka and grahi aushadhis
*If stool formation is very low, mild snehapāna (oleation) followed by mild purgation may help mobilise retained mala.
*Local therapies: mild basti (enema) with oil decoction for Vāta-dominant mala stagnation.
*Use of grahi diet: banana, jaggery, ghee, warm milk to support stool formation gently.


🔺UPASAYA 
(factors which relieve):

*Warm oleation, mild exercise, warm fluids
*Foods which are lightly lubricating, warm, and easy to digest
*Avoidance of suppression of stool urge

🔺ANUPASAYA 
(factors which aggravate):

*Prolonged fasting, heavy dry diet, cold/dry season, excessive Vāta-producing foods, suppression of urges
*Excessive exercise or restlessness increasing vāyu stagnation
*Intake of Rukṣa (dry), Kevala Laghū (purely light) without balancing marrow/nourishment
**References & Classical citations
*Suśruta Saṃhitā, Sūtra Sthāna 15 (Dosha-Dhātu-Mala Kṣaya Vr̥ddhi) describes mala kṣaya including puriṣa kṣaya. 
*The document “Critical Evaluation of Purīṣa Parīkṣā” gives lakṣaṇa of puriṣa kṣaya. 
*Various modern review articles (e.g., on purīṣa parīkṣā) list the decreased stool features.

*Ati-vyāyāma (excessive exertion)
*Ati-upavāsa (excess fasting)
*Rukṣa, laghu, śīta, alpa āhāra
*Injury to nerves or marmas (especially snāyu and majjā)
*Dhātu kṣaya (especially māṃsa and majjā dhātu)
*Vāta-anubandha after vāta-kaphaja rogas

🔺PURVARUPAM 
(पूर्वरूपम्) – Premonitory Symptoms

*Slight weakness or heaviness in limbs
*Stiffness in joints
*Reduced ability to move or lift limbs
*Mild pain or tingling sensation
*Feeling of instability or unsteadiness

🔺LAKSANAM 
 (लक्षणम्) – Signs & Symptoms

*Inability to walk or move limbs properly (especially legs)
*Loss of strength (bala-kṣaya)
*Stiffness or contraction of muscles
*Numbness or loss of sensation (supti)
*Reduced motor power without pain (mūtrita pāda, pada-akarmaṇya)
*According to Charaka, “पङ्घु” refers to a person who cannot walk due to vāta vitiation



🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION:

*Appearance: Weakness or paralysis in limbs
*Gait: Unsteady or dragging (limping)
*Posture: Abnormal limb positioning
*Speech: May be slurred if facial muscles involved
*Muscle tone: Decreased (flaccidity) or increased (spasticity)
*Reflexes: Diminished or exaggerated depending on site of lesion
*Sensory changes: Numbness, tingling, or loss of sensation
*Mental status: May be normal unless central cause involved

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION:

*Central Nervous System (CNS): Check for motor/sensory loss, cranial nerve involvement, tone, coordination, reflexes
*Cardiovascular system: Rule out hypertension or embolic causes (stroke)
*Respiratory system: Observe for breathing difficulty if bulbar palsy involved
*Musculoskeletal system: Muscle wasting, contractures, deformity

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*(According to modern diagnostic approach for neuromuscular disorders)
*Blood Tests:
*CBC, ESR (infection/inflammation)
*Blood sugar (diabetes-related neuropathy)
*Electrolytes (Na⁺, K⁺, Ca²⁺ imbalance)
*Thyroid profile (hypothyroid myopathy)
*Creatine phosphokinase (CPK) — for muscle damage
*Vitamin B12 levels — neuropathy
*Imaging:
*MRI / CT brain and spine: To detect stroke, lesion, compression, or demyelination
*Nerve conduction study (NCS) / Electromyography (EMG): For nerve/muscle involvement
*X-ray spine: For spondylotic changes or trauma
*Other tests:
*CSF analysis (for demyelinating disorders)
*Autoimmune profile (e.g., Myasthenia Gravis)

🔺LAKSANAM  (Symptoms / Clinical features)

*Snayu granthi (fibrous thickening) visible over śukla bhāga (white part of eye)
*Kṛṣṇa varna pīḍā (pain and blackish discoloration)
*Toda (pricking pain) and āśru srava (watering)

*(Sushruta Uttara Tantra, Netra Roga Vigyaniyam)

*Blood pressure — usually normal
*Temperature — afebrile

*Pallor, icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, lymphadenopathy, edema — usually absent

🔺 SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Nervous system:
*To rule out cranial nerve involvement (esp. optic nerve or oculomotor nerve)
*Musculoskeletal system:
*Check for associated tendon or ligament disorders (as snayu denotes ligaments/tendons)
*Ophthalmic (local eye examination):
*Inspection: visible swelling or bulge near the sclera or conjunctiva
*Palpation: firmness over the swelling (fibrous consistency)
*Slit lamp examination: localized thickening or fibrous nodule near the corneal/scleral junction
*Visual acuity test: may show mild blurring
*Extraocular movements: usually normal, but mild restriction may be present
*Fundoscopy: generally normal

🔺 LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*CBC — to rule out infection or inflammation
*ESR — may be slightly raised if chronic inflammation present
*Blood sugar — to exclude diabetic eye changes
*Specific Ophthalmic Tests:
*Slit-lamp biomicroscopy — to assess exact site and nature of lesion
*OCT (Optical Coherence Tomography) — for corneal/scleral tissue assessment
*Ultrasound B-scan — if deeper lesion suspected
*Histopathology (if excised) — to confirm fibrous tissue proliferation

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*Appearance: Distended abdomen with visible veins (“caput medusae”)
*Gait: Difficulty walking due to abdominal distension
*Facial appearance: Puffy face, pedal edema
*Posture: Sitting posture preferred due to dyspnea on lying down
*Skin: Pallor, icterus (in liver disease), spider nevi, palmar erythema
*Nails: Leukonychia (white nails in liver disease)
*Pulse: May be normal or rapid (tachycardia in anemia or heart failure)
*Blood Pressure: May be low in cirrhosis, high in cardiac causes

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

1. Abdominal Examination
*Inspection:
*Distension with full flanks
*Umbilicus everted
*Shiny stretched skin with dilated veins
*Palpation:
*Fluid thrill present
*Liver and spleen may be enlarged
*Percussion:
*Shifting dullness and fluid wave present
*Auscultation:
*Bowel sounds reduced or normal
2. Cardiovascular System
*Signs of right-sided heart failure (raised JVP, pedal edema, hepatomegaly)
3. Respiratory System
*Diminished breath sounds at lung bases (due to upward pressure by fluid)
4. Nervous System
*In chronic liver disease: possible signs of hepatic encephalopathy (confusion, tremor)

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*Blood Tests
*CBC: May show anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia
*Liver Function Tests:
*↑ Bilirubin, ↑ SGOT/SGPT, ↑ Alkaline phosphatase
*↓ Albumin
*Renal Function Tests:
*↑ Urea, ↑ Creatinine
*Serum Electrolytes:
*Hyponatremia, hypokalemia
*Coagulation Profile:
*Prolonged PT/INR (in liver disease)
*Urine Examination
*Proteinuria (in nephrotic causes)
*Low sodium (in cirrhosis with ascites)
*Ascitic Fluid Analysis (Paracentesis)
*Appearance: Clear, turbid, or bloody
*Protein Content:
*<2.5 g/dL → Transudate (e.g., cirrhosis)
* 2.5 g/dL → Exudate (e.g., malignancy, infection)

*SAAG (Serum-Ascitic Albumin Gradient):
*≥1.1 g/dL → Portal hypertension (Cirrhosis, CHF)
*<1.1 g/dL → Non-portal causes (malignancy, tuberculosis)
*Microscopy: WBC count, cytology, Gram stain, AFB test if infection suspected
*Imaging
*Ultrasound Abdomen: Confirms fluid, liver size, spleen, portal vein diameter
*CT Scan: For malignancy, peritoneal disease
*Echocardiography: To assess cardiac cause

🔺KRIMIJA SHIRASHOOLAM (कृमिज शिरःशूलम्)

🔺NIDANAM 
(निदानम् – Causes)

*Krimija (worm/microbial) infestation due to:
*Improper oral hygiene
*Kapha–pitta aggravating diet (guru, snigdha, amla, madhura, abhishyandi ahara)
*Excess sweet or fermented food
*Infected scalp wounds or nasal infections
*Negligence of cleanliness (mala sevana, shauchāchāra viruddha)
*Contaminated food/water

🔺PURVARUPAM 
(पूर्वरूपम् – Prodromal Symptoms)

*Mild itching or crawling sensation on scalp or inside nose
*Heaviness of head
*Bad smell from nose or mouth
*Mild fever or discomfort
*Drowsiness, anorexia
*Mucopurulent nasal discharge

🔺LAKṢAṆAM
(लक्षणम् – CLINICAL FEATURES

*Severe headache (Shirashoola), particularly in frontal and nasal region
*Kandu (itching) and Toda (piercing pain) on scalp
*Nasa srava (purulent nasal discharge, sometimes with worms)
*Karna-nāsa-gala-gandha dourgandhya (foul smell from ear, nose, throat)
*Netra daha, kapha-pitta srava
*Utklesha (nausea), jwara (fever)
*Occasionally visible worms emerging from nasal discharge

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*General appearance: Pallor, fatigue, weakness
*Vital signs:
*Temperature – may be normal or slightly raised
*Pulse – may be increased due to anemia or infection
*BP – usually normal or low (if chronic weakness present)
*Nutritional status: Often poor (malnutrition due to parasitic infestation)
*Skin and mucosa: Pallor, itching, urticaria (due to allergic reaction from parasites)
*Lymph nodes: May be mildly enlarged (reactive lymphadenopathy)
*Eyes: Pale conjunctiva, periorbital puffiness (if associated sinusitis or allergic reaction)

🔺 SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

1. Head and Neck

*Tenderness over scalp or sinuses
*Dull aching or throbbing headache
*Possible crawling/tingling sensation on scalp (subjective feeling of “worms”)
*Sinus congestion or nasal discharge (if secondary sinus infection)
2. Abdomen
*Distension, discomfort, borborygmi
*Signs of parasitic infestation — bloating, irregular bowel habits, itching around anus
3. Neurological Examination
*Usually normal; sometimes mild irritability, disturbed sleep, or anxiety due to chronic parasitic irritation

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

1. Complete Blood Count (CBC)
*Eosinophilia (↑ eosinophils – typical of parasitic infection)
*Mild anemia (microcytic hypochromic)
*Raised ESR occasionally
2. Peripheral Blood Smear
*To detect microfilaria (in filarial infection)
3. Stool Examination
*Ova or cysts of intestinal parasites (e.g., Ascaris, Ancylostoma, Taenia, Giardia, Entamoeba histolytica)
4. Urine Examination
*In rare cases, Schistosoma haematobium ova may be found
5. Allergy / IgE levels
*Elevated in parasitic infestations
6. Imaging (if needed)
*CT/MRI Brain or Paranasal Sinus (PNS) – to rule out sinusitis or intracranial parasitic lesions (neurocysticercosis, hydatid cyst)

🔺KRIMIJA SHIRASHOOLAM (कृमिज शिरःशूलम्)

🔺DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

	1. Neurocysticercosis (parasitic CNS infection)
	2. Sinusitis-associated headache
	3. Allergic rhinosinusitis
	4. Tension-type headache (with parasitic cause triggering irritability)
	5. Helminthic infestation with secondary headache
	6. Migraine with gastrointestinal parasitosis


🔺 SAMPRAPTI 
(संप्राप्तिः – Pathogenesis)

1. Due to nidana, kapha and pitta doshas aggravate.
2. These vitiate rakta and mamsa dhatus of the shira pradesha (head region).
3. The krimi (microorganisms) get localized in this region.
4. Leads to inflammation, suppuration, and pain (shoola) — forming Krimija Shirashoolam.
-Samprapti Ghataka:
*Dosha: Kapha–Pitta
*Dushya: Rakta, Mamsa
*Agni: Jatharagni and Dhatvagni mandya
*Srotas: Rasavaha, Raktavaha, Mamsavaha, Shiroroga marga
*Srotodushti: Sanga, Pūrana
*Roga marga: Uttamanga
*Rogabheda: Shiroga

🔺 SAMANYA CHIKITSA (General Line of Treatment)

*Krimighna Chikitsa (anti-parasitic treatment)
*Kapha–Pitta shamana
*Shiroshodhana (cleansing of head)
*Nasya, Dhoomapana, Kavala, Gandusha
*Drugs used:
*Vidanga, Triphala, Musta, Nimba, Haridra, Shunti, Trikatu

🔺 UPASHAYA 
(Relieving Factors)

*Use of krimighna dravya (e.g., Vidanga churna)
*Nasya with Nimba taila or Triphala taila
*Dhoomapana with krimighna herbs
*Light diet, bitter–astringent foods

🔺 ANUPASHAYA
  (Aggravating Factors)

*Sweet, heavy, oily, or sour foods
*Sleeping during daytime
*Ignoring nasal or scalp hygiene
*exposure to dust and heat

🔺 VISESHA  CHIKITSA (Specific Treatment)


a. Shodhana:
*Nasya Karma: with Nimba taila, Vidanga taila, or Triphala taila
*Vamana / Virechana: if dosha accumulation is severe
*Dhoomapana: with krimighna dravyas
b. Shamana 
*Internal medications:
*Vidanga churna
*Triphala churna
*Krimighna vati
*Gandhaka rasayana
*Nimba ghrita
c. Local applications:
*Shirolepa with Triphala + Nimba + Haridra
*Anjana with krimighna dravya *Reference (प्रमाण ग्रंथ):
*Sushruta Samhita, Uttara Tantra, Shiroroga Chikitsa Adhyaya
*Charaka Samhita – Chikitsa Sthana, Krimiroga Chikitsa
*Ashtanga Hridaya – Uttara Tantra, Shiroroga Nidana & Chikitsa

🔺PARISRAVA

🔺NIDANAM 
(Causative factors)

*(Susruta Samhita – Nidana Sthana 9/4; Chikitsa Sthana 1/6)
*Avaseka (repeated wetting of wound)
*Āghāta (injury or trauma)
*Dusta māṁsa saṁcaya (presence of necrotic tissue)
*Rakta duṣṭi (vitiation of blood)
*Improper wound management (aśuddha vrana sevana)
*Infections due to lack of aseptic care
*Doṣa involvement:
Mostly Pitta-Kapha predominance, with Rakta dushti.

🔺PURVARUPAM (Premonitory signs)

*Mild burning sensation (dāha)
*Slight oozing or serous discharge
*Local tenderness (sparsha asahatva)
*Redness (rāga)
*Feeling of heaviness or itching (kaṇḍu)

🔺 LAKSANAM 
 (Clinical features)

*(Sushruta Chikitsa Sthana 1/57–59)
*Excessive discharge (srava bahulyam) — purulent or serous
*Foul smell (durgandha)
*Pain and swelling around wound
*Burning sensation
*Discoloration (pita, shyava, rakta varna)
*Delayed wound healing
*Modern correlation:
*Chronic suppurative wound
*Sinus with discharge
*Chronic ulcer with infection

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*Observation:
*Site of discharge (e.g., wound, sinus, ulcer)
*Type of discharge – serous, purulent, bloody, foul-smelling
*Surrounding tissue – erythema, swelling, induration
*Signs of inflammation – redness, warmth, tenderness
*Palpation:
*Tenderness, fluctuation, induration
*Sinus or fistula tract
*Regional lymph node enlargement
*Vital Signs:
*Temperature – may indicate infection
*Pulse, BP, respiration rate
*Signs of systemic infection (fever, malaise)

🔺 SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Integumentary System: Look for abscesses, ulcers, cellulitis
*Musculoskeletal: Assess for involvement of bone (suggesting osteomyelitis)
*Lymphatic: Regional lymphadenitis
*Cardiovascular/Respiratory: Rule out sepsis-related changes
*Gastrointestinal/Genitourinary: If discharge is from perianal or genitourinary region, assess corresponding systems

🔺 LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

1. Blood Investigations:

*CBC (↑WBC count, ↑Neutrophils – suggest infection)
*ESR, CRP (elevated in chronic infection)
*Blood sugar (rule out diabetes as predisposing factor)
*Blood culture (if systemic infection suspected)

2. Local Investigations:

*Pus culture & sensitivity – to identify causative organism and antibiotic sensitivity
*Gram stain – bacterial morphology
*FNAC / Biopsy – if chronic non-healing lesion or malignancy suspected

3. Imaging (as needed):

*X-ray / MRI / CT – to assess for deeper extension, sinus tracts, or osteomyelitis
*Fistulogram – in case of sinus or fistula

🔺 DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

1. Chronic Abscess
2. Sinus Tract
3. Fistula-in-ano
4. Osteomyelitis
5. Pyoderma gangrenosum
6. Tubercular sinus
7. Chronic ulcer with secondary infection
8. Carbuncle or furuncle with discharge

🔺SAMPRAPTI (Pathogenesis)

1. Nidana sevana → Vitiation of Pitta and Kapha → involvement of Rakta dhatu
2. Doṣas localize at the wound site (Vrana sthāna)
3. Suppuration and tissue destruction → oozing of pus or serous fluid
4. Continued doṣa activity → chronic infected wound with Parisrava (continuous discharge)

🔺 SAMANYA CHIKITSA (General management)

*(Sushruta Chikitsa Sthana 1/74–79; Ashtanga Hridaya Chikitsa Sthana 25)
*Śodhana (Purification):
*Vrana śodhana dravyas – Panchavalkala kwatha, Triphala kwatha, Nimba, Haridra
*Parisheka (irrigation) with antiseptic decoctions
*Ropaṇa (Healing):
*Application of Jatyadi taila, Madhu, Ghrita
*Raktaprasādana:
*Manjishtha, Sariva, Triphala
*Internal medications:
*Guggulu, Kaishora guggulu, Gandhaka rasayana

🔺UPASAYA 
(Relieving factors)

*Use of tikta-kashaya dravyas (bitter-astringent drugs)
*Clean, dry wound management
*Use of Pitta-Kapha hara diet and medicines

🔺ANUPASAYA (Aggravating factors)

*Application of oil in suppurative stage
*Moist or unclean dressing
*Intake of amla, lavana, kshara foods
*Excessive heat or sun exposure

🔺VISESHA CHIKITSA (Specific treatment)

a) For Pitta-Kapha dushti vrana (Parisrava stage):
*Nimba patra, Triphala, Haridra, Daruharidra, Guduchi
*Parisheka with Triphala kwatha or Panchavalkala kwatha
*Lepa: Haridra + Ghee + Madhu
*Jatyadi taila or Nimba taila dressing
b) Surgical measures (if needed):
*Shastra karma (incision and drainage of pus)
*Kshara karma (chemical cauterization if sinus present)
*Ropana karma (healing therapy after proper shodhana)
** References:
*Suśruta Saṃhitā – Chikitsā Sthāna 1/74–79; Nidāna Sthāna 9/4
*Aṣṭāṅga Hṛdaya – Chikitsā Sthāna 25
*Bhāvaprakāśa – Chikitsā Prakaraṇa (Vrana chikitsā adhyāya)

🔺ANGAMARDHA 
 (अङ्गमर्द)

🔺NIDANAM 
(निदानम् — Causative factors)

*References: Charaka Sūtra 22/8; Mādhava Nidāna 2/6
*Causative factors include:
*Ati-vyāyāma (excessive physical exertion)
*Vega-dhāraṇa (suppression of natural urges)
*Ati-rukṣa āhāra (dry food intake)
*Ati-sīta or ati-uṣṇa sevana (excess exposure to cold or heat)
*Ratrijāgara (night vigil)
*Kṣhudhā, pipāsā (hunger, thirst)
*Vāta-prakopaka nidāna (anything increasing Vāta doṣa)

🔺 PURVARUPAM 
(पूर्वरूपम् — Premonitory symptoms)

*Laghutā (feeling of lightness and emptiness in limbs)
*Śunyata (numbness in the body)
*srama (fatigue on mild exertion)
*Manda aṅga-vedanā (mild body ache)

🔺 (लक्षणानि — SYMPTOMS)

*Main Features:
*Sarvanga-marda (generalized body ache)
*sula (pain in joints and muscles)
*Gaurava (heaviness of body)
*Jvara (mild fever may be associated)
*Klama (fatigue and tiredness)
*Stambha (stiffness of body parts)


🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*Parameter	Findings
*General Appearance	Tired, fatigued, malaise, muscle stiffness
*Body Temperature	May be normal or mildly raised (if associated with infection)
Pulse	May be increased (if fever or pain present)
*Blood Pressure	Usually normal; may vary with dehydration or systemic illness
*Respiratory Rate	Normal or slightly raised (due to discomfort or fever)
*Hydration Status	May show mild dehydration if due to viral or systemic illness
*Pain Assessment	Diffuse pain over muscles and joints
*Sleep and Appetite	Often disturbed, reduced appetite, lethargy

🔺 SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

1. Musculoskeletal System

*Tenderness over large and small muscle groups
*Muscle stiffness or spasm
*Normal joint mobility (unless associated condition present)
*No deformities or swelling unless secondary cause
2. Nervous System
*Normal reflexes and power
*May have mild fatigue or sensory dullness
3. Cardiovascular System
*Usually normal; tachycardia in fever
4. Respiratory System
*Normal breath sounds (unless infection like influenza)
5. Gastrointestinal System
*Sometimes mild indigestion, nausea, or anorexia

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*Test	Purpose / Finding
*CBC (Complete Blood Count)	To rule out infection or anemia
*ESR / CRP	Elevated in inflammatory or infectious causes
*LFT / RFT	To assess systemic illness
*Serum Electrolytes	To check for dehydration or imbalance
*Thyroid Profile (T3, T4, TSH)	To rule out hypothyroidism-induced fatigue
*Creatine Kinase (CK-MM)	Elevated in myositis or muscle inflammation
*Vitamin D & B12 Levels	Deficiency may cause muscle pain and fatigue
*Viral Marker Tests	Dengue, Influenza, Chikungunya (if fever present)
*Urine Routine / Microscopy	General health check

🔺GAMBHIRA HIKKA

🔺NIDANAM 
(Etiology / Causes):

*(Ref: Charaka Saṃhitā Chikitsāsthāna 17; Suśruta Saṃhitā Uttara Tantra 52)
*Ati-mātra bhojana (overeating)
*Guru, snigdha, madhura āhāra sevana
*Vega dhāraṇa (suppression of natural urges)
*Ati vyāyāma (excessive exercise)
*Ati bhāṣaṇa (excessive talking)
*Madyapāna (alcohol consumption)
*Dusta āhāra sevana (improper diet)
*Hṛd-roga, Udararoga, or Vāta prakopa due to kṣaya

🔺PURVARUPAM 
(Premonitory Symptoms):

*Prāṇa gati upadrava (disturbance in normal breath flow)
*Urah kampa (chest vibrations)
*Kṣavathu (frequent sneezing)
*Kaṇṭha shabda (throat sounds)
*Urah śūla (chest pain)

🔺LAKSANAM  
(Clinical Features / Symptoms):

*(As per Charaka Chikitsā 17/72-75)
*Gambhīra hikka is characterized by deep, forceful, and *continuous hiccups originating from āmāśaya or hṛdaya region.
*Gati hrasva (slow and deep inspiration)
*Bāhu, Pṛṣṭha, Uras, Kaṇṭha, Śira vedanā (pain in arms, back, chest, throat, head)
*Saṃmoha (fainting)
*Aśakti (loss of strength)
*Hṛdaya klama (fatigue of heart)
*Jīvitāśa hāni (life-threatening stage if uncontrolled)

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*General Appearance: Distressed due to continuous hiccups
-Vital Signs:
-Pulse: May be elevated due to anxiety or dehydration
*BP: Usually normal or slightly elevated due to stress
*Temperature: Normal unless underlying infection
*Respiratory Rate: May increase due to diaphragm irritation
*Hydration Status: Check for dehydration (dry tongue, poor skin turgor)
*Nutritional Status: Assess for malnutrition or chronic illness
*Neurological Assessment: Rule out CNS causes of persistent hiccups
*Abdominal Examination: Check for tenderness, distension, hepatomegaly

🔺 SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

A. Respiratory System
*Inspect for abnormal chest movements
*Palpate for diaphragmatic excursion
*Auscultate for any basal -crepitations (suggestive of pneumonia or effusion)
B. Gastrointestinal System
*Examine for hepatomegaly, splenomegaly
*Epigastric tenderness (gastritis, reflux)
*Abdominal distension (gas accumulation or ascites)
C. Cardiovascular System
*Check for pericarditis or myocardial infarction (rare cause of hiccups)
D. Central Nervous System
*Assess for cranial nerve abnormalities (especially IX, X involvement)
*Look for signs of stroke, space-occupying lesions, or brainstem disorders

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*Investigation	Purpose / Findings
*CBC	Detect infection, inflammation, or anemia
LFT (Liver Function Test)	Hepatitis, cirrhosis, or hepatic mass
*RFT (Renal Function Test)	Uremia as a cause of persistent hiccups
Serum Electrolytes	Check Na⁺, K⁺, Ca²⁺, Cl⁻ imbalances
Blood Glucose	*Diabetes-related autonomic neuropathy
Chest X-ray	Pneumonia, pleural effusion, mediastinal mass
*Abdominal Ultrasound / CT scan	Liver enlargement, gastric distension, tumors
*MRI Brain / CT Brain	CNS lesions affecting medulla or phrenic nerve center
Endoscopy (if needed)	*GERD, gastritis, or esophageal lesions

🔺 DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

*Intractable Hiccups	Hiccups lasting 
>48 hours, often due to irritation of vagus or phrenic nerve
*Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)	Acid reflux stimulating the diaphragm
Diaphragmatic Irritation (Phrenic Nerve Involvement)
*	Due to liver abscess, subphrenic abscess, or mediastinal tumor
*CNS Lesions (Stroke / Tumor / Encephalitis)	*Persistent hiccups with neurological signs
*Uremia (Renal Failure)	Toxin accumulation affecting respiratory centers
*Pneumonia / Pleuritis	Diaphragmatic irritation from infection
*Myocardial Infarction (Inferior wall)	Rare cause due to vagus nerve stimulation
*Hiatus Hernia / Gastric Distension	Mechanical irritation of the diaphragm

🔺 SAMPRAPTI (Pathogenesis):

*Due to nidāna sevana, Vāta and Kapha become vitiated.
*They obstruct the normal movement of Prāṇa and Udāna vāyu in the ūrasa (chest region).
*This results in spasmodic movement of the diaphragm and respiratory muscles → Hikka utpatti (hiccup generation).
*When the origin is deep (āmāśaya/hṛdaya), it becomes Gambhīra Hikkā — severe and life-threatening.

🔺SAMANYA CHIKITSA (General Line of Treatment):

*(Ref: Charaka Chikitsā 17/128–135)
-Snehana – internal and external oleation with Taila, Ghṛta
-Svedana – mild sudation for chest and back
*Mridu Vamana or Virechana – if Kapha dominance
*Nāsya – use of medicated oils
*Dhumapāna – mild medicated smoking
*Hṛdya dravya sevana – use of cardiac supportive herbs

🔺UPASHAYA 
(Relieving Factors):

*Use of warm ghṛta, milk, or water
*Gentle massage with warm oils
*Warm environment and rest
*Suppression of anxiety and stress

🔺ANUPASHAYA (Aggravating Factors):

*Cold, dry, or heavy food
*Exposure to cold air or water
*Excessive talking or exertion
*Anger or emotional stress



🔺VISESHA CHIKITSA :

*(Charaka Chikitsā 17/132–135, Suśruta Uttara 52/21–25)
*Taila snehapāna – e.g., Tila taila, Ksheerabala taila
*Ghṛta yoga – Vacha ghrita, Yashtimadhu ghrita
*Mridu abhyanga over Urah, Kaṇṭha, Pṛṣṭha
*Dhumapāna with Aguru, Vacha, Haridra
*Swedana with Dashamoola kvātha
*Sneha nasyam with Anu taila or Ksheerabala taila
*Hridaya-poshaka dravyas: Arjuna, Bala, Shatavari, Ashwagandha
*Mṛdu anuvasana basti with Eranda taila or Dashamoola taila

*Bowel sounds

🔺JIHWA UPARI MAMSA VRIDHI

🔺 NIDANA (निदानम्) – Causes

*The main causative factors (according to Acharya Sushruta – Su. Ut. 20/7) include:
*Kshata (trauma) to tongue or its base
*Kaphaja vitiation (especially due to kapha-aggravating ahara-vihara)
*Mamsa and Rakta dushti
*Retention of doshas under the tongue
*Overuse of heavy, unctuous, and cold foods


🔺PURVARUPA (पूर्वरूपाणि) – Premonitory Symptoms

*Although not distinctly mentioned, general prodromal signs of jihvaroga may include:
*Slight discomfort under the tongue
*Feeling of heaviness or swelling
*Mild pain or tension in the tongue or mouth floor


🔺LAKSHANA (लक्षणानि) – SYMPTOMS

As per Sushruta Samhita – Uttara Tantra 20/7:
*A rounded, raised swelling occurs beneath the tongue
*Swelling appears like a blister or air-filled balloon (resembling a frog’s underthroat sac – hence modern synonym ranula)
*It causes difficulty in speaking, chewing, or swallowing
*May be painless or mildly painful
*Soft, bluish, or translucent appearance (in kapha dominance)



🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION:

*Vital signs: Temperature (check for fever), pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate.
*Appearance: Look for signs of discomfort, drooling, or difficulty speaking/swallowing.
*Oral hygiene: Assess for poor hygiene or trauma.
*Lymph nodes: Palpate for submandibular or cervical lymphadenopathy.

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION:

*ENT Examination:
*Inspect oral cavity (floor of mouth, tongue movement, swelling, pus).
*Palpation of sublingual swelling: fluctuant or firm?
*Tongue elevation test: may reveal sublingual swelling.
*Neurological Exam (if speech/swallowing affected).
*Neck Examination: For tenderness, masses, or signs of spread.

🔺 LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS:

*Complete Blood Count (CBC): Look for elevated WBCs (infection).
*CRP/ESR: Inflammatory markers.

*General appearance – distress, pallor, cyanosis, respiratory difficulty
*Pulse – tachycardia (possible hypovolemia or shock)
*Blood pressure – hypotension in severe cases
*Respiratory rate – tachypnea or bradypnea depending on severity
*Temperature – normal or low (shock)
*Level of consciousness – alertness, confusion, or unconsciousness
*Skin – pallor, diaphoresis, cold clammy extremities
*Posture – splinting of chest, reluctance to move
*Inspection of chest – swelling, deformity, bruising, open wounds, asymmetry of movement

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Respiratory System
*Inspection: unequal chest movement, flail segment, visible wound
*Palpation: tenderness, crepitus (subcutaneous emphysema), rib step deformity
*Percussion: dullness (hemothorax) or hyperresonance (pneumothorax)
*Auscultation: diminished/absent breath sounds, crackles, wheeze
*Cardiovascular System
*Heart sounds: muffled (pericardial tamponade)
*Jugular venous distension (tension pneumothorax, cardiac tamponade)
*Signs of shock
*Abdomen
*Check for associated injuries (diaphragmatic rupture, organ injury)

🔺 LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*CBC – anemia, leukocytosis
*Blood grouping & cross-matching – if transfusion required
*ABG (Arterial Blood Gas) – hypoxia, acidosis
*Chest X-ray – rib fracture, lung collapse, hemothorax, pneumothorax
*CT scan (Thorax) – detailed injury mapping
*ECG – arrhythmia, myocardial injury
*Ultrasound / FAST – pericardial or pleural fluid
*Serum electrolytes – in severe trauma
*Coagulation profile – before surgery if indicated

🔺URA ABHIGHATAM (उरःअभिघात) 
[Trauma to chest]

🔺 DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS


*Rib fracture
*Sternum fracture
*Pneumothorax
*Hemothorax
*Pulmonary contusion
*Cardiac tamponade
*Myocardial contusion
*Flail chest
*Diaphragmatic rupture
*Massive hemoptysis (secondary to lung laceration)

🔺SAMPRAPTI (Pathogenesis)

1. Bahya Abhighata → Marmabhighata (Ura region includes vital marmas like Hridaya marma)
2. Dhatu Kshata – Raktadhatu, Mamsa Dhatu primarily affected → Vata aggravation due to kshata
3. Vata Prakopa → produces intense pain, dryness, and impaired function of prana vaha srotas
4. Pitta association → Inflammation, heat,bleeding
5. 5. Kapha association (later stage) → Swelling, stiffness, sluggish healing

🔺SAMANYA CHIKITSA  (General Management Principles)

*From Susruta & Astanga Hṛdaya:
*sodhana in contaminated wounds (Vrana sodhana)
*samana for pain, swelling, inflammation
*Ropana for healing of kshata
*Marmaraksha – Protection of vital points
*Vata-pitta samana measures


🔺UPASHAYA
 (Relieving Factors)

*Application of Sneha (Taila, Ghṛta) over wound margins
*Warm fomentation (Ushna Sveda) after initial swelling subsides
*Gentle binding (Bandhana) to protect injury
*Intake of madhura rasa & snigdha ahara to promote healing

🔺ANUPASHAYA (Aggravating Factors)

*Excessive movement of chest and arms
*Exposure to cold & dry air (increases Vāta)
*Consumption of dry, katu, tikta, kashaya ahara
*Coughing forcefully, straining voice, or heavy lifting

🔺 VISHESHA CHIKITSA (Specific Management)

*From Sus.sam – Chikitsa Sthāna (Vrana Chikitsa & Marmabhighata):
* For Fresh Injury (abhighata Janya Vrana)
*sodhana – Irrigation with Pañcavalkala kashaya or Triphalq kashaya
*Sthambhana (for bleeding) – Use of Lodhra, Yashtimadhu, Raktasthapaka dravyas
*Bandhana – Proper bandaging to immobilize chest area
*For Pain & Vata Pacification
*Abhyanga with Mahanārāyaṇa taila or Sahachara taila around wound site (not directly on fresh wound)
*Internal use of Ghṛta preparations like Mahakalyanaka Ghrta (if no infection present)
*For Healing Stage
*Jatyadi taila / Ropana taila application over wound
*Rasayana for tissue regeneration – Asvagandha, Guduchi, Shatavari
*Internal Medicines (examples from classical formulations)
*sodhana – Triphala kashaya, Nimba patra kaṣhāya
*Śamana – Guggulu preparations (Yogaraja Guggulu)
*Ropana – Chyavanaprasha, Pippalyqdi ghrta for prana vaha srotas support
*Classical References
*Susruta Samhitha– Nidana Sthana 6, Chikitsa Sthana 2, Sharura Sthana 6 (Marmavibhaga)
*AH – Uttara Sthana 25 (Vrana Chikitsa)
*Charaka Samhita – Chikitsa Sthana 25 (Vrana Chikitsa principles)

🔺निदानम् 
(Nidanam – Etiology)

*Classical references: Charaka Samhita, Sutra Sthana 1/57; Ashtanga Hridaya, Nidana Sthana 6; Charaka, Chikitsa Sthana 1 (Unmada)
*Manasika Hetu (psychological causes)
*Ati-chinta (excessive worry)
*Bhaya (fear), Shoka (grief)
*Krodha (anger), Irshya (jealousy)
*Asatmya indriyartha samyoga (improper sensory contact)
*Sharirika Hetu (physical causes)
*Roga upadrava (complication of other diseases)
*Vegadharana (suppression of natural urges) — especially manovega
*Vata-pitta prakopa by ahara-vihara


🔺 पूर्वरूपम् 
(PORVAROOPAM – Prodromal symptoms)

(Charaka Chikitsa 7/5 – Unmada Purvaroopam)
*Anavasthita chitta (unstable mind)
*Alpashabda-pralapam (occasional irrelevant speech)
*Nidra-viparyaya (disturbed sleep)
*Anavastitha drishti (wandering gaze)
*Hridaya spandanam (palpitation)
*Vikshepa (restlessness)

🔺लक्षाणम् 
(LAKSANAM 
– SIGNS & SYMPTOMS)

*(Charaka, Chikitsa Sthana 7/10; Sushruta, Uttara Tantra 62)
*Ati krodha (excessive anger)
*Ashru moksha (crying spells) or hasi (inappropriate laughter)
*Vikshepa (mental distraction)
*Vak-viparyaya (irrelevant speech)
*Cheshta asamarthata (incoherent actions)
*Shoka, bhaya, irshya pradhana bhava

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*Consciousness & Orientation: Level of alertness, orientation to time, place, person.
*Speech: Clarity, coherence, rate of speech (may be accelerated or disorganized in mania, slowed in depression).
*Facial Expression & Eye Contact: Flat affect, inappropriate smiling, agitation.
*Motor Activity: Psychomotor agitation or retardation, restlessness, pacing.
*Mood & Affect: Elevated, irritable, anxious, depressed, labile.
*Behavior: Aggressive, impulsive, withdrawn, uncooperative.
*Personal Hygiene: Neglect of grooming, disheveled appearance.

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*CNS Examination:
*Higher mental functions (memory, attention, judgment, insight)
*Cranial nerves
*Motor and sensory system screening
*Cardiovascular System: BP, pulse (can be elevated in anxiety/agitation)
*Respiratory System: Respiration rate (increased in anxiety, panic)
*Endocrine Evaluation: Look for signs of thyroid disease (tremor, goiter, exophthalmos in hyperthyroidism).


🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*(to rule out organic causes & support diagnosis)
*Complete Blood Count (CBC) – to rule out infections or anemia affecting mental state
*Thyroid Function Tests (T3, T4, TSH) – to exclude thyroid disorders mimicking psychiatric illness
*Fasting Blood Glucose / HbA1c – metabolic profile
*Liver Function Tests (LFTs) – hepatic encephalopathy exclusion
*Renal Function Tests (RFTs) – chronic kidney disease-related cognitive impairment
*Serum Electrolytes – Na+, K+, Ca2+, Mg2+
*Vitamin B12 & Folate Levels – deficiency-related mood/cognitive changes
*Urine Drug Screen – substance-induced psychiatric symptoms
*Neuroimaging (MRI/CT brain) – only if focal neurological signs present
*EEG – if seizure disorder suspected

*Pulse – tachycardia (possible hypovolemia or shock)
*Blood pressure – hypotension in severe cases
*Respiratory rate – tachypnea or bradypnea depending on severity
*Temperature – normal or low (shock)
*Level of consciousness – alertness, confusion, or unconsciousness
*Skin – pallor, diaphoresis, cold clammy extremities
*Posture – splinting of chest, reluctance to move
*Inspection of chest – swelling, deformity, bruising, open wounds, asymmetry of movement

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Respiratory System
*Inspection: unequal chest movement, flail segment, visible wound
*Palpation: tenderness, crepitus (subcutaneous emphysema), rib step deformity
*Percussion: dullness (hemothorax) or hyperresonance (pneumothorax)
*Auscultation: diminished/absent breath sounds, crackles, wheeze
*Cardiovascular System
*Heart sounds: muffled (pericardial tamponade)
*Jugular venous distension (tension pneumothorax, cardiac tamponade)
*Signs of shock
*Abdomen
*Check for associated injuries (diaphragmatic rupture, organ injury)

🔺 LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*CBC – anemia, leukocytosis
*Blood grouping & cross-matching – if transfusion required
*ABG (Arterial Blood Gas) – hypoxia, acidosis
*Chest X-ray – rib fracture, lung collapse, hemothorax, pneumothorax
*CT scan (Thorax) – detailed injury mapping
*ECG – arrhythmia, myocardial injury
*Ultrasound / FAST – pericardial or pleural fluid
*Serum electrolytes – in severe trauma
*Coagulation profile – before surgery if indicated

*Sensory deficit (numbness, tingling along dermatome).

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Higher mental functions (memory, attention, judgment, insight)
*Cranial nerves

🔺LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*(to rule out organic causes & support diagnosis)
*Complete Blood Count (CBC) – to rule out infections or anemia affecting mental state
*Thyroid Function Tests (T3, T4, TSH) – to exclude thyroid disorders mimicking psychiatric illness
*Fasting Blood Glucose / HbA1c – metabolic profile
*Liver Function Tests (LFTs) – hepatic encephalopathy exclusion
*Renal Function Tests (RFTs) – chronic kidney disease-related cognitive impairment
*Serum Electrolytes – Na+, K+, Ca2+, Mg2+
*Vitamin B12 & Folate Levels – deficiency-related mood/cognitive changes
*Urine Drug Screen – substance-induced psychiatric symptoms
*Neuroimaging (MRI/CT brain) – only if focal neurological signs present
*EEG – if seizure disorder suspected

🔺AYUKTHA  INDRIYARTHA SAMYOGAM

🔺NIDANAM (Etiology)

*Astmyendriyartha Samyoga refersto the improper contact of senses (Indriyas) with their respective objects (Artha).
*Types of improper contact:
*Atiyoga – Overuse (e.g., loud noise, excessive viewing)
*Ayoga – Non-use (e.g., avoiding sound, light, etc.)
*Mithyayoga – Misuse (e.g., watching terrifying images, listening to unpleasant sounds)
*Reference:Charaka Samhita Sutrasthana 8/5
*Charaka Samhita Sharirasthana 1/102
*Ashtanga Hridaya Sutrasthana 1/20


🔺PURVAROOPAM (Prodromal symptoms)

*Purvaroopas are generally vague sensory discomforts, such as:
*Dullness or over-sensitivity in a specific sense
*Avoidance or craving for certain stimuli
*Early fatigue or irritation upon sensory use
*These vary depending on the specific Indriya affected (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin, mind).

🔺LAKSANAM 
*(Symptoms)

*Depending on the Indriya involved:
*Indriya	Symptoms
-Chakshur (Eyes)	Blurred vision, photophobia, eye strain
*Shrotra (Ears)	Tinnitus, hearing loss, *hypersensitivity
Ghrana (Nose)	Loss of smell, aversion to smell
Jivha (Tongue)	Taste disorders
Sparshana (Skin)	Numbness, tingling, hypersensitivity
Mana (Mind)	Confusion, irritability, emotional imbalance
(Charaka Samhita Sutrasthana 8/5-10


🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*To assess physical and mental effects of improper sensory interaction:
*Parameter	Findings/Observations
*Vital Signs	Normal or altered (stress-induced changes possible)
*Behavioral Status	Irritability, anxiety, hyperactivity, depression
*Sleep Pattern	Insomnia, disturbed sleep (especially from screen exposure or overstimulation)
*Speech & Expression	Abnormal pace, lack of coherence (sensory-motor issues)
*Posture & Gait	Slouched or tensed posture (digital device overuse)
*Addiction History	Excessive use of TV, mobile, music, gaming, etc.

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Evaluate specific sensory organs and nervous system:
-Nervous System
*Altered reflexes, sensory hyper/hyposensitivity
*Headache, dizziness, poor memory, or coordination
-Ophthalmic Exam
*Eye strain, dryness, watering, photophobia
*Visual acuity issues from overexposure to screens
-ENT Exam
*Tinnitus, temporary hearing loss, discomfort from loud noise
*Smell sensitivity or aversion (olfactory disturbances)
*Integumentary System
*Allergies or rashes from cosmetic overuse (touch/smell)
*Excessive tactile stimulation (burns, bruises
*Psychiatric Evaluation
*Symptoms of depression, anxiety, ADHD
*Mood swings, hallucinations, delusions in extreme cases

🔺 LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS

*Though no direct lab test confirms Asatmya Indriya Samyoga, some tests help rule out or correlate with associated disorders:
*Test	Purpose
-CBC, ESR	To rule out infection/inflammation
Thyroid Profile (T3, T4, TSH)	Rule out metabolic causes of sensory imbalance
*Blood Glucose / HbA1c	To check for diabetic neuropathy (sensory changes)
*EEG / Brain Mapping	In case of seizures, sensory processing disorders
*Eye Examination	For Computer Vision Syndrome, refractive errors
*Audiometry	Hearing threshold testing (noise damage)
*Psychological Tests	PHQ-9 (Depression), GAD-7 (Anxiety), Sensory Profile

 (Signs & Symptoms)

*Gamanakrcchrata (difficulty in walking)
*sula (pain) in thighs, knees, calves
*Sankocha (stiffness, contracture of limbs)
*Bāhya-gati-hani (loss of external movement power)
*sopha (mild swelling in some cases)

📜 Charaka Chikitsa 28/56–57; Sushruta Nidana 1/32

🔺GENERAL EXAMINATION

*General appearance:
*Weakness or inability to move affected limb(s)
*Altered posture or support needed while walking/standing
*Gait:
*Limping, dragging limb, or inability to walk (depending on severity)
*Facial expression:
*May appear anxious, distressed, or apathetic
*vital signs:
*Temperature: Usually normal (may be raised if infection present)
*Pulse: Normal or irregular (e.g., atrial fibrillation in stroke)
*Blood pressure: May be elevated (common in stroke patients)
*Respiratory rate: Usually normal unless associated respiratory muscle weakness
*Nutritional status:
*Chronic cases may show muscle wasting

🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION

*Central Nervous System (CNS):
*Muscle power: Reduced or absent in affected limb(s)
*Tone: Hypotonia (LMN lesion) or hypertonia/spasticity (UMN lesion)
*Reflexes: Diminished (LMN) or exaggerated (UMN)
*Sensation: May be normal, reduced, or absent
*Cranial nerves: Involvement possible in central lesions
*Coordination: Often impaired in CNS involvement
*Musculoskeletal system:
*Disuse atrophy in chronic cases
*Joint stiffness from immobility
*Other systems: Usually normal unless there’s systemic illness

 🔺LABORATORY & IMAGING INVESTIGATIONS

*Basic blood tests:
*CBC – rule out infection/anemia
*ESR / CRP – inflammation markers
*Blood sugar – detect diabetic neuropathy
*Serum electrolytes – detect imbalances (e.g., hypokalemia)
*Neurological diagnostics:
*MRI/CT brain & spine – detect stroke, lesions, or compression
*Nerve conduction studies – peripheral nerve involvement
*Electromyography (EMG) – muscle/nerve function
*Other relevant tests:
*Lipid profile – stroke risk assessment
*ECG/Echocardiography – cardioembolic source in stroke
