🔺SHUKRAJA MUTRA KRICHRA
🔺PART NO : 01

🎯shukraja Mutrakrichra is a type of Mutrakrichra (dysuria) caused by vitiation or obstruction involving Shukra (semen/reproductive tissue) leading to painful and difficult urination.

🔻NIDANA

🔹️Aharaja Nidana:
*Excessively spicy and hot food
*Dry food
*Alcohol intake
*Incompatible food

🔹️Viharaja Nidana:
*Excessive sexual intercourse
*Suppression of ejaculation
*Suppression of urge of urination
*Excess riding/travel
*Trauma to genital region

🔹️Dosha involvement
*Predominantly Vata
*Associated with Shukra dushti

🔸️Classical concept
Vitiated Vata causes obstruction and vitiation of Shukra, leading to painful urination.

Classical reference
From Mutrakrichra descriptions:
“शुक्रावरोधात् मूत्रकृच्छ्रं...”
(Obstruction involving Shukra causes dysuria.)

🔻POORVAROOPA
*Mild discomfort during urination
*Heaviness in bladder region
*Pain in genital region
*Difficulty during ejaculation
*Reduced urinary flow
*Lower abdominal discomfort

🔻LAKSHANA

🔹️Main symptoms
*Mutrakrichrata – painful urination
*Basti vedana – bladder pain
*Pain in penis/perineum
*Passage of semen mixed with urine
*Burning sensation
*Dribbling urination
*Difficulty in complete voiding
*Lower abdominal pain

🔹️Characteristic feature
*Shukra mixed urine
*Pain associated with ejaculation or post-ejaculation

🔹️Associated symptoms
*Weakness
*Pain in groin
*Dysuria with seminal discharge

🔺MASTULUNGA  KSHAYAM
🔺PART NO : 01


*Mastulunga Kshaya is described in Ayurvedic classics as depletion of Mastulunga (brain tissue/majja within cranial cavity), predominantly involving Vata dosha and Majja dhatu kshaya. Clinical features resemble neurodegenerative conditions, cerebral atrophy, cognitive decline, and nervous system depletion.

🔻NIDANA

*Excessive fasting (Langhana atiyoga)
*Chronic illness
*Trauma to head
*Excessive stress, fear, grief
*Sleep deprivation
*Excessive sexual activity
*Vata aggravating diet and lifestyle
*Dhatu kshaya
*Old age
Classical Reference
Ashtanga Hridaya – Nidana of Vata vyadhi and Majjakshaya are applied.
Sloka

🔺MUTRAJATHARA

Mutrajathara is one among the types of Mutraghata described in Ayurveda. It is characterized by distension of abdomen due to retention of urine caused by obstruction to urinary flow.

Described mainly in:
*Ashtanga Hridaya – Nidana Sthana, Chapter 9 (Mutraghata Nidana)
*Sushruta Samhita – Uttara Tantra
*Charaka Samhita – Siddhi Sthana references to Mutraghata

🔻NIDANA

🔹️Aharaja Nidana:
*Excessively dry food
*Suppression of urge for micturition
*Inadequate water intake
*Excessive salty/pungent foods

🔹️Viharaja Nidana:
*Excessive riding/travel
*Trauma to pelvic region
*Excessive exercise
*Long sitting

🔹️Dosha involvement
*Predominantly Vata prakopa
*Apana Vayu dushti

Classical concept:
Obstruction to urinary passage causes accumulation of urine leading to abdominal enlargement.

Sloka Reference
From Ashtanga Hridaya – Nidana Sthana Chapter 9:
“मूत्रस्यावरोधात् उदरवृद्धिः...”
(Meaning: abdominal distension occurs due to obstruction of urine)

🔻POORVAROOPA 

*Difficulty in urination
*Reduced urine flow
*Heaviness in lower abdomen
*Mild abdominal distension
*Pain in bladder region
*Flatulence
*Discomfort in suprapubic area

🔻LAKSHANA

🔸️Main symptoms
*Mutravega dharana (retention of urine)
*Adhmana (abdominal distension)
*Basti shoola (bladder pain)
*Pain in lower abdomen
*Difficulty or absence of urination
*Tender suprapubic swelling
*Restlessness
*Constipation may be associated
🔸️Advanced symptoms
*Severe abdominal distension
*Dribbling of urine
*Burning micturition
*Features of urinary obstruction


🔺SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION 

*General condition of the patient
*Built and nourishment
Pallor, icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, edema, lymphadenopathy
*Vital signs – pulse, BP, temperature, respiratory rate
Hydration status
*Examination of abdomen
*Suprapubic fullness/distension
*Tenderness over bladder region
Palpation for enlarged bladder
*Percussion for dullness in suprapubic area
*Examination of external genitalia
*Per rectal examination (if indicated for prostate enlargement)
*Nervous system examination for neurogenic bladder causes
*Renal angle tenderness examination
*Assessment of urine output and urinary stream

🔺DIAGNOSTIC EXAMINATION 

*Complete blood count (CBC)
*Urine routine examination
*Urine culture and sensitivity
*Blood urea and serum creatinine
*Blood sugar examination
*Ultrasound abdomen and pelvis
*Post void residual urine assessment
*X-ray KUB region
*CT scan/MRI if required
*Uroflowmetry
*Cystoscopy if obstruction suspected
*PSA estimation in elderly males
*Renal function test
Electrolyte examination
*Ayurvedic assessment of dosha, dushya, srotas, and samprapti

🔺GARBHAJA PHAKKA(गर्भज फक्क)

🎯Phakka Roga is described in Kashyapa Samhita under Kaumarabhritya.
Garbhaja Phakka develops due to defects or disorders occurring during intrauterine life leading to delayed development, weakness, and inability to walk.

🔸️Definition of Phakka
“बालः संवत्सरः पन्नः पदाभ्यां यो न गच्छति ।
स फक्क इति विज्ञेयः ॥”
Meaning:
A child who does not walk even after the normal age of walking is called Phakka.
Reference-Kashyapa Samhita

🔸️Garbhaja Phakka – Classical Reference
“गर्भोपघातजैर्दोषैः क्षीणगर्भस्य जायते ।
दुर्बलत्वं शरीरस्य फक्कत्वं च प्रजायते ॥”
Meaning:
Due to factors affecting the fetus during pregnancy, the child becomes weak and develops Phakka.

🔻NIDANA

🔹️Maternal Causes
*Garbhini apachara
*Poor maternal nutrition
*Chronic maternal illness
*Trauma during pregnancy
*Excess fasting
*Mental stress
*Alcohol/toxin exposure
*Recurrent infections
🔹️Fetal Causes
*Congenital defects
*Improper fetal nourishment
*Beeja dosha
*Garbha upaghata
🔹️Dosha
*Vata predominant
*Associated dhatu kshaya

🔻POORVAROOPA

🔻LAKSHANA

🔺AJAGALLIKA (अजगल्लिका)

Ajagallika is described under Ksudra Roga in Ayurvedic classics. It is generally correlated with conditions like small glandular eruptions/boils resembling enlarged lymph nodes or molluscum-like lesions, often occurring in children.

Classical Reference
▫️AH
“अजगल्लिका कफवातजा…” — described in Ksudra Roga Adhyāya.


 – Ksudraroga Nidana Adhyaya
“अजगल्लिका नाम कफवातसमुद्भवा
मुद्गमात्रा घना श्वेता अल्परुजा…”
Meaning
Caused by Kapha and Vāta
*Small swelling resembling *mudga (green gram)
*Firm (ghana)
*Whitish
*Mildly painful

🔻NIDANA

🔹️Main dosic involvement:
*Kapha + Vata predominance
*Rakta and Mamsa dusti
🔸️Causes
*Guru, snigdha, abhishyandi ahara
*Excess intake of curd, fish, 
*Newly harvested grains
*Poor hygiene
*Krimi involvement
*Bala avastha(commonly in children)

▫️Vāta causes:
*Mild pain

🔺DHATU KSHAYA
(धातुक्षय)


🎯Dhatu Kshaya refers to depletion or inadequacy of body tissues (Rasa, Rakta, Mamsa, Meda, Asthi, Majja, Sukra). It is described in many contexts in Ayurvedic classics, especially in relation to Vata aggravation.

“धातूनां क्षयो धातुक्षयः” — Depletion of body tissues is called Dhatu Kshaya.

🔺KANDU- KOTHA

Kandu and Kotha are explained under Kshudra Kushta / Twak Vikara in Ayurveda.
▫️Kandu = severe itching disorder

🔸️Definition

▫️Madhava Nidana

🔺MALA SANGA

Mala Sanga refers to difficulty or obstruction in the normal expulsion of feces due to derangement of mainly Apana Vata. It is described in the context of Vibandha, Purisha Vega Dharana, and Udavarta in Ayurvedic classics.

🔹️Classical References

▫️Ashtanga Hridaya
Sutrasthana – Vega Dharaneeya Adhyaya
“वर्चोनिग्रहणात् पिण्डिकोद्वेष्टनादयः...”
Suppression of defecation urge causes abdominal disorders and constipation.
▫️Charaka Samhita
Siddhisthana – Basti Siddhi
Discusses Vibandha due to Vata aggravation.
▫️Sushruta Samhita
Nidanasthana – Udavarta Nidana
Explains bowel obstruction due to Vega Dharana and Vata prakopa.

🔻NIDANA

🔸️Manasika Nidana

*Anxiety
*Depression
🔸️Other Causes

🔺APARASANGA 

Aparasanga refers to retention or delayed expulsion of the placenta after delivery. In modern correlation, it is comparable to retained placenta / retained products of conception.
 
🔸️Classical References

▫️Sushruta Samhita
*Sharira Sthana and Chikitsa references regarding retained placenta and obstetric manipulations.
▫️Ashtanga Hridaya
*Sharira Sthana and Uttara Tantra references regarding management after delivery and Apara-related complications.
▫️Charaka Samhita
*Sutika care and Vata predominance after delivery.

Ayurvedic texts mention:
“Apara not expelled after delivery” requiring measures like stimulation, dhoopana, pressure techniques, and manual removal if needed.

🔻NIDANA

🔸️Ayurvedic causes:
*Vitiated Vata causing obstruction to expulsion
*Daurbalya of garbhashaya
*Atisrama during labour
*Apana vata dushti
*Improper prasava karma

🔸️Modern Causes

*Uterine atony
*Placenta adherens
*Placenta accreta spectrum
*Constriction ring
*Cervical closure before expulsion
*Prolonged labour
*Preterm delivery
*Premature pulling of umbilical cord 
*Prolonged labour 
*Improper uterine contractions 

🔻POORVAROOPA 

Classical texts do not describe elaborate poorvaroopa separately, but clinically:
*Delayed placental separation
*Feeling of incomplete evacuation
*Lower abdominal discomfort
*Inadequate uterine contractions
*Persistent bleeding

🔻LAKSHANA 

*Placenta not expelled after delivery
*Lower abdominal pain
*Excessive or persistent bleeding
*Feeling of heaviness in pelvis
*Fatigue
*Fever (if infected)
*Foul smelling discharge
*Uterine tenderness
▫️Severe Complications
*Postpartum hemorrhage
*Shock
*Sepsis

🔻CLINICAL EXAMINATION 

🔹️Ayurvedic Examination
▫️Dashavidha Pareeksha
▫️Obstetric Examination
*Yonipariksha
*Assessment of bleeding
*Uterine size and tenderness
*Retained tissue signs
🔹️Modern Examination
▫️General Examination
*Pulse
*BP
*Pallor
*Shock features
*Fever
▫️Obstetric Examination
*Uterine tone
*Height of fundus
*Vaginal bleeding
*Placental completeness

🔻DIAGNOSTIC TECHNIQUES 

*Ultrasonography (USG pelvis)
*CBC
*Hemoglobin
*CRP
*Culture if infection suspected
*Doppler studies if needed
▫️USG Findings
*Retained products
*Thickened endometrium
*Echognic material inside uterus

🔺PRATILOMA RAJAYAKSHMA
(प्रतिलोम राजयक्ष्म)

Rajayakshma is one among the Ashta Mahagada described in Ayurveda. “Pratiloma Rajayakshma” denotes a type where the manifestation of symptoms occurs in reverse order or with predominant upward/opposite movement of vitiated doshas causing progressive dhatu kshaya and systemic depletion. It is broadly correlated with chronic wasting disorders including pulmonary tuberculosis with atypical progression
.
🔸️Classical descriptions of Rajayakshma are available in:

*Charaka Samhita- Nidana sthana( Chapter 6), Chikitsa sthana( Chapter 8)
*Sushruta Samhita- Uttara tantra
*Ashtanga Hridaya- Nidana sthana
Modern reviews discuss Rajayakshma as a tridoshaja dhatukshayaja disorder correlated with tuberculosis and chronic wasting disease.

🔻NIDANA

▫️Classical causes
Described mainly in Charaka Samhita:
*Sahasa – excessive physical exertion
*Vega Sandharana – suppression of natural urges
*Kshaya – depletion of dhatus
*Vishamashana – irregular/incompatible food habits
▫️Additional Nidanas
*Ati maithuna
*Ruksha alpahara
*Chronic respiratory illness
*Mental stress and grief
*Exposure to dust/smoke
*Immunodeficiency and malnutrition

🔻POORVAROOPA 

Premonitory features include:
*Arochaka
*Avipaka
*Mild kasa
*Shrama
*Daurbalya
*Angamarda
*Arati
*Mild jwara
*Loss of enthusiasm
*Progressive weight loss

🔻LAKSHANA 
Classically Ekadasha Rupa are described:
*Kasa 
*Jwara 
*Shwasa 
*Parshva shoola
*Swarabhanga
*Atisara
*Aruchi
*Chardi
*Raktashtheevana 
*Daurbalya
*Karshya
▫️Features more suggestive of Pratiloma type
*Upward movement of dosha
*Severe kasa and shwasa first
*Progressive oja kshaya
*Marked emaciation
*Recurrent fever
*Hoarseness and chest pain

🔻CLINICAL EXAMINATION 

🔹️According to Ayurvedic 
▫️Dashavidha Pariksha
▫️Ashtavidha Pariksha
▫️Important findings
*Karshya
*Panduta
*Daurbalya
*Kaphayukta kasa
*Ushna sparsha
*Hrishva shwasa
🔹️According to Modern 
▫️General Examination
*Pallor
*Weight loss
*Fever
*Lymphadenopathy
*Clubbing
▫️Respiratory Examination

*Bronchial breath sounds

🔺ANTRA VRIDDHI

In Ayurveda, Antra Vriddhi is described under Vriddhi Roga and is commonly correlated clinically with inguinal/scrotal hernia, especially when intestinal loops descend into the scrotal region.

🔸️Classical references 
▫️Sushruta Samhita – Nidana Sthana, Vriddhi Nidana
▫️Ashtanga Hridaya – Nidana Sthana
▫️Madhava Nidana – Vriddhi Nidana

🔸️Definition

Due to aggravation of Vata, intestine (Antra) descends into the inguinal/scrotal region producing swelling and pain; this condition is called Antra Vriddhi.

🔻NIDANA
 
From Sushruta Samhita Nidana Sthana:
*Ati vyayama 
*Guru bharavahana 
*Ati gamana 
*Vegadharana
*Vata prakopa nidanas
*Abhighata 
*Sudden strain

From Sushruta Samhita Nidana Sthana – Vriddhi Nidana Adhyaya:
“Vata prakopaka hetus cause descent of antra into vrishana producing vriddhi.”

🔻POORVAROOPA 

*Mild groin discomfort
*Pulling pain in inguinal region
*Heaviness in scrotum
*Occasional swelling on straining
*Flatulence
*Lower abdominal discomfort

🔻LAKSHANA 

▫️Classical Features
*Vriddhi (swelling) in groin/scrotum
*Vata purna driti sparsha (air-filled feel)
*Shoola

*Relief on lying down
*Anaha
*Intestinal gurgling sound
▫️Advanced Features
*Irreducibility
*Severe pain
*Obstruction features
*Vomiting


🔻CLINICAL EXAMINATION

*Pain
*Straining history
*Constipation

🔺MEDOJA VRIDDHI (मेदोजवृद्धि)

*Medoja Vriddhi is one among the seven types of Vriddhi Roga described in Ayurveda. It occurs due to vitiation of Meda Dhatu with Kapha predominance, producing soft, unctuous, painless enlargement of the scrotal region. It is commonly correlated with conditions like lipomatous scrotal swelling, fatty enlargement, or certain chronic benign scrotal enlargements.

🔸️Classical References:
▫️Sushruta Samhita
*Nidana Sthana, Chapter 13 – Vriddhi Nidana
▫️Ashtanga Hridaya
*Nidana Sthana, Chapter 12 – Vriddhi Nidana
▫️Madhava Nidana

🔹️Definition
When vitiated Medas accumulates in the scrotal region producing soft, heavy, unctuous swelling, it is called Medoja Vriddhi.

🔺VISHPOTA KUSHTA

Kushta is described in Ayurvedic classics as a group of skin disorders caused by vitiation of Tridosha along with Dushya involvement such as Tvak, Rakta, Mamsa and Lasika.

🔺ROHINI(रोहिणी)

Rohini is a severe Kanthagata Roga (disease of the throat) described primarily in Susruta Samhita Nidana Sthana 16 (Mukharoga Nidana). It is characterized by rapidly developing fleshy growths (mamsankura) in the throat causing obstruction to swallowing and respiration.
🔸️Classical References
Susruta Samhita, Nidana Sthana 16 (Mukharoga Nidana)

🔻NIDANA

*Guru ahara 
*Abhishyandi ahara
*Dadhi 
*Navanna
*Excess sweets
*Fish and meat in excess
*Exposure to cold environment

*Improper oral hygiene
*Kapha- and Rakta-vitiating diet

*Kapha (predominant)
*Rakta
*Pitta
*Vata (advanced stage)

🔻POORVAROOPA 

*Kantha guruta
*Mild sore throat
*Difficulty swallowing

*Loss of appetite
*Feverish feeling
*Hoarseness of voice

🔹️Types of Rohini

🔺JWARATISARA
(ज्वरातिसार)
 
Jwaratisara is Atisara  associated with Jvara . It is described in Ayurvedic classics, particularly in the Atisara Chikitsa chapters of the Brihattrayi.

🔸️ Definition
When fever is associated with diarrhea or when improperly managed fever leads to diarrhea due to aggravated doshas

 affecting the grahani and pakvashaya, the condition is termed Jvaratisara.

🔻NIDANA

▫️Charaka Samhita
▫️Ashtanga Hridaya
🔹️Causes

🔸️Jvara-related factors
*Langhana beyond capacity during fever
*Improper diet during fever
*Untimely administration of heavy food
*Suppression of natural urges
*Agnimandya during fever

🔸️General Atisara factors
▫️Excessive intake of:
*Guru ahara
*Ati-snigdha ahara
*Viruddhahara
*Dushta jala
▫️Psychological causes:
*Bhaya
*Shoka

Charaka Chikitsa Sthana 19
ज्वरितस्याप्यपक्वेषु दोषेष्वतिसरो भवेत्
Meaning: Improper management of fever while doshas remain unripe leads to Atisara.

🔹️Ashtanga Hridaya

🔸️Definition

*Chronic Karnasrava (ear discharge)

*Trauma to ear canal
*Excessive scratching of ear
*Entry of contaminated water into ear
*Dust and smoke exposure
*Neglected Karnarogas

🔹️Dosha Involvement
*Kapha Prakopa
*Rakta Dushti
*Mamsa Vriddhi

🔺️POORVAROOPA

🔺OJO KSHAYA (Loss/Depletion of Ojas)

🔸️DEFINITION 

Ojas is the essence of all the seven dhatus and is responsible for bala (strength), immunity, vitality, and life itself.

🔹️Classical Reference

Ojas is considered the supreme essence of all dhatus.

🔺️NIDANA

Akshipakatyaya is a severe ocular disorder described under Sarvagata Netra Rogas. It is considered an advanced stage of Akshipaka where inflammation becomes intense, involving deeper ocular structures.

🔺️DEFINITION

🔺️NIDANA

🔺NIMESHA(निमेष) 

Nimesha is an eyelid disorder described under Vartmagata Roga (diseases of the eyelids).

🔸️Classical Reference
▫️Susruta Samhita, Uttara Tantra, Netraroga Vijnaniya Adhyaya (Vartmagata Rogas)

🔹️Definition
 
Nimesha is a condition characterized by frequent involuntary blinking or repeated closure of eyelids due to vitiation of Vata dosha affecting the eyelids.

"मुहुर्निमेषणं यत्र वाताद् भवति पिडितम् ।
तन्निमेषं विजानीयाद् वर्त्मरोगं भिषग्वरः ॥"
Reference: Susruta Samhita, Uttara Tantra, Vartmagata Roga.

🔺️NIDANA

Predominantly Vata-provoking factors:
*Excessive visual strain
*Night vigil (Ratri jagarana)
*Excessive crying
*Dust and smoke exposure
*Mental stress
*Excessive reading
*Exposure to wind
*Eye fatigue

🔺️POORVAROOPA
 
Not clearly described separately in classics. Possible premonitory features:
*Mild twitching of eyelids
*Dryness of eyes
*Eye fatigue
*Mild discomfort during blinking
*Foreign body sensation

🔺️LAKSHANA
 
*Frequent blinking
*Repeated involuntary closure of eyelids
*Difficulty keeping eyes open
*Vata-predominant discomfort
*Eye strain
*Mild pain or fatigue around eyelids

🔺️CLINICAL EXAMINATION 

🔸️According to Ayurveda

🔺GUHYA ROGA (Genital Disorders) 

🔸️DEFINITION

Guhya Roga refers to the group of diseases affecting the Guhya Pradesha (external genital organs and perineal region) caused by the vitiation of Doshas (Vata, Pitta, Kapha) and Rakta, producing symptoms such as swelling, pain, itching, burning sensation, ulcers, eruptions, and discharge.

🔸️Classical Reference

🔺GARBHA SHOSHA

🔸️DEFINITION 

 Garbha Shosha is a condition in which the fetus becomes undernourished and shows retarded intrauterine growth due to inadequate nourishment reaching the fetus. It is mainly caused by aggravated Vata leading to depletion of fetal nutrition and Ojas. It is commonly correlated with Intrauterine Growth Restriction (IUGR) 

🔸️Classical References
▫️Kashyapa Samhita – Khila Sthana – Garbha Shosha Adhyaya
▫️Charaka Samhita – discussion of Upavishtaka and Nagodara.
▫️Sushruta Samhita – fetal development and fetal disorders

🔺️NIDANA

🔹️Maternal Factors
*Alpa ashana 
*Ruksha, Laghu, Vata-prakopaka Ahara
*Upavasa 
*Excessive physical exertion
*Mental stress, anxiety, grief
*Chronic maternal diseases
*Placental insufficiency
🔸️Doshic Factors
*Predominant Vata prakopa
*Rasa Dhatu Kshaya
*Ambu Kshaya
*Ojo Kshaya

🔺️POORVAROOPA 

Classical texts do not describe specific Purvarupas separately. Features suggesting impending Garbha Shosha include:
*Reduced maternal weight gain
*Decreased uterine growth
*Reduced perception of fetal growth
*Maternal weakness
*Daurbalya
*Kshut-hani

🔺️LAKSHANA 

🔸️Maternal
*Kukshi vriddhi hani (less abdominal enlargement)
*Daurbalya
*Karshya
*Vata-pradhana symptoms

🔸️Fetal

*Alpavriddhi of Garbha
*Delayed fetal growth
*Reduced fetal nourishment
*Oja hani
*Low fetal weight

🔸️Modern Features
*Fundal height less than gestational age
*Estimated fetal weight below 10th percentile
*Reduced amniotic fluid
*Decreased fetal movements

🔺️DIAGNOSTIC TECHNIQUES 

🔸️Clinical

*Umbilical artery Doppler

🔺MUKHA ARBUDA(Oral Tumor)

🔸️DEFINITION 

A large, deep-seated, firm, slowly growing, usually painless swelling arising from vitiated Doshas affecting Mamsa and Rakta is called Arbuda.
Mukha Arbuda = Arbuda occurring in oral structures such as lips, tongue, palate, gums, buccal mucosa, floor of mouth, etc.

🔺️NIDANA 

▫️Excessive intake of:
*Guru Ahara
*Abhishyandi Ahara
*Ati Snigdha Ahara
*Viruddha Ahara
▫️Dosha aggravating factors:
*Kapha prakopaka nidana
*Rakta dushti nidana
*Mamsa dushti nidana
▫️Specific Mukha Arbuda Nidana
*Repeated trauma to oral mucosa
*Tobacco chewing
*Smoking
*Alcohol abuse
*Poor oral hygiene
*Chronic ulceration
*Sharp tooth irritation
*Excessively hot and spicy foods

🔺️POORVAROOPA 

Classical texts do not mention specific Purvarupa of Mukha Arbuda.
Possible manifestations:
*Mild swelling
*Local heaviness
*Mucosal thickening
*Discomfort during chewing
*Change in oral sensation
*Non-healing ulcer

🔺️LAKSHANA 

▫️General Arbuda Lakshana
According to Sushruta:
*Mahat (large swelling)
*Sthira 
*Mamsopachaya (muscular overgrowth)
*Gambhira (deep rooted)
*Alpavedana (slightly painful or painless)
*Chiravriddhi (slow growth)
▫️Mukha Arbuda Lakshana
*Oral mass/swelling
*Ulceration
*Bleeding
*Foul smell
*Difficulty in chewing
*Dysphagia
*Speech difficulty
*Pain (later stages)
*Excess salivation
*Weight loss (advanced stage)
